info.name: DIDWW API3 2026-11-19 (Latest)
info.description:
This collection covers DIDWW API 3 version **2026-11-19**. Every request, its parameters and its examples follow the [API 3 documentation for 2026-11-19](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/index.html); some requests also show further validation errors the API returns.

# Using this collection

1. Fork the collection together with the **DIDWW Sandbox** or **DIDWW Production** environment and select the environment.
2. Put your API key into the `apiKey` variable of the environment as its *current value*, as plain text. Do not put it in the initial value: initial values are shared with everyone who can see the environment. Keep forked environments private.
3. Send any request. The collection mints an access token with your API key (`POST https://{{authHost}}/token`) before the first request and reuses it until shortly before it expires. **Authentication › Mint access token** mints one on demand and shows the exchange. When minting fails, the request reports the reason as a script error.

| Variable | Where | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `host` | environment | API host, for example `sandbox-api.didww.com`. |
| `vinHost`, `voutHost`, `smsHost` | environment | Hosts of the inbound call, outbound call and SMS price services. |
| `authHost` | environment | Host of the token service, for example `auth-sandbox.didww.com`. |
| `apiKey` | environment | Your API key. The collection sends it only to the token service; the export file download also accepts it (see **Get CSV File of Export**). |
| `apiVersion` | collection | The API version the token selects: `2026-11-19`. |
| `tokenScope` | collection | `full` (the default) or `read`. |
| `accessToken`, `accessTokenExpiresAt`, `accessTokenFingerprint`, `accessTokenError` | collection | Set by the collection; do not edit or persist them. |

# API resources

The DIDWW API allows you to perform an extensive set of actions such as querying the DID coverage and inventory, ordering and configuring phone numbers and services, setting capacity, creating SIP and SMS trunks, and looking up prices by using the following methods:

> - **GET** - Fetch data, where the data can be a collection or resources or an individual resource
> - **HEAD** - Fetch only the headers of a price file
> - **POST** - Create a new resource
> - **PATCH** - Update an existing resource
> - **DELETE** - Remove an existing resource

| API Call | Method/s | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [balance](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/balance/index.html#balance-v35) | GET | Returns the prepaid balance as well as the available credit on the account. |
| [cities](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/city/index.html#cities-v35) | GET | Returns a list of cities included in the current DIDWW inventory, or returns the details of a specific city. |
| [countries](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/countries/index.html#countries-v35) | GET | Returns a list of countries included in the current DIDWW inventory, or return the details of a specific country. |
| [dids](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html#dids-v35) | GET, PATCH | Returns a list of all of the DIDs owned by an account or the details for a single DID, or modify the settings for a single DID owned by an account. |
| [did\_history](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did-history/index.html#did-history-v35) | GET | Returns a list of DID history records or a single DID history record. |
| [did\_groups](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/did-group/index.html#did-groups-v35) | GET | Returns a list of DID Groups, which is essentially a list of the current DIDWW coverage. DID Groups are phone numbers that share a common city or area code. |
| [capacity\_pools](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/capacity-pool/index.html#capacity-pools-v35) | GET, PATCH | Returns a list of the Capacity Pools which include information about channels quantity, supported Countries, Shared Capacity Groups. |
| [shared\_capacity\_groups](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/shared-capacity-group/index.html#shared-capacity-groups-v35) | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE | Returns a list of the Capacity Groups assigned to Capacity Pool. |
| [export](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/index.html#export-v35) | GET, POST, PATCH | Returns exports of call and message records, creates a new export, or updates an existing export. |
| [orders](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/order/index.html#orders-v35) | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE | Returns a list of the orders previously placed in this account, creates a new order, updates an existing order, or deletes an order. |
| [regions](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/regions/index.html#regions-v35) | GET | Returns a list of regions (for example, states within the USA) included in the current DIDWW inventory. |
| [voice\_in\_trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-in-trunks/index.html#voice-in-trunks-v35) | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE | Returns a list of all of the inbound trunks configured by this account, create a new trunk, modify the settings of an existing trunk, or delete a trunk. |
| [voice\_out\_trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/index.html#voice-out-trunks-v35) | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE | Returns a list of all outbound trunks configured by this account, create a new trunk, modify the existing trunk, or delete a trunk. |
| [voice\_out\_trunk\_regenerate\_credentials](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/voice-out-trunk-regenerate-credentials.html#voice-out-regenerate-credentials-v35) | POST | Regenerates the username and password of an outbound trunk that uses the `credentials_and_ip` authentication method. |
| [emergency\_calling\_services](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-calling-services/index.html#emergency-calling-services-v35) | GET, DELETE | Returns a list of Emergency Calling Services configured by the account, returns the details of a single service, or cancels an existing service. |
| [voice\_in\_trunk\_groups](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-in-trunk-groups/index.html#voice-in-trunk-groups-v35) | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE | Returns the details of an inbound trunk group, create a new trunk group, modify trunk group settings, or delete a trunk group. |
| [sms\_trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/index.html#sms-trunks-v35) | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE | Returns a list of all SMS trunks configured by this account, creates a new SMS trunk, modifies an existing SMS trunk, or deletes an SMS trunk. |
| [sms\_trunk\_regenerate\_credentials](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/sms-trunk-regenerate-credentials.html#sms-trunk-regenerate-credentials-v35) | POST | Regenerates the credentials of an SMPP ESME or HTTP OUT SMS trunk. |
| [sms\_trunk\_groups](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunk-groups/index.html#sms-trunk-groups-v35) | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE | Returns a list of SMS trunk groups, creates a new SMS trunk group, modifies an existing group or replaces its member trunks, or deletes a group. |
| [sender\_id\_verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sender-id-verifications/index.html#sender-id-verifications-v35) | GET, PATCH | Returns a list of Sender ID verifications or the details of a single one, or updates a verification. |
| [available\_dids](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/available-did/index.html#available-dids-v35) | GET | Returns a list of available DID numbers in the current DIDWW coverage. |
| [did\_reservation](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/did-reservation/index.html#did-reservation-v35) | GET, POST, DELETE | Returns a list or a single DID reservations for the account. |
| [address\_verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/index.html#address-verifications-v35) | GET, POST, PATCH | Returns a list of address verifications, the details of a single address verification, creates a new address verification, or updates an existing address verification. |
| [addresses](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/addresses/index.html#addresses-v35) | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE | Returns the details of a address, create a new address, modify address settings, or delete an address. |
| [encrypted\_files](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/index.html#encrypted-files-v35) | GET, POST, DELETE | Returns the details of a encrypted file, create a new encrypted file, or delete an encrypted file. |
| [public\_keys](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/public-keys.html#public-keys-v35) | GET | Returns a list of RSA public keys used to encrypt files. |
| [identities](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/index.html#identities-v35) | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE | Returns the details of a identity, create a new identity, modify identity settings, or delete an identity. |
| [permanent\_supporting\_documents](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/permanent-documents/index.html#permanent-documents-v35) | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE | Returns a list of permanent supporting documents or the details of a single permanent supporting document, creates a new permanent supporting document, updates an existing permanent supporting document, or deletes a permanent supporting document. |
| [proof\_types](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/proof-types/index.html#proof-types-v35) | GET | Returns a list or a single proof\_types for the account. |
| [proofs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/proofs/index.html#proofs-v35) | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE | Returns a list of proofs or the details of a single proof, creates a new proof, updates an existing proof, or deletes a proof. |
| [address\_requirements](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/index.html#address-requirements-v35) | GET | Returns a list or a single address requirement for the account. |
| [address\_requirement\_validations](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/address-requirement-validations.html#address-requirement-validations-v35) | POST | Checks whether an address and / or identity is valid against an address requirement. |
| [emergency\_requirements](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-requirements/index.html#emergency-requirements-v35) | GET | Returns a list of emergency requirements for the account. |
| [emergency\_requirement\_validations](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-requirements/emergency-requirement-validations.html#emergency-requirement-validations-v35) | POST | Checks whether an address and / or identity is valid against an emergency requirement. |
| [emergency\_verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-verifications/index.html#emergency-verifications-v35) | GET, POST, PATCH | Returns a list of Emergency Verifications, the details of a single Emergency Verification, creates a new Emergency Verification task, or updates an existing Emergency Verification. |
| [supporting\_document\_templates](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/supporting-document-templates/index.html#supporting-document-template-v35) | GET | Returns a list or a single supporting document templates for the account. |
| [areas](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/areas/index.html#areas-v35) | GET | Returns a list or a single regulatory area. |
| [nanpa\_prefixes](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/nanpa/index.html#nanpa-prefixes-v35) | GET | Returns a list NANPA prefixes or a single NANPA prefix. |
| [token](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/authentication.html#authentication-v35) | POST | Mints an access token on the token service (`auth.didww.com`) in exchange for an API key. |
| [inbound call prices](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/inbound-call-prices/index.html#inbound-call-prices-v35) | GET, HEAD | Looks up the inbound call prices of a number, or downloads the inbound call price file (`api-vin.didww.com`). |
| [outbound call prices](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/outbound-call-prices/index.html#outbound-call-prices-v35) | GET, HEAD | Looks up the outbound call prices of a number, or downloads the outbound call price file (`api-vout.didww.com`). |
| [SMS prices](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/sms-prices/index.html#sms-prices-v35) | GET, HEAD | Looks up SMS IN and SMS OUT prices of a number or a country, or downloads the SMS price files (`api-sms.didww.com`). |

item.name: Changelog
item.description: This changelog lists API changes introduced in version `2026-11-19`. ## New Endpoints ### The token service (`auth.didww.com`) now supports `POST /token`. `POST /token` on the DIDWW token service exchanges an API key for a short-lived bearer access token. **What changed** - Added `POST https://auth.didww.com/token` (Production) and `POST https://auth-sandbox.didww.com/token` (Sandbox). - The request is authenticated with an API key of the same environment in the `Api-Key` header and takes an `application/json` body. - Body parameters: `aud` (required; one service host or a list: `api.didww.com`, `api-vin.didww.com`, `api-vout.didww.com`, `api-sms.didww.com`), `scope` (`full` by default, or `read`), `api_version` (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and `expires_in` (seconds, default `900`, clamped into `60`-`3600`). - The `200 OK` response returns `access_token`, `token_type` (`Bearer`), `expires_in`, `aud`, `scope` and `api_version` with `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Pragma: no-cache`. - Errors use the OAuth shape `error` / `error_description`: `400` (`invalid_request`, `invalid_scope`), `401` (`invalid_client`) and `429` (`rate_limit_exceeded`, with `Retry-After`). **Behavior notes** - A token is accepted only in the environment that minted it and only by the services listed in its `aud`. Sandbox services use the production host names as audiences. - A `read:` value that is not known is granted as its closest known ancestor; compare `scope` in the response with the one requested. - Tokens cannot be refreshed. Mint a new token before `expires_in` runs out. **Affected resources** - [Authentication for API v2026-11-19](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/authentication.html) - [Scopes](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/authentication.html#authentication-scopes-v35) - [Audiences](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/authentication.html#authentication-audiences-v35) ### Read, write, update, and delete endpoints have been added for `/v3/sms_trunks`. `/v3/sms_trunks` read, create, update, and delete endpoints are available. **What changed** - Added `GET` `/v3/sms_trunks`. - Added `GET` `/v3/sms_trunks/{id}`. - Added `POST` `/v3/sms_trunks`. - Added `PATCH` `/v3/sms_trunks/{id}`. - Added `DELETE` `/v3/sms_trunks/{id}`. - SMS trunk responses include `name`, `external_reference_id`, `blocked`, `priority`, `allow_any_did_as_source`, `allow_in`, `allow_out`, `configuration`, `created_at`, and `updated_at`. - `configuration.type` is one of `sms_to_email`, `http_in`, `http_out`, `smpp_esme`, and `smpp_smsc`. - Supported relationships are `outgoing_dids`, `incoming_dids`, `sms_trunk_group`, and `sender_id_verifications`. - Collection filters include `id`, `name`, `external_reference_id`, and `configuration.type`. - Collection sorting includes `name`, `external_reference_id`, `blocked`, `priority`, `allow_in`, `allow_out`, `created_at`, and `updated_at`. - Pagination defaults to `50` records per page, with a maximum of `100`. **Behavior notes** - The configuration type cannot be changed after creation. On `PATCH`, `configuration.type` must match, and only the configuration attributes sent are written. - `smpp_esme` trunks return a generated `system_id` and `password`. `http_out` trunks return a generated `auth_name` and `auth_password`. - `http_out` trunks return `meta.host`, the full URL of the endpoint to which outbound messages are submitted. - `priority` and `sms_trunk_group` apply to `sms_to_email`, `http_in`, `smpp_esme`, and `smpp_smsc` trunks. On `http_out` trunks `priority` stays `null`. - Enabling `allow_any_did_as_source` removes all `outgoing_dids`. - `incoming_dids` is read-only. DIDs are routed to a trunk through the DID `sms_trunk` relationship. - `DELETE` returns `422` while any DID is routed to the trunk. - SMS trunks and SMS trunk groups share one account limit. When it is reached, `POST` returns `400` with the title `Quota limit reached`. **Affected resources** - [Get SMS Trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/get-sms-trunks.html) - [Get SMS Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/get-sms-trunk.html) - [Create SMS Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/create-sms-trunk.html) - [Update SMS Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/update-sms-trunk.html) - [Delete SMS Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/delete-sms-trunk.html) - [SMS Trunk Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/sms-trunk-object.html#sms-trunk-object-v35) ### Read, write, update, and delete endpoints have been added for `/v3/sms_trunk_groups`. `/v3/sms_trunk_groups` read, create, update, and delete endpoints are available. **What changed** - Added `GET` `/v3/sms_trunk_groups`. - Added `GET` `/v3/sms_trunk_groups/{id}`. - Added `POST` `/v3/sms_trunk_groups`. - Added `PATCH` `/v3/sms_trunk_groups/{id}`. - Added `DELETE` `/v3/sms_trunk_groups/{id}`. - SMS trunk group responses include `name`, `external_reference_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `meta.sms_trunks_count`. - Supported relationships are `sms_trunks` and `incoming_dids`. - Collection filters include `id`, `name`, and `external_reference_id`. - Collection sorting includes `name`, `external_reference_id`, `created_at`, and `updated_at`. **Behavior notes** - Sending `sms_trunks` replaces the whole membership of the group. - Only `sms_to_email`, `http_in`, `smpp_esme`, and `smpp_smsc` trunks can be members. - `DELETE` also deletes every trunk in the group, and returns `422` while any DID is routed to the group or to one of its trunks. - `incoming_dids` is read-only. DIDs are routed to a group through the DID `sms_trunk_group` relationship. **Affected resources** - [Get SMS Trunk Groups](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunk-groups/get-sms-trunk-groups.html) - [Get SMS Trunk Group](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunk-groups/get-sms-trunk-group.html) - [Create SMS Trunk Group](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunk-groups/create-sms-trunk-group.html) - [Update SMS Trunk Group](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunk-groups/update-sms-trunk-group.html) - [Delete SMS Trunk Group](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunk-groups/delete-sms-trunk-group.html) - [SMS Trunk Group Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunk-groups/sms-trunk-group-object.html#sms-trunk-group-object-v35) ### A write endpoint has been added at `/v3/sms_trunk_regenerate_credentials`. `/v3/sms_trunk_regenerate_credentials` write endpoint is available. **What changed** - Added `POST` `/v3/sms_trunk_regenerate_credentials` with the required `sms_trunk` relationship. - `smpp_esme` trunks receive a new `system_id` and `password`. `http_out` trunks receive a new `auth_name` and `auth_password`. **Behavior notes** - The `201` response contains only the trunk ID. Retrieve the trunk to read the new credentials. - Other trunk types return `422`. **Affected resources** - [Regenerate SMS Trunk Credentials](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/sms-trunk-regenerate-credentials.html) - [SMS Trunk Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/sms-trunk-object.html#sms-trunk-object-v35) ### Read and update endpoints have been added for `/v3/sender_id_verifications`. `/v3/sender_id_verifications` lists the Sender ID verifications of the account and updates them. **What changed** - Added `GET` `/v3/sender_id_verifications` and `GET` `/v3/sender_id_verifications/{id}`. - Added `PATCH` `/v3/sender_id_verifications/{id}`, which changes the name, or the SMS trunk outbound messages are routed through. Send `sms_trunk` with `data: null` to unassign the trunk. **Behavior notes** - A `closed` verification cannot be updated. **Affected resources** - [Sender ID Verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sender-id-verifications/index.html) - [Get Sender ID Verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sender-id-verifications/get-sender-id-verifications.html) - [Get Sender ID Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sender-id-verifications/get-sender-id-verification.html) - [Update Sender ID Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sender-id-verifications/update-sender-id-verification.html) - [Sender ID Verification Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sender-id-verifications/sender-id-verification-object.html#sender-id-verification-object-v35) - [SMS Trunk Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/sms-trunk-object.html#sms-trunk-object-v35) ### Inbound call prices are now available for audience `api-vin.didww.com`. Inbound call price lookups and the inbound call price file are available from the Inbound Call Rates service. **What changed** - Added `GET` `/v3/lookup/prices` on host `api-vin.didww.com` (Sandbox: `api-vin-sandbox.didww.com`). - Added `GET` and `HEAD` `/v3/prices.csv.gz` on the same host, which return the gzipped CSV file `voice_in_prices.csv.gz`. - `filter[number]` is required. `filter[src_country_iso]` is optional. - The lookup returns resources of type `prices` with `destination`, `country`, `src_country_name`, `source_type`, `rate`, `connection_fee`, `initial_interval`, `next_interval`, and `reject_calls`, plus `meta.total_records`. **Behavior notes** - Requests require a bearer access token whose `aud` lists `api-vin.didww.com`. The `read` scope is enough. - `data` is never empty: no match returns `404` `price_not_found`. - `sort`, `page`, `fields`, `include`, and unknown parameters return `400`. - The file supports `If-Modified-Since` (`304`) and returns `503` `serving_failure` with `Retry-After` when it cannot be served. - An account with no price plan receives `404` `price_plan_not_assigned`. Rate-limited requests receive `429` with `Retry-After`. **Affected resources** - [Inbound Call Prices](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/inbound-call-prices/index.html) - [Look up Inbound Call Prices](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/inbound-call-prices/lookup-inbound-call-prices.html) - [Get Inbound Call Price File](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/inbound-call-prices/get-inbound-call-price-file.html) - [Inbound Call Price Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/inbound-call-prices/inbound-call-price-object.html#inbound-call-price-object-v35) ### Outbound call prices are now available for audience `api-vout.didww.com`. Outbound call price lookups, including scheduled price changes, and the outbound call price file are available from the Outbound Call Rates service. **What changed** - Added `GET` `/v3/lookup/prices` on host `api-vout.didww.com` (Sandbox: `api-vout-sandbox.didww.com`). - Added `GET` and `HEAD` `/v3/prices.csv.gz` on the same host, which return the gzipped CSV file `voice_out_prices.csv.gz`. - `filter[number]` is the only supported filter. - The lookup returns resources of type `prices` with `category`, `country`, `network`, `prefix`, `rate`, `connection_fee`, `initial_increment`, `recurring_increment`, `reject_calls`, `next_rate`, `next_connection_fee`, `next_initial_increment`, `next_recurring_increment`, `effective_at`, and `comment`, plus `meta.total_records`. **Behavior notes** - Requests require a bearer access token whose `aud` lists `api-vout.didww.com`. The response body is unchanged. **Affected resources** - [Create Encrypted File](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/create-encrypted-files.html) **Upgrade** - Accept `application/vnd.api+json` as the media type of a successful upload response. ### The `dids` relationship on `/v3/voice_out_trunks` rejects DIDs awaiting registration. `/v3/voice_out_trunks` no longer accepts a DID that is awaiting registration as an allowed CLI. **Why this is a breaking change** A create or update request that assigns such a DID in the `dids` relationship fails with `422 Unprocessable Entity`. **What changed** - `POST` `/v3/voice_out_trunks` and `PATCH` `/v3/voice_out_trunks/{id}` return `422 Unprocessable Entity` when the `dids` relationship contains a DID whose `awaiting_registration` is `true`. - The response contains one error per rejected DID, with `source.pointer` /data/relationships/dids/<DID ID>. **Affected resources** - [Create Outbound Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/create-voice-out-trunk.html#voice-out-trunks-v35-create) - [Update Outbound Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/update-voice-out-trunk.html) **Upgrade** - Assign a DID as an allowed CLI only after its registration is approved (`awaiting_registration` is `false`). ### The `Source` column in `cdr_in` files from `/v3/exports` has been replaced with `Source Number` and `Source Number Out`. `cdr_in` export files no longer contain the `Source` column. **Why this is a breaking change** Integrations that read the `Source` column by name or by position must be updated: the column is replaced, and new columns shift the positions of the columns that follow it. **What changed** - Removed the `Source` column from `cdr_in` export files. - Added `Source Number`: the caller number as it reached DIDWW. - Added `Source Number Out`: the caller number as delivered to the trunk. It holds the value previously returned in `Source`. - Added `Source Country` and `Source Network`: the country and network of the caller number. - Column order after the time columns: `Status`, `Source Number`, `Source Number Out`, `Source Name`, `Source Country`, `Source Network`, `Destination DID`, followed by the remaining columns unchanged. **Affected resources** - [Get CSV File of Export](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/get-csv-file-of-export.html) **Upgrade** - Read the caller number from `Source Number Out` instead of `Source`. - Map CSV columns by header name rather than by position. ## Enhancements ### The `is_demo` attribute has been added to `/v3/did_groups`. `/v3/did_groups` now exposes the is\_demo attribute. **What changed** - Added the read-only `is_demo` boolean attribute. - Added `filter[is_demo]` and the `is_demo` and `-is_demo` sort values. - `fields[did_groups]` accepts `number_type` and `is_demo`. **Affected resources** - [Get DID Groups](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/did-group/get-did-groups.html) - [Get DID Group](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/did-group/get-did-group.html) - [DID Group Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/did-group/did-group-object.html#did-group-object-v35) ### The `sms_trunk` and `sms_trunk_group` relationships have been added to `/v3/dids`. `/v3/dids` routes inbound SMS to an SMS trunk or an SMS trunk group. **What changed** - Added the `sms_trunk` and `sms_trunk_group` to-one relationships to DID responses. - `include`, `fields[dids]`, and the new `filter[sms_trunk.id]` and `filter[sms_trunk_group.id]` accept them. - `PATCH` `/v3/dids/{id}` accepts both relationships. **Behavior notes** - A DID routes inbound SMS to one SMS trunk or one SMS trunk group. Assigning one replaces the other. Sending both with an ID in one request returns `422 Unprocessable Entity`. - The SMS trunk must accept inbound SMS. A trunk with the `http_out` configuration type is rejected with `422`. - The DID group must support inbound SMS. Otherwise the request returns `422`. - `"data": null` clears the route only when the DID is currently routed through that relationship. **Affected resources** - [Get DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/get-dids.html) - [Get DID](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/get-did.html) - [Update DID](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/update-did.html) - [DID Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/did-object.html#did-object-v35) ### The `company_website` attribute has been added to `/v3/identities`. `/v3/identities` now exposes the company\_website attribute. **What changed** - Added the nullable attribute `company_website`. - `POST` `/v3/identities` and `PATCH` `/v3/identities/{id}` accept `company_website` for business identities. A personal identity rejects it with `422 Unprocessable Entity`. - Added the filters `company_website` (exact match) and `company_website_contains`, and the sort value `company_website`. - `company_website` can be requested with `fields[identities]`. **Behavior notes** - Once the identity is in use, for example linked to DIDs or to a verification, a stored `company_website` cannot be changed or removed, and the request returns `422 Unprocessable Entity`. **Affected resources** - [Get Identities](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/get-identities.html) - [Get Identity](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/get-identity.html) - [Create Identity](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/create-identity.html) - [Update Identity](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/update-identity.html) - [Identity Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/identity-object.html#identity-object-v35) ### The `sms_in` and `sms_out` export types have been added to `/v3/exports`. `/v3/exports` exports inbound and outbound SMS records. **What changed** - `export_type` accepts `sms_in` (inbound message records) and `sms_out` (outbound message records) in addition to `cdr_in` and `cdr_out`. - `from` and `to` are required for both types, with the same range rules as CDR exports. - Both types accept `source_address_eq`, `source_address_cont`, `destination_address_eq`, `destination_address_cont`, `status`, `sms_trunk.id`, and `sms_id`. - `sms_in` also accepts `trunk_type` (`smpp_smsc`, `smpp_esme`, `sms_to_email`, `http_in`). - `sms_out` also accepts `service_type` (`p2p` or `a2p`) and `sender_id_verification.id`. - SMS exports follow the same lifecycle as CDR exports: statuses, `external_reference_id`, callbacks (`callback_url`, `callback_method`) that include the download URL, and a `.csv.gz` download. **Behavior notes** - The `sms_out` file contains the `Sender ID Verification` column only for accounts with A2P messaging enabled. **Affected resources** - [Create Export](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/create-export.html) - [Get Exports](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/get-exports.html) - [Get CSV File of Export](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/get-csv-file-of-export.html) - [Export Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/export-object.html#export-object-v35) - [Export Filters Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/export-filters-object.html#export-filters-object-v35) - [Callback Details](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/callbacks-details.html) ### The `source_number`, `source_number_out`, and `source_country_iso` filters have been added for `cdr_in` exports in `/v3/exports`. `cdr_in` exports can be limited by caller number and caller country. **What changed** - Added the optional `source_number` filter: the caller number as it reached DIDWW. - Added the optional `source_number_out` filter: the caller number as delivered to the trunk. - Added the optional `source_country_iso` filter: an upper-case ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, for example `GB`. **Affected resources** - [Create Export](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/create-export.html) - [Export Filters Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/export-filters-object.html#export-filters-object-v35) ### The `source`, `cli`, and `destination` filters have been added for `cdr_out` exports in `/v3/exports`. `cdr_out` exports can be limited by source number, CLI, and destination number. **What changed** - Added the optional `source`, `cli`, and `destination` filters. They match the `Source`, `CLI`, and `Destination Number` file columns exactly. **Affected resources** - [Create Export](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/create-export.html) - [Export Filters Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/export-filters-object.html#export-filters-object-v35) ### The `created_at_gteq`, `created_at_lteq`, `export_type`, and `status` filters have been added to `GET /v3/exports`. The export collection can be filtered by creation time, export type, and status. **What changed** - Added `filter[created_at_gteq]` and `filter[created_at_lteq]`. - Added `filter[export_type]` with values `cdr_in`, `cdr_out`, `sms_in`, and `sms_out`. - Added `filter[status]` with values `pending`, `processing`, and `completed`. **Affected resources** - [Get Exports](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/get-exports.html) ### The `codecs` attribute has been added to `/v3/voice_out_trunks`. Outbound trunks list their codecs by name, in priority order. **What changed** - Added `codecs`, a list of names. The first codec has the highest priority. - The values are `telephone_event`, `g723`, `g729`, `pcmu`, `pcma`, `gsm`, `g722`, `opus`, `amr`, and `amr_wb`. - `codecs` defaults to `pcma`, `pcmu`, `telephone_event`. **Affected resources** - [Get Outbound Trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/get-voice-out-trunks.html) - [Get Outbound Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/get-voice-out-trunk.html) - [Create Outbound Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/create-voice-out-trunk.html) - [Update Outbound Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/update-voice-out-trunk.html) - [Outbound Trunk Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/voice-out-trunk-object.html#voice-out-trunk-object-v35) ### ICE and RTCP modes have been added to `/v3/voice_in_trunks` and `/v3/voice_out_trunks`. Trunks set how ICE, RTCP multiplexing, and RTCP feedback are handled on their calls. **What changed** - Added `ice_mode`, `rtcp_mux_mode`, and `rtcp_feedback_mode`, with the values `disabled`, `accept`, and `initiate`. - On inbound trunks these attributes are part of the SIP `configuration` and default to `disabled`. - On outbound trunks they default to `accept`. **Affected resources** - [Create Inbound Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-in-trunks/create-voice-in-trunk.html) - [Update Inbound Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-in-trunks/update-voice-in-trunk.html) - [Inbound Trunk Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-in-trunks/voice-in-trunk-object.html#voice-in-trunk-object-v35) - [Create Outbound Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/create-voice-out-trunk.html) - [Update Outbound Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/update-voice-out-trunk.html) - [Outbound Trunk Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/voice-out-trunk-object.html#voice-out-trunk-object-v35) ### Operations answer `429 Too Many Requests` with `Retry-After`. Requests spend the account's rate-limit budget. Once it is spent, the answer is `429` with `Retry-After`. **What changed** - The operations that can answer `429` list it in their responses. - `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait. **Affected resources** - [Authentication](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/authentication.html#authentication-v35) ### `GET /v3/exports/{filename}.csv.gz` accepts bearer access tokens. The export file download accepts an access token as well as an API key. **What changed** - The download accepts Authorization: Bearer <access token>, like every other request in this version. - The download also accepts an API key in the `Api-Key` header. **Affected resources** - [Get CSV File of Export](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/get-csv-file-of-export.html) - [Authentication](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/authentication.html#authentication-v35)

request.description: ## Mint an access token HTTP Method: `POST` URL: `https://auth.didww.com/token` (Production), `https://auth-sandbox.didww.com/token` (Sandbox) The token service uses plain JSON, not JSON:API. ### Request headers | Header | Is Required? | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `Api-Key` | Yes | API key created in the User Panel of the same environment. | | `Content-Type` | Yes | Must be `application/json`. | ### Request body | Name | Type | Is Required? | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | aud | `string` or Array of `strings` | Yes | The service or services that will accept the token. Provide one audience string or an array of audience strings. Duplicates are ignored. An unknown audience rejects the whole token request. See [Audiences](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/authentication.html#authentication-audiences-v35) to choose the value for your operation. | | scope | `string` | No | `full` (default) or `read`. An empty value or `null` grants the default. A `read:` value that is not known, such as `read:prices`, is granted as its closest known ancestor, so compare `scope` in the response with the one requested. Any other value is refused. See [Scopes](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/authentication.html#authentication-scopes-v35). | | api\_version | `string` | No | Name of the API version the token selects on `api.didww.com`, in the `YYYY-MM-DD` format, for example `2026-11-19`. If omitted, the default version of the account is used, or the current default version of the platform when the account has none. See [Version selection](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/authentication.html#authentication-version-v35). | | expires\_in | `integer` | No | Requested token lifetime in seconds. Default: `900`. A value outside `60`-`3600` is clamped into that range, not refused. | ### Response attributes A successful request returns `200 OK` with `Content-Type: application/json`, `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Pragma: no-cache`. | Name | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | access\_token | `string` | The access token. Send it as Authorization: Bearer <access_token>. It is valid only in the environment that minted it. | | token\_type | `string` | Always `Bearer`. | | expires\_in | `integer` | Lifetime granted, in seconds, from `60` to `3600`. | | aud | Array of `strings` | The services the token was minted for. | | scope | `string` | The scope granted: `full` or `read`. It can be wider than the one requested when a `read:` value was granted as its ancestor. | | api\_version | `string` | The version name the token carries: the requested one or, when `api_version` is omitted, the default version of the account, or the current default version of the platform when the account has none. |

item.description: DIDWW API v3 version `2026-11-19` authenticates requests with short-lived bearer access tokens. Authentication takes two steps: 1. Exchange an API key for an access token with `POST /token` on the DIDWW token service of your environment. 2. Send the access token in the `Authorization` request header of every API request: ``` Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN ``` In version `2026-11-19`, an API key sent in the `Api-Key` header is refused with `401 Unauthorized`. The API key is used only to mint access tokens. The following operations are the exceptions: | Operation | Credential | | --- | --- | | `POST /token` on the token service | API key in the `Api-Key` header. | | `GET /v3/exports/{filename}.csv.gz` ([Get CSV File of Export](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/get-csv-file-of-export.html)) | Either an access token in the `Authorization` header or an API key in the `Api-Key` header. | | `GET /v3/public_keys` ([Public Keys](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/public-keys.html)) | No authentication. | The same access tokens authenticate requests to the DIDWW prices services. See [Prices Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/index.html). --- ## API keys API keys are created and managed in the DIDWW User Panel. For creation instructions, see [How to Get Your API Key](https://doc.didww.com/api3/configuration.html#api-key). When creating an API key, you can configure: | Setting | Description | | --- | --- | | Friendly name | A recognizable name for the API key. | | Allowed IP addresses | Optional source-IP restrictions. They apply to requests made with the key (token requests and the export file download) and are copied into each access token minted with it. A change applies to tokens minted afterwards, not to tokens already issued. | --- ## Environments | Environment | Token service | API base URL | Manage API keys | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Sandbox | `https://auth-sandbox.didww.com/token` | `https://sandbox-api.didww.com/v3` | [Sandbox User Panel](https://my-sandbox.didww.com/#/api) | | Production | `https://auth.didww.com/token` | `https://api.didww.com/v3` | [Production User Panel](https://my.didww.com/#/api) | Production and Sandbox use separate accounts and API keys. Mint tokens on the token service of the environment you call, with an API key created in that environment. An access token is accepted only in the environment that minted it. --- ## Mint an access token HTTP Method: `POST` URL: `https://auth.didww.com/token` (Production), `https://auth-sandbox.didww.com/token` (Sandbox) The token service uses plain JSON, not JSON:API. ### Request headers | Header | Is Required? | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `Api-Key` | Yes | API key created in the User Panel of the same environment. | | `Content-Type` | Yes | Must be `application/json`. | ### Request body | Name | Type | Is Required? | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | aud | `string` or Array of `strings` | Yes | The service or services that will accept the token. Provide one audience string or an array of audience strings. Duplicates are ignored. An unknown audience rejects the whole token request. See [Audiences](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/authentication.html#authentication-audiences-v35) to choose the value for your operation. | | scope | `string` | No | `full` (default) or `read`. An empty value or `null` grants the default. A `read:` value that is not known, such as `read:prices`, is granted as its closest known ancestor, so compare `scope` in the response with the one requested. Any other value is refused. See [Scopes](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/authentication.html#authentication-scopes-v35). | | api\_version | `string` | No | Name of the API version the token selects on `api.didww.com`, in the `YYYY-MM-DD` format, for example `2026-11-19`. If omitted, the default version of the account is used, or the current default version of the platform when the account has none. See [Version selection](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/authentication.html#authentication-version-v35). | | expires\_in | `integer` | No | Requested token lifetime in seconds. Default: `900`. A value outside `60`-`3600` is clamped into that range, not refused. | ### Response attributes A successful request returns `200 OK` with `Content-Type: application/json`, `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Pragma: no-cache`. | Name | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | access\_token | `string` | The access token. Send it as Authorization: Bearer <access_token>. It is valid only in the environment that minted it. | | token\_type | `string` | Always `Bearer`. | | expires\_in | `integer` | Lifetime granted, in seconds, from `60` to `3600`. | | aud | Array of `strings` | The services the token was minted for. | | scope | `string` | The scope granted: `full` or `read`. It can be wider than the one requested when a `read:` value was granted as its ancestor. | | api\_version | `string` | The version name the token carries: the requested one or, when `api_version` is omitted, the default version of the account, or the current default version of the platform when the account has none. | ### Examples **Full Access Token** **Request** ``` 1POST /token HTTP/1.1 2Host: auth.didww.com 3Content-Type: application/json 4Api-Key: [API key] 5 6{ 7 "aud": "api.didww.com", 8 "api_version": "2026-11-19" 9} ``` **Response** ``` 1HTTP/1.1 200 OK 2Content-Type: application/json 3Cache-Control: no-store 4Pragma: no-cache 5 6{ 7 "access_token": "eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOi...", 8 "token_type": "Bearer", 9 "expires_in": 900, 10 "aud": [ 11 "api.didww.com" 12 ], 13 "scope": "full", 14 "api_version": "2026-11-19" 15} ``` **Read-only Token for Several Services** **Request** ``` 1POST /token HTTP/1.1 2Host: auth.didww.com 3Content-Type: application/json 4Api-Key: [API key] 5 6{ 7 "aud": [ 8 "api.didww.com", 9 "api-vout.didww.com" 10 ], 11 "scope": "read", 12 "api_version": "2026-11-19", 13 "expires_in": 3600 14} ``` **Response** ``` 1HTTP/1.1 200 OK 2Content-Type: application/json 3Cache-Control: no-store 4Pragma: no-cache 5 6{ 7 "access_token": "eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOi...", 8 "token_type": "Bearer", 9 "expires_in": 3600, 10 "aud": [ 11 "api.didww.com", 12 "api-vout.didww.com" 13 ], 14 "scope": "read", 15 "api_version": "2026-11-19" 16} ``` **Unknown Audience** **Request** ``` 1POST /token HTTP/1.1 2Host: auth.didww.com 3Content-Type: application/json 4Api-Key: [API key] 5 6{ 7 "aud": "example.com" 8} ``` **Response** ``` 1HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request 2Content-Type: application/json 3Cache-Control: no-store 4Pragma: no-cache 5 6{ 7 "error": "invalid_request", 8 "error_description": "aud is not a configured audience" 9} ``` --- ## Use the access token Send the access token in the `Authorization` header with the `Bearer` prefix: **Request** ``` 1GET /v3/countries HTTP/1.1 2Host: api.didww.com 3Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json 4Accept: application/vnd.api+json 5Authorization: Bearer [access token] ``` **Response** ``` 1HTTP/1.1 200 OK 2Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json 3 4{ 5 "data": [ 6 { 7 "id": "9c56fe0f-eff0-4742-85f6-24868959344a", 8 "type": "countries", 9 "attributes": { 10 "name": "United Kingdom", 11 "prefix": "44", 12 "iso": "GB" 13 }, 14 "relationships": { 15 "regions": { 16 "links": { 17 "self": "https://api.didww.com/v3/countries/9c56fe0f-eff0-4742-85f6-24868959344a/relationships/regions", 18 "related": "https://api.didww.com/v3/countries/9c56fe0f-eff0-4742-85f6-24868959344a/regions" 19 } 20 } 21 } 22 } 23 ], 24 "meta": { 25 "api_version": "2026-11-19" 26 } 27} ``` Reuse the same token for every request until it expires. A token is accepted only when all of the following hold: - it has not expired; - it was minted in the environment of the API you call; - its `aud` lists the service you call; - the request comes from an address allowed by the IP restrictions the API key had when the token was minted; - its scope covers the request method. ### Version selection For requests authenticated with an access token, the API version is selected by the token's `api_version`, set when the token is minted. The `X-DIDWW-API-Version` request header does not select the version of a bearer request. - If `api_version` is omitted when minting, the token carries the default version of the account. For an account without a default version, it carries the current default version of the platform, which can change when a newer version is released. Minting tokens and requests with access tokens do not assign a default version to the account. - A well-formed version name that the API does not know selects the newest version. - An access token is never served a version older than `2026-11-19`, the first version that accepts access tokens, nor a version older than the default version of the account. Set `api_version` explicitly and check `meta.api_version` in the responses to confirm the version that served the request. For version policy and upgrade steps, see [API Versioning and Deprecation Policy](https://doc.didww.com/api3/api-versioning.html). ### Scopes | Scope | Allowed requests | | --- | --- | | `full` | All methods. This is the default. | | `read` | `GET` and `HEAD` only. Any other method is refused with `403 Forbidden` and `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope"`. | Use a `read` token for integrations that only read data, such as reporting or price downloads. ### Audiences The audience (`aud`) attribute specifies which DIDWW services can accept your access token. Use the production host name of the service you call, even when using its sandbox host. For multiple services, provide an array of their production host names. | Audience | Use for | Production host | Sandbox host | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `api.didww.com` | [All main API resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/overview.html). | `api.didww.com` | `sandbox-api.didww.com` | | `api-vin.didww.com` | [Inbound call rates](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/inbound-call-prices/index.html): look up rates for toll-free, shared-cost and metered numbers, or download the assigned price list. | `api-vin.didww.com` | `api-vin-sandbox.didww.com` | | `api-vout.didww.com` | [Outbound call rates](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/outbound-call-prices/index.html): look up current and scheduled rates, or download the assigned price list. | `api-vout.didww.com` | `api-vout-sandbox.didww.com` | | `api-sms.didww.com` | [SMS rates](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/sms-prices/index.html): look up inbound SMS rates and outbound A2P, P2P and OTP SMS rates, or download the assigned price lists. | `api-sms.didww.com` | `api-sms-sandbox.didww.com` | The three dedicated price services provide the price lookups, price-file downloads and file-header checks listed in [Prices Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/index.html). Configuring inbound voice trunks, outbound voice trunks and SMS trunks uses `api.didww.com`. For example, creating an outbound voice trunk uses `POST /v3/voice_out_trunks` on `api.didww.com`. Looking up the outbound call rate for a destination uses `GET /v3/lookup/prices` on `api-vout.didww.com`. Mint one token per service, or list every service you call in one token. An integration that manages outbound voice trunks and reads outbound call rates needs both `api.didww.com` and `api-vout.didww.com` in `aud`. ### Token lifetime and renewal A token is valid for the `expires_in` seconds returned when it is minted: `900` by default, from `60` to `3600` on request. Tokens cannot be refreshed. Mint a new token before the current one expires, and keep using the current token until then instead of minting one per request. On `api.didww.com`, a token is refused before it expires once the API key it was minted with is deleted, or once API access is disabled for the account. --- ## Authentication errors ### Token service errors Errors from `POST /token` are returned as JSON objects with `error` and `error_description`, and carry `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Pragma: no-cache`. | Status code | `error` | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | `400 Bad Request` | `invalid_request` | The body is not valid JSON, `aud` is missing or lists an unknown service, `api_version` is not a version name, or `expires_in` is not an integer. `error_description` names the parameter at fault. | | `400 Bad Request` | `invalid_scope` | `scope` holds several values or an unknown value outside the `read` family. | | `401 Unauthorized` | `invalid_client` | The API key is missing, unknown, disabled, belongs to another environment, or is used from an address it does not allow. | | `429 Too Many Requests` | `rate_limit_exceeded` | Too many token requests from this address. The `Retry-After` header gives the number of seconds to wait before retrying. | ### API errors The following responses apply to `api.didww.com`. For the prices services, see [Prices Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/index.html). | Status code | `WWW-Authenticate` | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | `401 Unauthorized` | `Bearer error="invalid_token"` | The access token was refused: it is malformed or expired, was minted for another audience or environment, is presented from an address outside the IP restrictions it was minted with, or the API key it was minted with has been deleted or API access is disabled for the account. The body is a JSON:API error object with code `401`. | | `401 Unauthorized` | None | The request has no access token: it sends no credentials or only an `Api-Key` header. The body is a JSON:API error object with code `401`. Only [Get CSV File of Export](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/get-csv-file-of-export.html), which accepts an API key, answers a missing or refused API key with an empty body. An API key sent from an address outside its allowed IP addresses receives `403 Forbidden` instead. | | `403 Forbidden` | `Bearer error="insufficient_scope"` | The token's scope does not cover the request method, for example a `read` token sending `POST`, `PATCH` or `DELETE`. The body is a JSON:API error object with title `Insufficient scope`. | | `403 Forbidden` | None | Authentication succeeded, but the account is not allowed to perform the requested operation. | | `429 Too Many Requests` | None | The request budget of the account for the current window is spent (`too_many_requests`). `Retry-After` gives the number of seconds to wait. | The following example shows a `read` token sending a write request: **Request** ``` 1PATCH /v3/dids/9df99644-f1a5-4a3c-99a4-559d758eb96b HTTP/1.1 2Host: api.didww.com 3Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json 4Accept: application/vnd.api+json 5Authorization: Bearer [access token] 6 7{ 8 "data": { 9 "id": "9df99644-f1a5-4a3c-99a4-559d758eb96b", 10 "type": "dids", 11 "attributes": { 12 "description": "Support line" 13 } 14 } 15} ``` **Response** ``` 1HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden 2Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json 3WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope" 4 5{ 6 "errors": [ 7 { 8 "title": "Insufficient scope", 9 "detail": "The token does not carry the full scope this operation requires.", 10 "code": "403", 11 "status": "403" 12 } 13 ] 14} ``` --- ## Security recommendations Keep API keys and access tokens secure and use them only from trusted server-side environments. Recommended practices: - Store API keys in environment variables or a secure secrets manager. - Mint access tokens on your server. Do not expose API keys or access tokens in client-side code, public repositories, browser applications, mobile apps, or logs. - Request only the audiences and the scope the integration needs, and prefer a short lifetime. - Use allowed IP address restrictions where possible. They are copied into the access tokens minted with the key, so mint new tokens after changing them. - Use separate API keys for different applications or environments. - Replace API keys if they may have been exposed. - Remove API keys that are no longer used. ## Related pages - [OpenAPI Reference](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/api-reference.html) - [Getting Started](https://doc.didww.com/api3/configuration.html) - [API Specification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/specification/index.html) - [API Requests in Postman](https://doc.didww.com/api3/postman.html) - [DIDWW API Sandbox](https://doc.didww.com/api3/sandbox.html)

item.name: Specification
Sorting
item.description:
You can sort API results by one or more fields using the `sort` parameter. Separate multiple fields with commas.

If no sorting option is specified, results are sorted by their ID (for example, country ID, order ID, or CDR ID) in ascending order.

> **Note**
>
> Sorting applies to any endpoint that returns a resource collection as primary data, regardless of the request type.

---

## Sorting DIDs by expiration date

You can retrieve a list of DIDs sorted by their `expires_at` attribute in ascending order (earliest expiration date first). Use this to view DIDs based on their expiration sequence and prioritize those that are expiring soon.

**Request**

```
1GET /v3/dids?sort=expires_at HTTP/1.1
2Host: api.didww.com
3Accept: application/vnd.api+json
```

---

## Sorting by related resource attributes

You can sort results based on attributes of related resources using dot notation.
For example, sorting DIDs by `did_group.area_name` organizes them according to their associated area name.

This is useful for grouping DIDs by their geographic or organizational classification.

**Request**

```
1GET /v3/dids?sort=did_group.area_name HTTP/1.1
2Host: api.didww.com
3Accept: application/vnd.api+json
```

---

## Sorting by multiple fields

You can sort results by multiple fields, separated by commas.
Fields are applied in the order they are listed.

In this example, results are sorted first by `did_group.area_name` and then, for DIDs with the same area name, by `number` in ascending order.

This helps you organize data hierarchically, starting with broader attributes and refining by more specific ones.

**Request**

```
1GET /v3/dids?sort=did_group.area_name%2Cnumber HTTP/1.1
2Host: api.didww.com
3Accept: application/vnd.api+json
```

In this example, DIDs are sorted by `did_group.area_name` first, and then by `number`.

---

## Reverse sorting

Prefixing a field with a minus sign (`-`) sorts it in descending order.
In this example, DIDs are sorted by `did_group.area_name` from Z to A, and then by `number` in ascending order within each area.

This is useful when you need to view the most recent or highest-value items first.

**Request**

```
1GET /v3/dids?sort=-did_group.area_name%2Cnumber HTTP/1.1
2Host: api.didww.com
3Accept: application/vnd.api+json
```

item.name: Pagination
item.description:
Pagination helps manage large datasets by dividing results into pages. Use the `page` query parameter to control the size of each page and specify which page to retrieve.

If pagination is not applied, some endpoints may return all records in a single response.

> **Important**
>
> - Pagination applies to any endpoint that returns a resource collection as primary data, regardless of the request type.
> - Page size is **50** by default, unless it is overridden at a particular endpoint.
> - The maximum page size is **100**, unless it is overridden at a particular endpoint.
> - If `page[number]` is not specified, page **1** is returned by default.
> - Some endpoints may disable pagination and return all records in a single response.

---

## Define page size

Use the `page[size]` parameter to set the maximum number of items returned per page.

In this example, the cities collection returns up to 10 records per page.
If `page[size]` is not specified, page size is **50** by default, unless it is overridden at a particular endpoint.

**Request**

```
1GET /v3/cities?page%5Bsize%5D=10 HTTP/1.1
2Host: api.didww.com
3Accept: application/vnd.api+json
4Authorization: Bearer [access token]
```

---

## Retrieve a specific page

Use the `page[number]` parameter to request a specific page of results.

For example, if the `page[size]` is set to `10` and the `page[number]` is set to `3`, entry numbers `21` to `30` will be returned in the data.

**Request**

```
1GET /v3/cities?page%5Bnumber%5D=3&page%5Bsize%5D=10 HTTP/1.1
2Host: api.didww.com
3Accept: application/vnd.api+json
4Authorization: Bearer [access token]
```

---

## Pagination links

Paginated responses include navigation links in the top-level `links` object:

- `first` - the first page of data
- `last` - the last page of data
- `prev` - the previous page of data
- `next` - the next page of data

These links help you navigate through paginated results without manually calculating page numbers.

Follow the `next` link returned by the server while another page is available.
Preserve your filters and requested includes when paging through a collection.
Check the endpoint's [OpenAPI Reference](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/api-reference.html) for
pagination support and endpoint-specific page-size limits. The Countries collection,
for example, does not use pagination.

item.name: Filtering
item.description:
Filtering allows you to narrow API results using specific conditions. You can filter resources by one or more attributes using query parameters that start with `filter`.

This feature supports both simple and complex queries, including combining multiple conditions and using arrays.

> **Important**
>
> Filters are supported on any endpoint that responds with a resource collection.

---

## Filter by a single attribute

Use a single filter parameter to retrieve resources matching a specific value.

In this example, cities are filtered by their `country.id` and returns only cities within the specified country:

**Request**

```
1GET /v3/cities?filter%5Bcountry.id%5D=72f22218-ab1f-4933-a74d-a6467f3f6cb0 HTTP/1.1
2Host: api.didww.com
3Accept: application/vnd.api+json
```

---

## Filter by multiple attributes

You can combine multiple filter parameters to refine results further.

In this example, cities are filtered by both `country.id` and `region.id`, and returns only cities that match both conditions:

**Request**

```
1GET /v3/cities?filter%5Bcountry.id%5D=72f22218-ab1f-4933-a74d-a6467f3f6cb0&filter%5Bregion.id%5D=0800cac6-a0eb-4d58-8284-e5207b65a91b HTTP/1.1
2Host: api.didww.com
3Accept: application/vnd.api+json
```

---

## Filter by arrays

You can use arrays in filters by separating values with commas.

For example, to filter DIDs that support specified features such as voice, voice\_out, t38, sms, sms\_out:

```
filter[features]=voice,voice_out,t38,sms,sms_out
```

> **Important**
>
> Do **not** provide the same filter multiple times (e.g., `filter[features]=voice&filter[features]=sms`). Instead, use a single filter with comma-separated values.

item.name: Inclusion of Related Resources
item.description:
The `include` parameter allows you to retrieve related resources in a single request.
This is also known as **side-loading** and reduces the need for multiple API calls by returning related objects alongside the primary resource.

Included resources are returned in the top-level `included` array. The `relationships` object of each resource links to them by `type` and `id`.

> **Note**
>
> Using `include` reduces the number of requests needed to fetch related data and improves performance when working with linked resources.

---

## Include a single related resource

You can include a single related resource by specifying it in the `include` parameter.

In this example, each DID record includes its associated `voice_in_trunk` resource.
This allows you to retrieve additional details about related resources without sending a separate request:

**Request**

```
1GET /v3/dids?include=voice_in_trunk HTTP/1.1
2Host: api.didww.com
3Accept: application/vnd.api+json
```

---

## Include multiple related resources

You can include multiple related resources by separating them with commas.

In this example, the request includes the DID's `voice_in_trunk` and `voice_in_trunk_group` resources in a single request.

**Request**

```
1GET /v3/dids?include=voice_in_trunk%2Cvoice_in_trunk_group HTTP/1.1
2Host: api.didww.com
3Accept: application/vnd.api+json
```

---

## Include nested related resources

You can also include relationships of already-included objects.

In this example, the request includes `voice_in_trunk` and its related `voice_in_trunk_group`:

**Request**

```
1GET /v3/dids?include=voice_in_trunk.voice_in_trunk_group HTTP/1.1
2Host: api.didww.com
3Accept: application/vnd.api+json
```

item.name: Sparse Fieldsets
item.description:
Sparse fieldsets allow you to limit the number of attributes returned for a resource.
Use the `fields` query parameter to request only the specific attributes you need, reducing payload size and improving performance.

This feature is especially useful when working with large or complex datasets, or when optimizing API responses for performance, bandwidth, or security.
For example, you can:

- Retrieve only specific status attributes (e.g., `terminated` or `blocked`) to monitor resource state.
- Fetch minimal data when displaying resource lists or summaries.
- Limit sensitive or unused fields in API integrations to control data exposure.

> **Tip**
>
> Combine sparse fieldsets with other query parameters such as [filter](https://doc.didww.com/api3/specification/filtering.html#api-filters) or [include](https://doc.didww.com/api3/specification/includes.html#api-includes) to build efficient and highly targeted API requests.

This follows the [JSON:API sparse fieldsets](https://jsonapi.org/format/#fetching-sparse-fieldsets) specification.

> **Note**
>
> Sparse fieldsets can be applied to any endpoint that returns a resource collection or a single resource object.
> Use this feature to retrieve only the most relevant fields for your application.

---

## Retrieve a Single Attribute

You can request a specific attribute by passing its name in the `fields` parameter.

In this example, the response for DIDs includes only the `terminated` attribute:

**Request**

```
1GET /v3/dids?fields%5Bdids%5D=terminated HTTP/1.1
2Host: api.didww.com
3Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json
4Accept: application/vnd.api+json
5Authorization: Bearer [access token]
```

**Response**

```
 1HTTP/1.1 200 OK
 2Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json
 3
 4{
 5  "data": [
 6    {
 7      "id": "d223efc9-34c3-48e4-9f1e-7a1057808127",
 8      "type": "dids",
 9      "attributes": {
10        "terminated": false
11      }
12    }
13  ],
14  "meta": {
15    "total_records": 1,
16    "api_version": "2026-11-19"
17  },
18  "links": {
19    "first": "https://api.didww.com/v3/dids?fields%5Bdids%5D=terminated&page%5Bnumber%5D=1&page%5Bsize%5D=50",
20    "last": "https://api.didww.com/v3/dids?fields%5Bdids%5D=terminated&page%5Bnumber%5D=1&page%5Bsize%5D=50"
21  }
22}
```

This is useful when you only need a single attribute from each resource, such as a DID's termination state.

---

## Retrieve Multiple Attributes

To include more than one attribute, list them as comma-separated values within the `fields` parameter.

In this example, the response includes both `terminated` and `blocked` attributes:

**Request**

```
1GET /v3/dids?fields%5Bdids%5D=terminated%2Cblocked HTTP/1.1
2Host: api.didww.com
3Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json
4Accept: application/vnd.api+json
5Authorization: Bearer [access token]
```

**Response**

```
 1HTTP/1.1 200 OK
 2Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json
 3
 4{
 5  "data": [
 6    {
 7      "id": "d223efc9-34c3-48e4-9f1e-7a1057808127",
 8      "type": "dids",
 9      "attributes": {
10        "terminated": false,
11        "blocked": false
12      }
13    },
14    {
15      "id": "2c2a4cdd-5514-419f-abe2-2777d9b95533",
16      "type": "dids",
17      "attributes": {
18        "terminated": false,
19        "blocked": false
20      }
21    }
22  ],
23  "meta": {
24    "total_records": 2,
25    "api_version": "2026-11-19"
26  },
27  "links": {
28    "first": "https://api.didww.com/v3/dids?fields%5Bdids%5D=terminated%2Cblocked&page%5Bnumber%5D=1&page%5Bsize%5D=50",
29    "last": "https://api.didww.com/v3/dids?fields%5Bdids%5D=terminated%2Cblocked&page%5Bnumber%5D=1&page%5Bsize%5D=50"
30  }
31}
```

This approach helps minimize unnecessary data transfer while retrieving key status attributes.

---

## Apply Sparse Fieldsets to Multiple Resources

When including related resources, you can define separate `fields` parameters for each type.

In this example, the request returns only selected attributes for both `dids` and their related `did_group` resources:

**Request**

```
1GET /v3/dids?include=did_group&fields%5Bdids%5D=number%2Cterminated&fields%5Bdid_groups%5D=area_name HTTP/1.1
2Host: api.didww.com
3Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json
4Accept: application/vnd.api+json
5Authorization: Bearer [access token]
```

**Response**

```

12      }

18      "type": "did_groups",
```

This allows you to retrieve compact responses containing exactly the fields you need across related objects.

item.name: Headers
item.description: API requests and responses must use specific headers to comply with the JSON API specification. These headers define the content type, accepted formats, and authentication requirements. --- ## Client responsibilities Clients must include the following headers in requests: - `Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json` - Required for all requests that send JSON API data. Do **not** include media type parameters. If these headers are not correctly set, the server may reject the request. --- ## Server responsibilities Servers must include the following headers in responses: - `Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json` - All responses containing JSON API data must use this header without media type parameters. Servers return the following errors if headers are invalid: - **415 Unsupported Media Type** - Returned if the request contains a `Content-Type` header with invalid parameters. - **406 Not Acceptable** - Returned if the request's `Accept` header specifies JSON API but modifies it with parameters. Refer to the [JSON API specification](https://jsonapi.org/format/#content-negotiation) for detailed content negotiation rules. --- ## Required headers The table below lists the required headers for all API requests: | **Header** | **Optional** | **Description** | | --- | --- | --- | | `Accept` | No | Must be `application/vnd.api+json`. | | `Content-Type` | No | Must be `application/vnd.api+json`. | | `Authorization` | No (version 2026-11-19) | `Bearer` followed by an access token, for example Authorization: Bearer <access token>. Used for authentication in version 2026-11-19. See [Authentication for API v2026-11-19](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/authentication.html). | | `Api-Key` | No (versions up to 2026-04-16) | [API key](https://doc.didww.com/api3/configuration.html#api-key) used for authentication in versions up to 2026-04-16. In version 2026-11-19, it is sent to the token service to mint access tokens; the API refuses it, except for the export file download. |

item.name: Assigning of Related Resources
Errors
item.description:
The DIDWW API returns JSON:API error responses with a top-level `errors` array.
Each error includes a human-readable `title` and `detail`, a machine-readable
`code`, and the HTTP `status` represented as a string.

Inspect every entry in `errors`; a validation response can describe more than
one invalid field. The application-specific `code` is not necessarily the HTTP
status code. For example, validation errors use code `100` with status `422`.
When supplied, `source.pointer` identifies the affected field or relationship
using a JSON Pointer into the request document.

See [OpenAPI Reference](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/api-reference.html) for the typed error
schema and documented status codes for each endpoint. The compressed Export
file-download endpoint is not a JSON:API success response; see
[Download Export File](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/get-csv-file-of-export.html).

---

## Validation Error Object

A validation error occurs when a request contains invalid or missing data.

| **Name** | **Type** | **Nullable** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string | False | Short error description. |
| `detail` | string | False | Detailed error description. |
| `code` | string | False | Always returns `100`. |
| `source.pointer` | string | False | Path to the error attribute or relationship in the request payload. |

## Can't Be Blank Error Object

This validation error occurs when a required attribute is missing from the request.

| **Name** | **Type** | **Nullable** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string | False | Always returns `can't be blank`. |
| `detail` | string | False | Field-specific message describing which required attribute is missing. |
| `code` | string | False | Always returns `100`. |
| `source.pointer` | string | False | Path to the missing attribute in the request payload. |
| `status` | string | False | HTTP status code `422`. |

---

## Bad Request Error Object

This error occurs when the request contains an invalid or not allowed parameter or attribute.

| **Name** | **Type** | **Nullable** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string | False | Short error description, for example `Param not allowed`. |
| `detail` | string | False | Detailed message describing which parameter or attribute is not allowed. |
| `code` | string | False | Error-specific code, for example `105` for a parameter that is not allowed. |
| `status` | string | False | HTTP status code `400`. |

---

## Not Found Error Object

This error occurs when the requested resource cannot be found.

| **Name** | **Type** | **Nullable** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string | False | Record not found. |
| `detail` | string | False | The record identified by `{id}` could not be found. |
| `code` | string | False | Always returns `404`. |
| `status` | string | False | HTTP status code `404`. |

---

## Insufficient Balance Error Object

This error occurs when your account balance is too low to complete the request.

| **Name** | **Type** | **Nullable** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string | False | Insufficient balance. |
| `detail` | string | False | Insufficient balance. |
| `code` | string | False | HTTP status code or error code returned by the API, for example `400`. |
| `status` | string | False | HTTP status code `400`. |
| `meta.total_cost` | string | False | Total cost of the current order only. |
| `meta.available_balance` | string | False | Customer balance including credit at the time of the check. |

### Example

item.description:
Use the Countries resource to retrieve countries available in the DIDWW inventory.

A country represents the top-level geographic market used by Coverage Resources. Country
records can be used to filter related resources such as regions, cities, NANPA prefixes,
DID Groups, and Available DIDs.

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retrieve all countries | `GET` | `/v3/countries` |
| Retrieve a country | `GET` | `/v3/countries/{id}` |

## Retrieve all countries

Retrieves all countries available in the DIDWW inventory.

See [Retrieve All Countries](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/countries/get-countries.html).

```
GET /v3/countries
```

## Retrieve a country

Retrieves a specific country by its unique ID.

See [Retrieve a Country](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/countries/get-country.html).

```
GET /v3/countries/{id}
```

## Common country use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Filter DID inventory by country | Use country IDs to retrieve DID Groups available for a specific country. |
| Find regions in a country | Use a country ID to retrieve regions available within that country. |
| Find cities in a country | Use a country ID to retrieve cities available within that country. |
| Search country-level coverage | Find countries where DIDWW provides DID coverage. |
| Check DID availability | Use countries with DID Groups or Available DIDs to check whether DID numbers are available for purchase in a selected country. |
| Filter NANPA prefixes | Use country IDs to retrieve NANPA prefixes for supported countries with country code `+1`. |

## Related resources

Use the country ID to filter other Coverage Resources.

| Resource | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [Regions](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/regions/index.html) | Regions available for a country. |
| [Cities](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/city/index.html) | Cities available for a country. |
| [NANPA Prefixes](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/nanpa/index.html) | NANPA prefixes available for supported countries. |
| [DID Groups](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/did-group/index.html) | DID inventory groups available for a country. |
