request.description:
Creates an outbound trunk.

In version `2026-11-19`, customers with the Outbound API enabled can create outbound trunks even if the Outbound feature is not enabled on the account. Without the Outbound API, the request returns `403 Forbidden`.

## Request

HTTP Method: `POST`

URI Path: `/v3/voice_out_trunks`

### Body Parameters

| Name | Type | Nullable | Is Required? | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| type | `string` | No | Yes | Must be `voice_out_trunks`. |
| attributes | `object` | No | Yes | Outbound trunk attributes object. |

### Data Attributes

| Name | Type | Nullable | Is Required? | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| name | `string` | No | Yes | The outbound trunk name. |
| external\_reference\_id | `string` | Yes | No | Optional identifier for the outbound trunk in the customer's external system. Maximum length is 100 characters. |
| allowed\_rtp\_ips | Array of `strings` | Yes | No | Allowed RTP IP addresses for media traffic. Null means no restriction. An empty list is rejected. `0.0.0.0/0` and `::/0` are rejected. |
| authentication\_method | `object` | No | Yes | Authentication method object. Supported POST types: `credentials_and_ip` - use SIP credentials together with allowed IP addresses. `twilio` - use a Twilio Account SID for authentication. `ip_only` is not supported in `POST` requests. |
| on\_cli\_mismatch\_action | `string` | No | Yes | Possible values: `send_original_cli` - pass the original `From` header value from your system to the destination without modification. `reject_call` - reject the call if the `From` header value does not match any DID allowed on the trunk. `replace_cli` - replace the CLI with one of the DIDs allowed on the trunk. `randomize_cli` - replace the CLI with a random DID allowed on the trunk. An action the account does not have the feature for is rejected. |
| capacity\_limit | `integer` | Yes | No | The capacity limit of the outbound trunk. Allowed values from 1 to 32767. |
| allow\_any\_did\_as\_cli | `boolean` | No | No | When set to `true`, all eligible DIDs can be used as CLI and the `dids` relationship must not contain explicit DIDs. |
| status | `string` | No | No | Possible values: `active` - the trunk can be used for outbound traffic. `blocked` - outbound traffic on the trunk is blocked. If omitted, the default value is `active`. |
| threshold\_amount | `string` | No | No | The outbound trunk 24-hour threshold limit. The accepted range depends on the account. |
| default\_dst\_action | `string` | No | No | Possible values: `allow_all` - allow calls to all destinations except the prefixes listed in `dst_prefixes`. `reject_all` - reject calls to all destinations except the prefixes listed in `dst_prefixes`. |
| dst\_prefixes | Array of `strings` | No | No | The destination prefixes allowed or rejected based on `default_dst_action`. Each prefix is digits only, without a leading `+` or separators; any other value returns `422 Unprocessable Entity`. Repeated prefixes are stored once. |
| emergency\_enable\_all | `boolean` | No | No | Allows all eligible DIDs to be used for emergency calling on the trunk. Default value is `false`. |
| media\_encryption\_mode | `string` | No | No | Media encryption mode. Possible values: `disabled` - media encryption is turned off. `srtp_sdes` - use SRTP encryption with SDES key exchange. `srtp_dtls` - use SRTP encryption with DTLS key exchange. `zrtp` - use SRTP encryption with ZRTP key exchange. |
| ice\_mode | `string` | No | No | ICE (Interactive Connectivity Establishment) for calls from the trunk: not used, accepted when the trunk offers it, or initiated by DIDWW. Possible values: `disabled`, `accept`, `initiate`. Defaults to `accept`. |
| rtcp\_mux\_mode | `string` | No | No | RTP and RTCP multiplexed on one port: not used, accepted when the trunk offers it, or initiated by DIDWW. Possible values: `disabled`, `accept`, `initiate`. Defaults to `accept`. |
| rtcp\_feedback\_mode | `string` | No | No | RTCP feedback (AVPF): not used, accepted when the trunk offers it, or initiated by DIDWW. Possible values: `disabled`, `accept`, `initiate`. Defaults to `accept`. With `disabled`, a call whose SDP offer uses a feedback profile (`RTP/AVPF` or `UDP/TLS/RTP/SAVPF`) is rejected with SIP `500 No suitable media`. WebRTC clients always offer such a profile, so use `accept` or `initiate` for them. |
| codecs | Array of `strings` | No | No | Codecs offered on calls from the trunk, in priority order: the first has the highest priority. Send at least one value, without repeats. Possible values: `telephone_event`, `g723`, `g729`, `pcmu`, `pcma`, `gsm`, `g722`, `opus`, `amr`, `amr_wb`. Defaults to `pcma`, `pcmu`, `telephone_event`. |
| callback\_url | `string` | Yes | No | Can be `null` or a valid HTTP(S) URL. |
| force\_symmetric\_rtp | `boolean` | No | No | Enables symmetric RTP / COMEDIA mode. |
| rtp\_ping | `boolean` | No | No | Enables RTP ping after the call is connected. |
| rtp\_timeout | `integer` | No | No | Disconnects the call if RTP packets do not arrive within the specified time. Supported values are from 30 to 600 seconds. |

See [Outbound Trunk callback details](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/callbacks-details.html#callbacks-voice-out-trunk-v35) for
information about `callback_url` and the JSON callback payload.

### Request Body Object Relationships

| Title | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default\_did | [DID Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/did-object.html#did-object-v35) | The DID used as the caller ID. Required while `on_cli_mismatch_action` is `replace_cli`, and rejected otherwise. Only accepted on accounts with the `replace_cli` feature. |
| dids | [DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html#dids-v35) | The DID numbers explicitly allowed as CLI when `allow_any_did_as_cli` is `false`. DIDs must support `voice_out` feature to be selected. A DID that is awaiting registration (`awaiting_registration` is `true`) cannot be used as an allowed CLI: the request returns `422 Unprocessable Entity` with one error per such DID. |
| emergency\_dids | [DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html#dids-v35) | The DID numbers explicitly enabled for emergency calling when `emergency_enable_all` is `false`. DIDs must support `voice_out` and `emergency` features and have `emergency_enabled = true` to be selected. |

### Authentication Method

The outbound trunk authentication is configured through the `authentication_method` attribute.

Supported authentication method types:

- `credentials_and_ip` - uses SIP credentials together with allowed IP addresses.
- `twilio` - uses a Twilio Account SID for authentication.
- `ip_only` is returned by `GET` endpoints but is not supported in `POST` requests.

#### Authentication Method Attributes by Type

**credentials\_and\_ip**

| Name | Type | Nullable | Is Required? | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| allowed\_sip\_ips | Array of `strings` | No | Yes | The allowed originating SIP IPs. |
| tech\_prefix | `string` | Yes | No | Prefix stripped from the dialled number before routing. The maximum length is 8 characters and only digits and `#` are supported. |

**twilio**

| Name | Type | Nullable | Is Required? | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| twilio\_account\_sid | `string` | No | Yes | The Twilio Account SID. It is a 34-character identifier of the Twilio account. |

## Other Responses

| Code | Success | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 422 | No | [Validation Error Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/specification/errors/index.html#api-validation-error-object) |
| 400 | No | [Bad Request](https://doc.didww.com/api3/specification/errors/index.html#api-bad-request). Also returned with the title `Quota limit reached` when the account has reached its limit of outbound trunks. |
| 401 | No | [Unauthorized](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/authentication.html#authentication-v35) |
| 403 | No | The Outbound API is not enabled for the account. Also returned when the access token carries the `read` scope, which does not cover this method (title `Insufficient scope`, `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope"`). See [Scopes](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/authentication.html#authentication-scopes-v35). |
| 429 | No | The request budget of the account for the current window is spent (`too_many_requests`). `Retry-After` gives the number of seconds to wait. |

request.description:
Updates an outbound trunk.

In version `2026-11-19`, customers with the Outbound API enabled can update outbound trunks even if the Outbound feature is not enabled on the account. Without the Outbound API, the request returns `403 Forbidden`.

## Request

HTTP Method: `PATCH`

URI Path: `/v3/voice_out_trunks/{id}`

### URI Query Parameters

| Name | Type | Is Required? | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id | `string` | Yes | Unique identifier of the outbound trunk. |

### Data Attributes

| Name | Type | Nullable | Is Required? | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| name | `string` | No | No | The outbound trunk name. |
| external\_reference\_id | `string` | Yes | No | Optional identifier for the outbound trunk in the customer's external system. Maximum length is 100 characters. |
| allowed\_rtp\_ips | Array of `strings` | Yes | No | Allowed RTP IP addresses for media traffic. Null means no restriction. An empty list is rejected. `0.0.0.0/0` and `::/0` are rejected. |
| authentication\_method | `object` | No | No | Authentication method object. Supported PATCH target types are `credentials_and_ip` and `twilio`. `ip_only` may be returned by `GET` endpoints but cannot be set through `PATCH`. |
| on\_cli\_mismatch\_action | `string` | No | No | Possible values: `send_original_cli` - pass the original `From` header value from your system to the destination without modification. `reject_call` - reject the call if the `From` header value does not match any DID allowed on the trunk. `replace_cli` - replace the CLI with one of the DIDs allowed on the trunk. `randomize_cli` - replace the CLI with a random DID allowed on the trunk. An action the account does not have the feature for is rejected. |
| capacity\_limit | `integer` | Yes | No | The capacity limit of the outbound trunk. Allowed values from 1 to 32767. |
| allow\_any\_did\_as\_cli | `boolean` | No | No | When set to `true`, all eligible DIDs can be used as CLI and the `dids` relationship must not contain explicit DIDs. |
| status | `string` | No | No | Possible values: `active` - the trunk can be used for outbound traffic. `blocked` - outbound traffic on the trunk is blocked. |
| threshold\_amount | `string` | No | No | The outbound trunk 24-hour threshold limit. The accepted range depends on the account. |
| default\_dst\_action | `string` | No | No | Possible values: `allow_all` - allow calls to all destinations except the prefixes listed in `dst_prefixes`. `reject_all` - reject calls to all destinations except the prefixes listed in `dst_prefixes`. |
| dst\_prefixes | Array of `strings` | No | No | The destination prefixes allowed or rejected based on `default_dst_action`. Each prefix is digits only, without a leading `+` or separators; any other value returns `422 Unprocessable Entity`. Repeated prefixes are stored once. |
| emergency\_enable\_all | `boolean` | No | No | Allows all eligible DIDs to be used for emergency calling on the trunk. |
| media\_encryption\_mode | `string` | No | No | Media encryption mode. Possible values: `disabled` - media encryption is turned off. `srtp_sdes` - use SRTP encryption with SDES key exchange. `srtp_dtls` - use SRTP encryption with DTLS key exchange. `zrtp` - use SRTP encryption with ZRTP key exchange. |
| ice\_mode | `string` | No | No | ICE (Interactive Connectivity Establishment) for calls from the trunk: not used, accepted when the trunk offers it, or initiated by DIDWW. Possible values: `disabled`, `accept`, `initiate`. |
| rtcp\_mux\_mode | `string` | No | No | RTP and RTCP multiplexed on one port: not used, accepted when the trunk offers it, or initiated by DIDWW. Possible values: `disabled`, `accept`, `initiate`. |
| rtcp\_feedback\_mode | `string` | No | No | RTCP feedback (AVPF): not used, accepted when the trunk offers it, or initiated by DIDWW. Possible values: `disabled`, `accept`, `initiate`. With `disabled`, a call whose SDP offer uses a feedback profile (`RTP/AVPF` or `UDP/TLS/RTP/SAVPF`) is rejected with SIP `500 No suitable media`. WebRTC clients always offer such a profile, so use `accept` or `initiate` for them. |
| codecs | Array of `strings` | No | No | Codecs offered on calls from the trunk, in priority order: the first has the highest priority. Send at least one value, without repeats. Possible values: `telephone_event`, `g723`, `g729`, `pcmu`, `pcma`, `gsm`, `g722`, `opus`, `amr`, `amr_wb`. |
| callback\_url | `string` | Yes | No | Can be `null` or a valid HTTP(S) URL. |
| force\_symmetric\_rtp | `boolean` | No | No | Enables symmetric RTP / COMEDIA mode. |
| rtp\_ping | `boolean` | No | No | Enables RTP ping after the call is connected. |
| rtp\_timeout | `integer` | No | No | Disconnects the call if RTP packets do not arrive within the specified time. Supported values are from 30 to 600 seconds. |

See [Outbound Trunk callback details](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/callbacks-details.html#callbacks-voice-out-trunk-v35) for
information about `callback_url` and the JSON callback payload.

### Request Body Object Relationships

| Title | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default\_did | [DID Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/did-object.html#did-object-v35) | The DID used as the caller ID. Required while `on_cli_mismatch_action` is `replace_cli`, and rejected otherwise. Only accepted on accounts with the `replace_cli` feature. Send `data: null` to clear it. |
| dids | [DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html#dids-v35) | The DID numbers explicitly allowed as CLI when `allow_any_did_as_cli` is `false`. A DID that is awaiting registration (`awaiting_registration` is `true`) cannot be used as an allowed CLI: the request returns `422 Unprocessable Entity` with one error per such DID. |
| emergency\_dids | [DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html#dids-v35) | The DID numbers explicitly enabled for emergency calling when `emergency_enable_all` is `false`. |

### Authentication Method

Supported authentication method types:

- `credentials_and_ip` - uses SIP credentials together with allowed IP addresses.
- `twilio` - uses a Twilio Account SID for authentication.
- `ip_only` - may be returned by `GET` endpoints, but `PATCH` does not allow changing `authentication_method.type` to `ip_only`.

> **Note**

**twilio**

| Name | Type | Nullable | Is Required? | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| twilio\_account\_sid | `string` | No | Yes | The Twilio Account SID. It is a 34-character identifier of the Twilio account. |

item.description:
Use the Outbound Trunks resource to create, retrieve, update, and delete SIP trunks used
for outbound calling through DIDWW.

An Outbound Trunk defines how outbound calls are authenticated and controlled. Its
configuration can specify allowed SIP and RTP addresses, CLI policies, destination-prefix
rules, simultaneous-call and 24-hour spending limits, media settings, status, callbacks,
and DIDs allowed for regular or emergency calling.

Outbound Trunks support `credentials_and_ip`, `ip_only`, and `twilio` authentication
when retrieved. New or updated trunks can use `credentials_and_ip` or `twilio`;
`ip_only` cannot be selected through `POST` or `PATCH`.

> **Note**
>
> The Outbound feature and the Outbound API are not enabled by default. In version
> `2026-11-19`, customers with the Outbound API enabled can use every endpoint on this
> page even when the Outbound feature is not enabled. Without the Outbound API, each of
> them returns `403 Forbidden`. For more information, contact DIDWW Sales.

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retrieve all Outbound Trunks | `GET` | `/v3/voice_out_trunks` |
| Retrieve Outbound Trunk | `GET` | `/v3/voice_out_trunks/{id}` |
| Create Outbound Trunk | `POST` | `/v3/voice_out_trunks` |
| Update Outbound Trunk | `PATCH` | `/v3/voice_out_trunks/{id}` |
| Delete Outbound Trunk | `DELETE` | `/v3/voice_out_trunks/{id}` |
| Regenerate Outbound Trunk credentials | `POST` | `/v3/voice_out_trunk_regenerate_credentials` |

## Retrieve all Outbound Trunks

Retrieves all Outbound Trunks configured for the account.

Use this endpoint to filter trunks by ID, name, external reference ID, authentication type,
CLI policy, status, threshold state, destination policy, media encryption, or default
caller ID. Related regular and emergency DIDs can be included in the response.

See [Retrieve All Outbound Trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/get-voice-out-trunks.html).

```
GET /v3/voice_out_trunks
```

## Retrieve Outbound Trunk

Retrieves a specific Outbound Trunk by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint to inspect the trunk's authentication, call policies, limits, media
configuration, status, and related DIDs.

See [Retrieve Outbound Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/get-voice-out-trunk.html).

```
GET /v3/voice_out_trunks/{id}
```

## Create Outbound Trunk

Creates an Outbound Trunk using `credentials_and_ip` or `twilio` authentication.

Use this endpoint to configure authentication, allowed network addresses, CLI handling,
destination rules, limits, media behavior, callbacks, and DIDs allowed for regular or
emergency calling. The `ip_only` authentication type cannot be used when creating a
trunk. A DID that is awaiting registration cannot be used as an allowed CLI in the `dids`
relationship.

See [Create Outbound Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/create-voice-out-trunk.html).

```
POST /v3/voice_out_trunks
```

## Update Outbound Trunk

Updates a specific Outbound Trunk.

Use this endpoint to change the trunk's configuration, authentication type, call policies,
limits, status, callbacks, or related DIDs. When the authentication type is changed, the
previous authentication attributes are cleared. The authentication type cannot be changed
to `ip_only`. A DID that is awaiting registration cannot be assigned as an allowed CLI.

See [Update Outbound Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/update-voice-out-trunk.html).

```
PATCH /v3/voice_out_trunks/{id}
```

## Delete Outbound Trunk

Permanently deletes a specific Outbound Trunk. A deleted trunk cannot be retrieved.

See [Delete Outbound Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/delete-voice-out-trunk.html).

```
DELETE /v3/voice_out_trunks/{id}
```

## Regenerate Outbound Trunk credentials

Regenerates the username and password for an Outbound Trunk that uses
`credentials_and_ip` authentication.

This endpoint does not apply to trunks that use `ip_only` or `twilio` authentication.

See [Regenerate Outbound Trunk Credentials](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/voice-out-trunk-regenerate-credentials.html).

```
POST /v3/voice_out_trunk_regenerate_credentials
```

## Data reference

See [Outbound Trunk Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/voice-out-trunk-object.html) for the complete trunk attributes,
authentication objects, and DID relationships.

## Common Outbound Trunk use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Configure SIP authentication | Authenticate calls using SIP credentials with allowed IP addresses or a Twilio Account SID. |
| Restrict originating addresses | Define the SIP and RTP IP addresses allowed to send signaling and media traffic. |
| Control outbound CLI | Assign eligible DIDs and define how calls are handled when the presented CLI does not match the allowed DID list. DIDs awaiting registration cannot be assigned. |
| Control called destinations | Allow or reject destinations according to the default action and configured prefix exceptions. |
| Manage trunk availability | Set the trunk status to `active` or `blocked`. |
| Apply usage limits | Configure a simultaneous-call limit and a 24-hour threshold amount. |
| Configure media handling | Set allowed RTP addresses, media encryption, symmetric RTP, RTP ping, and timeout behavior. |
| Configure Emergency Calling | Allow all eligible DIDs or select specific emergency-enabled DIDs for Emergency Calling through the trunk. |
| Regenerate credentials | Replace the username and password for a `credentials_and_ip` trunk. |

## Related resources

Use Outbound Trunks together with DIDs and Emergency Calling resources to configure
outgoing call origination.

| Resource | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html) | Eligible DID phone numbers that can be used as CLI on an Outbound Trunk. |
| [Emergency Calling Services](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-calling-services/index.html) | Emergency Calling services associated with eligible DIDs. |
| [Inbound Trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-in-trunks/index.html) | Routing destinations used for incoming rather than outgoing calls. |

request.description:
Creates an SMS trunk.

The `configuration` object is required. Its `type` decides which configuration
attributes the trunk takes and whether the trunk handles inbound messages, outbound
messages, or both. The type cannot be changed after the trunk is created.

| blocked | `boolean` | No | No | When `true`, the trunk does not handle messages. Default value is `false`. |
| priority | `integer` | Yes | No | Routing priority of the trunk within its SMS trunk group. The range is 0-32767. On `sms_to_email`, `http_in`, `smpp_esme`, and `smpp_smsc` trunks, the value `100` is used when `priority` is omitted or `null`. On `http_out` trunks, `priority` must be omitted or `null`. |

| configuration | `object` | No | Yes | Trunk configuration object with `type` and `attributes`. `type` is one of `sms_to_email`, `http_in`, `http_out`, `smpp_esme`, `smpp_smsc`. Send the configuration attributes in `configuration.attributes`. Read-only attributes

With `html_multipart` or `html_url_encoded`, an object of string names and string values. With `raw`, a string. Required when `http_method` is `post` or `put`. item.description:
> **Note**
>
> To configure SMS trunks in the User Panel, see [SMS Trunks](https://doc.didww.com/sms/sms-trunks/index.html#userpanel-sms).
> For the message formats and protocols used by the trunks, see the
> [SMS HTTP specification](https://doc.didww.com/sms/sms-trunks/technical-data/http-specification.html#user-panel-sms-http-specification) and the
> [SMPP specification](https://doc.didww.com/sms/sms-trunks/technical-data/smpp-specification.html#service-smpp-specification).

Use the SMS Trunks resource to create, retrieve, update, and delete SMS trunks, and to
regenerate the credentials DIDWW generates for some trunk types.

An SMS trunk defines how DIDWW delivers the inbound SMS sent to your DIDs, how your
application submits outbound SMS to DIDWW, or both. The `configuration` attribute selects
the trunk type, and the type decides which configuration attributes the trunk takes and
which directions it handles:

| Configuration type | Direction | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sms_to_email` | Inbound | DIDWW forwards inbound SMS as email. |
| `http_in` | Inbound | DIDWW delivers inbound SMS as an HTTP request to your endpoint. |
| `http_out` | Outbound | Your application submits outbound SMS to DIDWW over HTTP. |
| `smpp_esme` | Inbound and outbound | Your application connects to DIDWW as an SMPP ESME. |
| `smpp_smsc` | Inbound and outbound | DIDWW connects to your SMSC as an SMPP client. |

SMS trunks are available starting from version `2026-11-19`.

## Requirements and behavior

When creating or updating an SMS trunk:

- Provide a `name` and a `configuration` object when creating the trunk. The name must
  be unique among the SMS trunks and SMS trunk groups of the account.
- The configuration type cannot be changed after the trunk is created. On update, the
  `configuration.type` must match the trunk's type; the configuration attributes you send
  are written and the others keep their stored values.
- Each configuration type requires its own set of attributes on creation. See
  [Create SMS Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/create-sms-trunk.html).
- `priority` and the `sms_trunk_group` relationship apply only to the trunk types that
  can join an [SMS Trunk Group](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunk-groups/index.html): `sms_to_email`,
  `http_in`, `smpp_esme`, and `smpp_smsc`. On these types `priority` defaults to
  `100`. On `http_out` trunks `priority` must stay `null` and a group cannot be
  assigned.
- `allow_any_did_as_source` can be enabled only on the trunk types that send messages:
  `http_out`, `smpp_esme`, and `smpp_smsc`. Enabling it removes all
  `outgoing_dids`, which must stay empty while it is `true`.
- `outgoing_dids` accepts only DIDs of your account that support the `p2p` feature, and
  rejects DIDs awaiting registration.
- `incoming_dids` is read-only. To route inbound SMS of a DID to a trunk, update the
  `sms_trunk` relationship of the [DID](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html). To route it to a group, use
  the DID `sms_trunk_group` relationship instead.
- `smpp_esme` and `http_out` trunks receive credentials generated by DIDWW. They are
  returned as read-only configuration attributes and can be replaced with
  [Regenerate SMS Trunk Credentials](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/sms-trunk-regenerate-credentials.html).
- The number of SMS trunks and SMS trunk groups an account can create is limited. When the
  limit is reached, a create request returns `400 Bad Request` with the title
  `Quota limit reached`. Contact DIDWW Support to request a higher limit.
- A trunk cannot be deleted while any DID is routed to it for inbound SMS. Sender ID
  verifications that use a deleted trunk are left without one, and their outbound messages
  stop until another trunk is assigned.
- `sender_id_verifications` is read-only. To route a verification through a trunk, update
  the `sms_trunk` relationship of the
  [Sender ID Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sender-id-verifications/index.html).

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retrieve all SMS Trunks | `GET` | `/v3/sms_trunks` |
| Retrieve SMS Trunk | `GET` | `/v3/sms_trunks/{id}` |
| Create SMS Trunk | `POST` | `/v3/sms_trunks` |
| Update SMS Trunk | `PATCH` | `/v3/sms_trunks/{id}` |
| Delete SMS Trunk | `DELETE` | `/v3/sms_trunks/{id}` |
| Regenerate SMS Trunk credentials | `POST` | `/v3/sms_trunk_regenerate_credentials` |

## Retrieve all SMS Trunks

Retrieves all SMS trunks configured for the account.

Use this endpoint to filter trunks by name, external reference ID, ID, or configuration
type. Outgoing DIDs, incoming DIDs, the SMS trunk group, and Sender ID verifications can be
included in the response.

See [Retrieve All SMS Trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/get-sms-trunks.html).

```
GET /v3/sms_trunks
```

## Retrieve SMS Trunk

Retrieves a specific SMS trunk by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint to inspect the trunk configuration, including the generated credentials
of `smpp_esme` and `http_out` trunks, and the URL of the endpoint to which `http_out`
trunks submit outbound SMS (`meta.host`).

See [Retrieve SMS Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/get-sms-trunk.html).

```
GET /v3/sms_trunks/{id}
```

## Create SMS Trunk

Creates an SMS trunk of one of the five configuration types.

Provide a unique name and the configuration, and optionally set the external reference ID,
status, priority, source-address settings, outgoing DIDs, and the SMS trunk group.

See [Create SMS Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/create-sms-trunk.html).

```
POST /v3/sms_trunks
```

## Update SMS Trunk

Updates a specific SMS trunk.

Use this endpoint to change the trunk name, external reference ID, status, priority,
source-address settings, configuration attributes, outgoing DIDs, or SMS trunk group. The
configuration type cannot be changed.

See [Update SMS Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/update-sms-trunk.html).

```
PATCH /v3/sms_trunks/{id}
```

## Delete SMS Trunk

Permanently deletes a specific SMS trunk. The request is rejected while any DID is routed
to the trunk for inbound SMS; route those DIDs elsewhere first. Sender ID verifications that
use the trunk are left without one, and their outbound messages stop until another trunk is
assigned.

See [Delete SMS Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/delete-sms-trunk.html).

```
DELETE /v3/sms_trunks/{id}
```

## Regenerate SMS Trunk credentials

Replaces the generated credentials of an `smpp_esme` trunk (`system_id` and
`password`) or an `http_out` trunk (`auth_name` and `auth_password`). The response
contains only the trunk ID; retrieve the trunk to read the new credentials.

See [Regenerate SMS Trunk Credentials](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/sms-trunk-regenerate-credentials.html).

```
POST /v3/sms_trunk_regenerate_credentials
```

## Data reference

See [SMS Trunk Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/sms-trunk-object.html) for the complete trunk attributes, the
configuration attributes of each trunk type, relationships, and metadata.

## Common SMS Trunk use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Receive inbound SMS by email | Create an `sms_to_email` trunk and route DIDs to it. |
| Receive inbound SMS on a web endpoint | Create an `http_in` trunk with the URL, method, and request template DIDWW uses to deliver each message. |
| Send outbound SMS over HTTP | Create an `http_out` trunk, read its generated credentials and the endpoint URL in `meta.host`, and submit messages as described in the [SMS OUT HTTP specification](https://doc.didww.com/sms/outbound-sms-api/index.html#sms-out-specification). |
| Exchange SMS over SMPP | Create an `smpp_esme` trunk to bind to DIDWW, or an `smpp_smsc` trunk to let DIDWW bind to your SMSC. |
| Control source addresses | Assign `outgoing_dids` or enable `allow_any_did_as_source` on a trunk that sends messages. |
| Configure failover for inbound SMS | Add trunks to an [SMS Trunk Group](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunk-groups/index.html) and set their `priority`. |
| Rotate credentials | Regenerate the credentials of an `smpp_esme` or `http_out` trunk. |
| Pause a trunk | Set `blocked` to `true` to stop the trunk from handling messages. |

item.description:
> **Note**
>
> To configure SMS trunk groups in the User Panel, see
> [SMS Trunk Groups](https://doc.didww.com/sms/sms-trunks/trunk-groups/sms-trunk-groups.html#user-panel-sms-trunk-group).

Use the SMS Trunk Groups resource to create, retrieve, update, and delete groups of SMS
trunks used for inbound SMS routing.

An SMS Trunk Group organizes several inbound-capable [SMS Trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/index.html)
into one routing destination that can be assigned to DIDs. The `priority` of each member
trunk defines the order in which DIDWW attempts delivery: inbound SMS are offered to the
trunk with the higher `priority` value first, which provides failover between the trunks
of the group.

Each group has a unique name and an optional external reference ID. Group records also
provide their member trunks, the DIDs routed to the group, and the number of trunks in the
group.

SMS trunk groups are available starting from version `2026-11-19`.

## Requirements and behavior

When creating, updating, or deleting an SMS Trunk Group:

- Provide a `name` when creating the group. The name must be unique among the SMS trunks
  and SMS trunk groups of the account.
- Sending the `sms_trunks` relationship replaces the whole membership of the group with
  the listed trunks. Send an empty list to remove all trunks.
- Only SMS trunks of your account that handle inbound messages can be members:
  `sms_to_email`, `http_in`, `smpp_esme`, and `smpp_smsc`. `http_out` trunks and
  other groups cannot be added, and the list must not contain duplicates.
- A trunk can also join or leave a group through the `sms_trunk_group` relationship of the
  [SMS Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/index.html). The member order is set with the trunk's
  `priority`.
- `incoming_dids` is read-only. To route inbound SMS of a DID to a group, update the
  `sms_trunk_group` relationship of the [DID](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html).
- SMS trunk groups count toward the same account limit as SMS trunks. When the limit is
  reached, a create request returns `400 Bad Request` with the title
  `Quota limit reached`.
- Deleting a group also deletes every trunk in the group; the member trunks are not kept as
  standalone trunks. The request is rejected while any DID is routed to the group or to any
  of its trunks.

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retrieve all SMS Trunk Groups | `GET` | `/v3/sms_trunk_groups` |
| Retrieve SMS Trunk Group | `GET` | `/v3/sms_trunk_groups/{id}` |
| Create SMS Trunk Group | `POST` | `/v3/sms_trunk_groups` |
| Update SMS Trunk Group | `PATCH` | `/v3/sms_trunk_groups/{id}` |
| Delete SMS Trunk Group | `DELETE` | `/v3/sms_trunk_groups/{id}` |

## Retrieve all SMS Trunk Groups

Retrieves all SMS Trunk Groups configured for the account.

Use this endpoint to filter groups by name, external reference ID, or ID, and sort results
by name, external reference ID, creation time, or update time. Member trunks and incoming
DIDs can be included in the response.

See [Retrieve All SMS Trunk Groups](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunk-groups/get-sms-trunk-groups.html).

```
GET /v3/sms_trunk_groups
```

## Retrieve SMS Trunk Group

Retrieves a specific SMS Trunk Group by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint to inspect the group settings, member-trunk count, member trunks, and the
DIDs routed to the group.

See [Retrieve SMS Trunk Group](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunk-groups/get-sms-trunk-group.html).

```
GET /v3/sms_trunk_groups/{id}
```

## Create SMS Trunk Group

Creates an SMS Trunk Group.

Provide a unique group name and optionally set an external reference ID and the SMS trunks
that should belong to the group.

See [Create SMS Trunk Group](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunk-groups/create-sms-trunk-group.html).

```
POST /v3/sms_trunk_groups
```

## Update SMS Trunk Group

Updates a specific SMS Trunk Group.

Use this endpoint to change the group name, external reference ID, or member trunks.
Sending `sms_trunks` replaces the whole membership.

See [Update SMS Trunk Group](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunk-groups/update-sms-trunk-group.html).

```
PATCH /v3/sms_trunk_groups/{id}
```

## Delete SMS Trunk Group

Deletes a specific SMS Trunk Group together with all of its member trunks. The request is
rejected while any DID is routed to the group or to any of its trunks.

See [Delete SMS Trunk Group](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunk-groups/delete-sms-trunk-group.html).

```
DELETE /v3/sms_trunk_groups/{id}
```

## Data reference

See [SMS Trunk Group Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunk-groups/sms-trunk-group-object.html) for the complete group
attribute, relationship, and metadata definitions.

## Common SMS Trunk Group use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Configure failover for inbound SMS | Combine several inbound-capable trunks and set their `priority` values to control the delivery order. |
| Route DIDs to one destination | Assign the group to DIDs through the DID `sms_trunk_group` relationship. |
| Manage group membership | Replace the member trunks when creating or updating the group. |
| Inspect member trunks | Include the `sms_trunks` relationship and review the returned `sms_trunks_count` metadata. |
| Synchronize external systems | Store an `external_reference_id` for the corresponding record in another system. |

## Related resources

Use SMS Trunk Groups together with SMS Trunks and DIDs to configure inbound SMS delivery.

| Resource | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [SMS Trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/index.html) | Inbound SMS destinations that can be members of a group. |
| [DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html) | DID phone numbers that can use an SMS Trunk Group for inbound SMS routing. |

item.description:
> **Note**
>
> To learn how Sender ID verification works, see
> [Sender ID Verifications](https://doc.didww.com/sms/sender-id-verifications/index.html#sender-id-verifications).

Use the Sender ID Verifications resource to retrieve the Sender ID verifications of your
account, and to change their name or SMS trunk.

A Sender ID verification is a verification request for a sender identity used for outbound
messages. The `sender_type` attribute shows the kind of sender it covers: `alphanumeric`,
`carrier`, `long_code`, `short_code`, or `toll_free`. The `sender_ids` attribute
lists the covered Sender IDs. For `long_code` and `toll_free` verifications, they are the
numbers of the account's `dids`.

Each verification provides its reference, status, renewal date, charges, and the
[SMS Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/index.html) its outbound messages are routed through.

Sender ID verifications are available starting from version `2026-11-19`.

## Requirements and behavior

When updating a Sender ID verification:

- Only `name` and the `sms_trunk` relationship can be changed.
- `sms_trunk` accepts only `http_out`, `smpp_smsc`, and `smpp_esme` trunks.
- Send `sms_trunk` with `data: null` to unassign the trunk. Outbound messages then stop
  until a trunk is assigned again.
- The request is rejected with `422` when another verification already uses a Sender ID of
  this one on the SMS trunk.
- A `closed` verification cannot be updated. The request is rejected with `422`.

Deleting an SMS trunk leaves the verifications that use it without a trunk, and their outbound
messages stop until another trunk is assigned.

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retrieve all Sender ID Verifications | `GET` | `/v3/sender_id_verifications` |
| Retrieve Sender ID Verification | `GET` | `/v3/sender_id_verifications/{id}` |
| Update Sender ID Verification | `PATCH` | `/v3/sender_id_verifications/{id}` |

## Retrieve all Sender ID Verifications

Retrieves all Sender ID verifications of the account.

Use this endpoint to filter verifications by ID, name, reference, status, sender type, or SMS
trunk, and sort results by name, status, creation time, or renewal date. The SMS trunk,
countries, DIDs, order, identity, and address can be included in the response.

See [Retrieve All Sender ID Verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sender-id-verifications/get-sender-id-verifications.html).

```
GET /v3/sender_id_verifications
```

## Retrieve Sender ID Verification

Retrieves a specific Sender ID verification by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint to inspect the status of the verification, the reasons the last submission
was rejected, its renewal date, and its charges.

See [Retrieve Sender ID Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sender-id-verifications/get-sender-id-verification.html).

```
GET /v3/sender_id_verifications/{id}
```

## Update Sender ID Verification

Updates a specific Sender ID verification.

Use this endpoint to change the name of the verification, or the SMS trunk its outbound
messages are routed through.

See [Update Sender ID Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sender-id-verifications/update-sender-id-verification.html).

```
PATCH /v3/sender_id_verifications/{id}
```

## Data reference

See [Sender ID Verification Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sender-id-verifications/sender-id-verification-object.html) for the complete
attribute, relationship, and metadata definitions.

## Common Sender ID Verification use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Track verification status | Filter by `status`, and review `reject_reasons` and `reject_comment` of a verification in `changes_required`. |
| Route outbound messages | Assign an `http_out`, `smpp_smsc`, or `smpp_esme` trunk through the `sms_trunk` relationship. |
| Find the verifications of a trunk | Filter by `sms_trunk.id`, or include `sender_id_verifications` when retrieving the [SMS Trunk](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/index.html). |
| Plan renewals | Sort by `renew_date` and review the charges in `meta`. |
| Limit an outbound SMS export | Use the verification ID in the `sender_id_verification.id` filter of an [Export](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/index.html). |

## Related resources

Use Sender ID Verifications together with SMS Trunks, DIDs, and Exports.

| Resource | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [SMS Trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/index.html) | The trunks outbound messages are routed through. |
| [DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html) | DID phone numbers related to a verification. |
| [Exports](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/index.html) | Exports of outbound SMS records, which can be limited by Sender ID verification. |

item.description:
> **Note**
>
> For an introduction to capacity options, see [Capacity](https://doc.didww.com/phone-numbers/capacity/index.html#flexible-capacity).

Use the Capacity Pools resource to retrieve and manage channels used by inbound voice
services.

A Capacity Pool contains channels that can be assigned directly to DID phone numbers or
allocated through [Shared Capacity Groups](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/shared-capacity-group/index.html). Each pool
provides its total and assigned channel counts, renewal date, minimum limits, ordering
requirements, and pricing.

Capacity Pools are associated with supported countries, Shared Capacity Groups, and
quantity-based pricing tiers. Use Orders to add channels to a pool, and use the Capacity
Pools resource to remove channels that are not assigned.

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retrieve all Capacity Pools | `GET` | `/v3/capacity_pools` |
| Retrieve Capacity Pool | `GET` | `/v3/capacity_pools/{id}` |
| Update Capacity Pool | `PATCH` | `/v3/capacity_pools/{id}` |

## Retrieve all Capacity Pools

Retrieves all Capacity Pools available for the account.

Use this endpoint to filter pools by ID, name, supported country, or the availability of
unassigned channels. Results can be sorted by channel counts, renewal date, ordering
limits, or pricing. Related countries, Shared Capacity Groups, and quantity-based pricing
tiers can be included in the response.

See [Retrieve All Capacity Pools](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/capacity-pool/get-capacity-pools.html).

```
GET /v3/capacity_pools
```

## Retrieve Capacity Pool

Retrieves a specific Capacity Pool by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint to inspect its channel allocation, renewal date, ordering limits,
pricing, supported countries, Shared Capacity Groups, and quantity-based pricing tiers.

See [Retrieve Capacity Pool](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/capacity-pool/get-capacity-pool.html).

```
GET /v3/capacity_pools/{id}
```

## Update Capacity Pool

Updates the total number of channels in a specific Capacity Pool.

Use this endpoint to remove unassigned channels by reducing `total_channels_count`.
Channels that are already assigned to DIDs or Shared Capacity Groups cannot be removed
through this operation.

See [Update Capacity Pool](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/capacity-pool/update-capacity-pool.html).

```
PATCH /v3/capacity_pools/{id}
```

## Data reference

See [Capacity Pool Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/capacity-pool/capacity-pool-object.html) for the complete pool attribute and
relationship definitions.

## Common Capacity Pool use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Review inbound capacity | Compare the total and assigned channel counts for each Capacity Pool. |
| Find unassigned channels | Filter for Capacity Pools that currently have channels available for assignment. |
| Find capacity by country | Filter Capacity Pools by the countries in which their channels can be used. |
| Review capacity pricing | Inspect setup, monthly, metered, and quantity-based pricing information. |
| Check ordering requirements | Review the minimum number of channels that can be purchased per Order. |
| Add channels | Create an Order using the Capacity Pool ID and the required quantity. |
| Remove unassigned channels | Reduce `total_channels_count` without affecting channels assigned to DIDs or Shared Capacity Groups. |
| Plan renewals | Use the pool renewal date to plan capacity and billing changes. |

## Related resources

Use Capacity Pools together with Orders, DIDs, and Shared Capacity Groups to manage
inbound voice capacity.

| Resource | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [Orders](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/order/index.html) | Orders used to add channels to a Capacity Pool. |
| [DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html) | DID phone numbers to which dedicated channels can be assigned. |
| [Shared Capacity Groups](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/shared-capacity-group/index.html) | Groups through which channels from a Capacity Pool are shared among DIDs. |
| [Countries](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/countries/index.html) | Countries supported by a Capacity Pool. |
| [Inbound Trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-in-trunks/index.html) | Routing destinations used by inbound voice services. |
| [Common Definitions](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/common-definitions/index.html) | Shared embedded objects such as the Quantity Based Price Object. |

item.description:
> **Note**
>
> For an introduction to inbound call capacity, see [Capacity](https://doc.didww.com/phone-numbers/capacity/index.html#flexible-capacity)
> and [Capacity groups](https://doc.didww.com/phone-numbers/capacity/capacity-groups.html#capacity-groups).

Use the Shared Capacity Groups resource to create, retrieve, update, and delete groups that
provide shared or metered channels to multiple DID phone numbers.

A Shared Capacity Group belongs to a [Capacity Pool](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/capacity-pool/index.html). DID
numbers assigned to the group can use its shared flat-rate channels, metered pay-per-minute
channels, or both. Dedicated channels are assigned directly to individual DIDs and do not
use a Shared Capacity Group.

When both shared and metered channels are configured, shared channels are used first and
metered channels provide overflow after the shared channels are unavailable. Capacity
applies to inbound calls only.

## Requirements and behavior

When creating or updating a Shared Capacity Group:

- Select the Capacity Pool to which the group belongs.
- Provide a unique group name.
- Assign at least one shared or metered channel.
- Do not assign more shared channels than the unassigned channels available in the selected
  Capacity Pool.
- Assign no more than 1,000 metered channels.
- Assign only DIDs that support additional capacity.

The number of Shared Capacity Groups an account can create is limited. When the limit is
reached, a create request returns `400 Bad Request` with the title `Quota limit reached`.

DIDs must be assigned to the group before they can use its shared or metered channels.
Removing a DID from the group stops that DID from using those channels. A group cannot be
deleted while any DID is assigned to it.

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retrieve all Shared Capacity Groups | `GET` | `/v3/shared_capacity_groups` |
| Retrieve Shared Capacity Group | `GET` | `/v3/shared_capacity_groups/{id}` |
| Create Shared Capacity Group | `POST` | `/v3/shared_capacity_groups` |
| Update Shared Capacity Group | `PATCH` | `/v3/shared_capacity_groups/{id}` |
| Delete Shared Capacity Group | `DELETE` | `/v3/shared_capacity_groups/{id}` |

## Retrieve all Shared Capacity Groups

Retrieves all Shared Capacity Groups configured for the account.

Use this endpoint to filter groups by name, external reference ID, or Capacity Pool ID.
Related DIDs and Capacity Pool data can be included in the response.

See [Retrieve All Shared Capacity Groups](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/shared-capacity-group/get-shared-capacity-groups.html).

```
GET /v3/shared_capacity_groups
```

## Retrieve Shared Capacity Group

Retrieves a specific Shared Capacity Group by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint to inspect the shared and metered channel counts, group details, assigned
DIDs, and related Capacity Pool.

See [Retrieve Shared Capacity Group](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/shared-capacity-group/get-shared-capacity-group.html).

```
GET /v3/shared_capacity_groups/{id}
```

## Create Shared Capacity Group

Creates a Shared Capacity Group in a selected Capacity Pool.

Provide a unique name, the shared or metered channel counts, and the Capacity Pool
relationship. An external reference ID and the DIDs assigned to the group can also be
provided.

See [Create Shared Capacity Group](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/shared-capacity-group/create-shared-capacity-group.html).

```
POST /v3/shared_capacity_groups
```

## Update Shared Capacity Group

Updates a specific Shared Capacity Group.

Use this endpoint to change the group name, external reference ID, shared or metered
channel counts, Capacity Pool relationship, or assigned DIDs. Providing an empty DID
relationship removes all DIDs from the group.

See [Update Shared Capacity Group](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/shared-capacity-group/update-shared-capacity-group.html).

```
PATCH /v3/shared_capacity_groups/{id}
```

## Delete Shared Capacity Group

Deletes a specific Shared Capacity Group from the account. The request is rejected while
any DID is assigned to the group; remove those DIDs from the group first.

See [Delete Shared Capacity Group](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/shared-capacity-group/delete-shared-capacity-group.html).

```
DELETE /v3/shared_capacity_groups/{id}
```

## Data reference

See [Shared Capacity Group Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/shared-capacity-group/shared-capacity-group-object.html) for the complete
group attribute and relationship definitions.

## Common Shared Capacity Group use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Share flat-rate channels | Allow multiple DIDs to use shared channels allocated from a Capacity Pool. |
| Provide metered overflow | Use pay-per-minute channels when higher-priority capacity is unavailable. |
| Combine shared and metered channels | Use shared channels for expected traffic and metered channels for overflow. |
| Assign DIDs to a group | Add eligible DID phone numbers to the group's `dids` relationship. |
| Change channel allocation | Update `shared_channels_count` or `metered_channels_count` as requirements change. |
| Find groups in a Capacity Pool | Filter Shared Capacity Groups by their related Capacity Pool ID. |
| Synchronize external systems | Store an `external_reference_id` for the corresponding record in another system. |

## Related resources

Use Shared Capacity Groups together with Capacity Pools and DIDs to distribute inbound
call capacity among multiple phone numbers.

| Resource | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [Capacity Pools](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/capacity-pool/index.html) | Pools that provide the shared channels assigned to a group. |
| [DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html) | Eligible DID phone numbers that can use a group's shared or metered channels. |
| [Orders](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/order/index.html) | Orders used to add flat-rate channels to a Capacity Pool. |
| [Inbound Trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-in-trunks/index.html) | Routing destinations used by DIDs receiving inbound calls. |

Use Inventory Resources to retrieve and manage services related to your DIDWW account.

These resources cover account balance, orders, purchased DIDs, DID history, inbound
routing, outbound routing, SMS routing, and capacity management.

## Resource overview

| Resource | Use it to |
| --- | --- |
| [Balance](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/balance/index.html) | Retrieve the current account balance. |

| [DID History](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did-history/index.html) | Retrieve historical DID records. |
| [Inbound Trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-in-trunks/index.html) | Configure inbound voice routing destinations. |

| [Outbound Trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/index.html) | Configure outbound SIP trunking services. |
| [SMS Trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/index.html) | Configure where inbound SMS are delivered and how outbound SMS are sent. |
| [SMS Trunk Groups](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunk-groups/index.html) | Group SMS trunks for inbound SMS routing. |
| [Sender ID Verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sender-id-verifications/index.html) | Retrieve Sender ID verifications and change their name or SMS trunk. |
| [Capacity Pool](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/capacity-pool/index.html) | Manage assigned capacity pools. |
| [Shared Capacity Group](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/shared-capacity-group/index.html) | Create and manage shared capacity groups. |

## Common workflows

### Place an order

Use [Orders](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/order/index.html) after selecting available inventory from
[Coverage Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/index.html).

Recommended resources:

- [Balance](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/balance/index.html)
- [Orders](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/order/index.html)
- [DID](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html)

### Manage purchased DIDs

Use DID resources to retrieve existing numbers and update their service configuration.

Recommended resources:

- [DID](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html)
- [DID History](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did-history/index.html)
- [Inbound Trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-in-trunks/index.html)
- [Inbound Trunk Group](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-in-trunk-groups/index.html)

### Configure inbound routing

Use inbound trunks and trunk groups to control where incoming calls are routed.

Recommended resources:

- [Inbound Trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-in-trunks/index.html)
- [Inbound Trunk Group](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-in-trunk-groups/index.html)
- [DID](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html)

### Manage inbound capacity

Use capacity pools and shared capacity groups to manage channel capacity for inbound
voice services.

Recommended resources:

- [Capacity Pool](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/capacity-pool/index.html)
- [Shared Capacity Group](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/shared-capacity-group/index.html)

### Configure outbound services

Use outbound trunks to configure and manage outbound SIP services.

Recommended resources:

- [Outbound Trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/index.html)

### Configure SMS routing

Use SMS trunks and SMS trunk groups to receive and send SMS, then route DIDs to them.

Recommended resources:

- [SMS Trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/index.html)
- [SMS Trunk Groups](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunk-groups/index.html)
- [Sender ID Verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sender-id-verifications/index.html)
- [DID](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html)

## Related resources

  creating an order.
- [Regulation Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/index.html) - Provide required identity,
  address, and proof information.
- [Emergency Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/index.html) - Configure emergency calling
  services where required.

item.description:
Use the Identities resource to retrieve and manage personal or business identity records
used for DID registration and verification.

An Identity represents the person or business responsible for a DID phone number. It stores
contact and registration details and can be related to a country, birth country, Addresses,
Proofs, and Permanent Supporting Documents. The `verified` attribute is `true` once the
Identity is registered to at least one DID. It is not a statement about whether DIDWW has
reviewed its documents.

Before creating an Identity, retrieve the applicable [Address Requirement](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/index.html). The requirement determines which identity type can be used, where
the Identity must be located, which fields are mandatory, and whether proofs or supporting
documents are needed.

> **Note**
>
> For the complete registration workflow, see [Regulation Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/index.html). For
> an end-to-end purchasing and verification example, see [Buy a DID Number That
> Requires Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/examples/buy-dids-with-verification.html).

## Requirements and behavior

- Set `identity_type` to `personal` or `business` when creating an Identity.
- A personal Identity requires `first_name`, `last_name`, and `phone_number`.
- A business Identity also requires `company_name` and the first name, last name, and
  phone number of the company representative.
- A business Identity can also store a `company_website`. A personal Identity does not
  accept `company_website`.
- Once the Identity is in use, for example linked to DIDs or to a verification,
  `first_name`, `last_name` and `company_name` cannot be changed. The same applies to
  `company_website`, `company_reg_number`, `id_number`, `personal_tax_id`,
  `birth_date` and `country` once a value is stored for them. A stored
  `company_website` cannot be removed either.
- Once stored, `id_number`, `company_reg_number`, `personal_tax_id` and `birth_date`
  cannot be removed, whether or not the Identity is in use: sending `null` returns
  `422 Unprocessable Entity`.
- Fields that are normally optional become required when they appear in the Address
  Requirement's `personal_mandatory_fields` or `business_mandatory_fields` array. The
  `vat_id` attribute is listed as `tax_id` in these arrays.
- In API version `2026-11-19`, `country` and `birth_country` are separate
  relationships. Assigning `country` does not assign `birth_country` automatically.
- Proofs can be linked to an Identity when proof of personal or business identity is
  required. Permanent Supporting Documents can also be linked for reuse.
- Once approved, an Identity may be reused for DID types with the same level of
  restrictions, provided that it continues to satisfy the applicable Address Requirement.

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retrieve all Identities | `GET` | `/v3/identities` |
| Retrieve Identity | `GET` | `/v3/identities/{id}` |
| Create Identity | `POST` | `/v3/identities` |
| Update Identity | `PATCH` | `/v3/identities/{id}` |
| Delete Identity | `DELETE` | `/v3/identities/{id}` |

## Retrieve all Identities

Retrieves all Identities associated with the account.

Use this endpoint to find existing records before creating another Identity. Results can be
filtered by personal or business details, identity type, country ID, or external reference
ID. Related countries, birth countries, Proofs, Addresses, and Permanent Supporting
Documents can be included in the response.

See [Retrieve All Identities](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/get-identities.html).

```
GET /v3/identities
```

## Retrieve Identity

Retrieves a specific Identity by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint to inspect the Identity's attributes, `verified` status, and related
country, birth country, Proofs, Addresses, or Permanent Supporting Documents.

See [Retrieve Identity](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/get-identity.html).

```
GET /v3/identities/{id}
```

## Create Identity

Creates a personal or business Identity.

Use the applicable Address Requirement to select the identity type and supply all required
attributes and country relationships. Set `birth_country` explicitly when it is required.

See [Create Identity](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/create-identity.html).

```
POST /v3/identities
```

## Update Identity

Updates an existing Identity by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint to correct or complete personal details, business details, contact data,
external references, or country relationships. Updating `country` does not update
`birth_country` automatically.

See [Update Identity](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/update-identity.html).

```
PATCH /v3/identities/{id}
```

## Delete Identity

Permanently deletes an Identity by its unique ID. A deleted Identity cannot be restored.

See [Delete Identity](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/delete-identity.html).

```
DELETE /v3/identities/{id}
```

## Data reference

See [Identity Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/identity-object.html) for all attributes and relationships returned
by the resource.

## Common Identity use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Find a reusable Identity | Search existing records before creating a duplicate Identity for another DID verification. |
| Create a personal Identity | Store the personal and contact details required for an individual end user. |
| Create a business Identity | Store company details and the required details of its representative. |
| Meet mandatory field requirements | Supply the fields listed in `personal_mandatory_fields` or `business_mandatory_fields` for the applicable Address Requirement. |
| Add identity proofs | Link accepted Proofs when the Address Requirement requires proof of personal or business identity. |
| Reuse permanent documents | Link Permanent Supporting Documents to an Identity for regulations that accept the same reusable document. |
| Review verification readiness | Retrieve the Identity with its related Addresses, Proofs, and Permanent Supporting Documents before validating the registration data. |
| Reconcile external records | Store and filter by `external_reference_id` to associate the Identity with a record in another system. |

## Related resources

- [Address Requirements](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/index.html) - Determine the allowed identity
  type, location restrictions, mandatory fields, and required evidence.
- [Addresses](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/addresses/index.html) - Create and manage addresses linked to the
  Identity.
- [Proofs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/proofs/index.html) - Link accepted evidence to a personal or business
  Identity.
- [Permanent Supporting Documents](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/permanent-documents/index.html) - Attach reusable
  supporting documents to the Identity.
- [Address Verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/index.html) - Submit DIDs and the
  prepared compliance records for review.
- [Countries](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/countries/index.html) - Retrieve country IDs for
  the `country` and `birth_country` relationships.

item.description:
Use the Addresses resource to retrieve and manage address records used for DID registration
and verification.

An Address represents the physical location associated with an Identity. It stores the city
name, postal code, and full address and is linked to an Identity and country. It can also be
related to Proofs, a regulatory Area, and a City. The `verified` attribute is `true`
once the Address is registered to at least one DID. It is not a statement about whether
DIDWW has reviewed its proofs.

Before creating an Address, retrieve the applicable [Address Requirement](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/index.html). Its `address_area_level` determines whether the Address may be
worldwide or must be within the requirement country, the DID's regulatory area, or the same
city as the DID.

> **Note**
>
> For the complete registration workflow, see [Regulation Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/index.html). For
> an end-to-end purchasing and verification example, see [Buy a DID Number That
> Requires Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/examples/buy-dids-with-verification.html).

## Requirements and behavior

- `city_name`, `postal_code`, and `address` are required when creating an Address.
- The Address must be linked to the relevant Identity and country.
- The location must satisfy the Address Requirement's `address_area_level` value. Possible
  values are `world_wide`, `country`, `area`, and `city`.
- Proofs can be linked to the Address when `address_proof_qty` is greater than zero. Use
  the Address Requirement's `address_proof_types` relationship to determine which Proof
  Types are accepted.
- `external_reference_id` is optional and has a maximum length of 100 characters.
- Once approved, an Address may be reused for DID types with the same level of restrictions,
  provided that it continues to satisfy the applicable Address Requirement.

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retrieve all Addresses | `GET` | `/v3/addresses` |
| Retrieve Address | `GET` | `/v3/addresses/{id}` |
| Create Address | `POST` | `/v3/addresses` |
| Update Address | `PATCH` | `/v3/addresses/{id}` |
| Delete Address | `DELETE` | `/v3/addresses/{id}` |

## Retrieve all Addresses

Retrieves all Addresses associated with the account.

Use this endpoint to find an existing Address before creating another one. Results can be
filtered by city name, postal code, full address, description, external reference ID, or
related Identity, country, Area, and City IDs. Related Identity, country, Proof, Area, and
City records can be included in the response.

See [Retrieve All Addresses](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/addresses/get-addresses.html).

```
GET /v3/addresses
```

## Retrieve Address

Retrieves a specific Address by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint to inspect the Address attributes, `verified` status, and related
Identity, country, Proofs, Area, or City. Related Identity proofs and permanent documents can
also be included when reviewing registration readiness.

See [Retrieve Address](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/addresses/get-address.html).

```
GET /v3/addresses/{id}
```

## Create Address

Creates an Address associated with an Identity and country.

Use the applicable Address Requirement to select a compliant location. Provide the city
name, postal code, and full address, then link the Address to the Identity that represents
the end user.

See [Create Address](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/addresses/create-address.html).

```
POST /v3/addresses
```

## Update Address

Updates an existing Address by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint to modify the city name, postal code, full address, description, or
external reference ID.

See [Update Address](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/addresses/update-address.html).

```
PATCH /v3/addresses/{id}
```

## Delete Address

Permanently deletes an Address by its unique ID. A deleted Address cannot be restored.

See [Delete Address](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/addresses/delete-address.html).

```
DELETE /v3/addresses/{id}
```

## Data reference

See [Address Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/addresses/address-object.html) for all attributes and relationships returned by
the resource.

## Common Address use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Find a reusable Address | Search existing records by Identity, country, Area, City, or address details before creating a duplicate. |
| Create an address for an Identity | Store the physical location required for an end-user registration and link it to the appropriate Identity. |
| Meet geographic restrictions | Use the requirement country, Area, or City to provide an Address that satisfies `address_area_level`. |
| Add address proofs | Link accepted Proofs when the Address Requirement requires evidence of the physical location. |
| Review verification readiness | Retrieve the Address with its Identity, Proofs, and location relationships before validating the registration data. |
| Reconcile external records | Store and filter by `external_reference_id` to associate the Address with a record in another system. |
| Correct address information | Update address attributes before creating an Address Requirement Validation or Address Verification. |

## Related resources

- [Address Requirements](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/index.html) - Determine the permitted address
  location and required Proof Types.
- [Identities](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/index.html) - Retrieve or create the Identity linked to the
  Address.
- [Areas](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/areas/index.html) - Retrieve regulatory Areas used for area-level location
  restrictions.
- [Proofs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/proofs/index.html) - Link accepted evidence to the Address.
- [Address Requirement Validation](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/address-requirement-validations.html) - Check the Identity and Address
  against the selected requirement.
- [Address Verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/index.html) - Submit DIDs and the
  prepared Address for review.
- [Countries](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/countries/index.html) - Retrieve country IDs for
  the Address relationship.
- [Cities](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/city/index.html) - Retrieve City records used by
  city-level address requirements.
