item.description:
Use the Address Requirements resource to retrieve the registration conditions that apply
to DID phone numbers in the DIDWW coverage catalog.

An Address Requirement defines the compliance data needed for a particular country and number
type. It specifies the permitted Identity type, Identity and Address location scopes,
mandatory Identity fields, required proof quantities and accepted Proof Types, required
supporting documents, and whether a service description is needed.

Address Requirements are read-only. Retrieve the applicable requirement before creating or
reusing an Identity, Address, Proof, or supporting document. After preparing the required
records, use an Address Requirement Validation to check them before creating an Address
Verification.

> **Note**
>
> For the complete registration workflow, see [Regulation Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/index.html). For
> an end-to-end purchasing and verification example, see [Buy a DID Number That
> Requires Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/examples/buy-dids-with-verification.html).

## Selecting the applicable requirement

Use [Retrieve All DID Groups](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/did-group/get-did-groups.html) to check `meta.needs_registration` and
identify the DID Group's country and `number_type`. You can include the DID Group's related
`address_requirement` or retrieve Address Requirements filtered by `country.id` and
`number_type`.

Inspect the selected requirement before creating any dependent records:

- `number_type` identifies the number type the requirement applies to: `local`,
  `national`, `mobile`, `toll_free`, `shared_cost`, or `global`.
- `identity_type` determines whether the end user may be personal, business, or either.
- `personal_area_level` and `business_area_level` determine whether the applicable
  Identity may be worldwide or must be from the requirement country.
- `address_area_level` determines whether the Address may be worldwide or must be within
  the requirement country, the DID's regulatory Area, or the same City as the DID.
- `personal_proof_qty`, `business_proof_qty`, and `address_proof_qty` specify how many
  Proofs are required.
- The related `personal_proof_types`, `business_proof_types`, and
  `address_proof_types` specify which Proof Types are accepted.
- `personal_mandatory_fields` and `business_mandatory_fields` identify additional
  Identity fields that must be supplied. An array is empty when none are mandatory. The
  company VAT number is listed as `tax_id`: supply it as the Identity `vat_id` attribute.
- The permanent and one-time Supporting Document Template relationships identify forms that
  must be completed and uploaded.
- `service_description_required` indicates whether a service description must be included
  in the Address Verification. `restriction_message` provides additional instructions for
  the selected country and number type.

> **Note**
>
> Proofs, supporting documents, and a service description are not required by every
> regulation. Create or submit them only when the applicable Address Requirement calls for
> them.

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retrieve all Address Requirements | `GET` | `/v3/address_requirements` |
| Retrieve Address Requirement | `GET` | `/v3/address_requirements/{id}` |
| Validate an Identity or Address | `POST` | `/v3/address_requirement_validations` |

## Retrieve all Address Requirements

Retrieves all Address Requirements available in the DIDWW coverage catalog.

Use this endpoint to find the requirement for a DID Group. Results can be filtered by
Address Requirement ID, country ID, or `number_type`. Related country, Proof Type, and
Supporting Document Template records can be included in the response.

See [Retrieve All Address Requirements](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/get-address-requirements.html).

```
GET /v3/address_requirements
```

## Retrieve Address Requirement

Retrieves a specific Address Requirement by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint when the applicable Address Requirement is already known and you need to
inspect its attributes or include its related Proof Types and Supporting Document Templates.

See [Retrieve Address Requirement](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/get-address-requirement.html).

```
GET /v3/address_requirements/{id}
```

## Validate an Identity or Address

Checks whether an Identity and/or Address satisfies a selected Address Requirement.

Use this endpoint after preparing the required records and before creating an Address
Verification. Link the Address Requirement and the Identity and/or Address to be checked. A
successful request returns `201 Created`. A `422 Unprocessable Entity` response lists
missing or invalid registration data that should be corrected before submission.

See [Validate an Address Requirement](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/address-requirement-validations.html).

```
POST /v3/address_requirement_validations
```

## Data reference

See [Address Requirement Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/address-requirement-object.html) for all attributes and
relationships returned by the resource. The [Retrieve All Address Requirements](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/get-address-requirements.html) page also lists the values that may appear in the personal and
business mandatory field arrays.

## Requirement scope

### Identity location

The `personal_area_level` and `business_area_level` attributes can contain:

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `world_wide` | An Identity from any country can be used. |
| `country` | The Identity must be from the requirement country. |

### Address location

The `address_area_level` attribute can contain:

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `world_wide` | An Address from any country can be used. |
| `country` | The Address must be within the requirement country. |
| `area` | The Address must be within the locality or region covered by the DID prefix. |
| `city` | The Address must be from the same City as the DID. |

## Common Address Requirement use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Determine whether registration is required | Check the DID Group's `meta.needs_registration` value and retrieve its related Address Requirement when registration is needed. |
| Find a requirement by coverage | Filter Address Requirements by country ID and `number_type` to identify the applicable compliance rules. |
| Select an Identity type | Use `identity_type` to determine whether a personal Identity, business Identity, or either type may be used. |
| Apply location restrictions | Use the Identity and Address area-level attributes to select records from an accepted country, regulatory Area, or City. |
| Prepare mandatory data | Supply all fields listed in the applicable personal or business mandatory field array. |
| Prepare proofs | Use the proof quantities and related Proof Types to determine how many proofs are required and which types are accepted. |
| Prepare supporting documents | Use the related permanent and one-time Supporting Document Templates to identify, complete, and upload required forms. |
| Check registration readiness | Create an Address Requirement Validation to find missing or invalid information before submitting an Address Verification. |

## Related resources

- [DID Groups](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/did-group/index.html) - Determine whether
  registration is required and identify the applicable country and number type.
- [Identities](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/index.html) - Create or retrieve the personal or business
  Identity required by the selected requirement.
- [Addresses](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/addresses/index.html) - Create or retrieve an Address that meets the
  required location scope.
- [Areas](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/areas/index.html) - Retrieve regulatory Areas used by area-level address
  restrictions.
- [Proof Types](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/proof-types/index.html) - Retrieve details about the proof categories
  accepted by the requirement.
- [Proofs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/proofs/index.html) - Link accepted evidence to an Identity or Address.
- [Supporting Document Templates](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/supporting-document-templates/index.html) - Retrieve
  permanent or one-time forms referenced by the requirement.
- [Address Verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/index.html) - Submit the prepared DIDs
  and compliance data for review.

item.description:
Use the Address Verifications resource to submit DID registration data for compliance review
and monitor the result.

An Address Verification links one or more purchased DIDs to the Address prepared for the end
user. The Identity is connected through that Address. The task can also include one-time
Encrypted Files and a service description when required by the applicable Address
Requirement.

All Address Verifications are reviewed by the DIDWW Compliance Team. A newly created task
has a `pending` status and later becomes `approved` or `rejected`. You can retrieve
the task to monitor its status or configure a callback when creating it.

> **Note**
>
> For the complete registration workflow, see [Regulation Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/index.html). For
> an end-to-end purchasing and verification example, see [Buy a DID Number That
> Requires Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/examples/buy-dids-with-verification.html).

## Before creating a verification

- Use [Retrieve Address Requirements](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/get-address-requirements.html) to identify the requirement for the DID's
  country and number type.
- Create or reuse an [Identity](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/index.html) and an [Address](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/addresses/index.html) that satisfy the selected requirement.
- Add the required Identity and Address Proofs and any permanent supporting documents.
- Use [Address Requirement Validation](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/address-requirement-validations.html) to identify missing or invalid data
  before submitting the verification.
- Include `onetime_files` only when the requirement references a personal or business
  one-time Supporting Document Template.
- Include `service_description` only when `service_description_required` is `true`.
  Supplying a one-time document or service description when it is not needed can cause a
  `422 Unprocessable Entity` response.

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retrieve all Address Verifications | `GET` | `/v3/address_verifications` |
| Retrieve Address Verification | `GET` | `/v3/address_verifications/{id}` |
| Create Address Verification | `POST` | `/v3/address_verifications` |
| Update Address Verification | `PATCH` | `/v3/address_verifications/{id}` |

## Retrieve all Address Verifications

Retrieves all Address Verifications associated with the account.

Use this endpoint to monitor multiple verification tasks. Results can be filtered by
Address ID, Identity ID, status, reference, or external reference ID and sorted by creation
time or external reference ID. Related Addresses, DIDs, and DID Groups can be included in
the response.

See [Retrieve All Address Verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/get-address-verifications.html).

```
GET /v3/address_verifications
```

## Retrieve Address Verification

Retrieves a specific Address Verification by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint to inspect the current status and reference. For a rejected task, review
`reject_reasons` and `reject_comment` to determine what must be corrected. The related
Address, DIDs, and DID Groups can be included in the response.

See [Retrieve Address Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/get-address-verification.html).

```
GET /v3/address_verifications/{id}
```

## Create Address Verification

Creates an Address Verification and submits it for compliance review.

Link the DIDs being registered and the Address prepared for the end user. When required,
also link one-time Encrypted Files and provide a service description. You may set
`external_reference_id` to associate the task with an external system and configure
`callback_url` and `callback_method` to receive the final status.

The callback method can be `get` or `post`. Callback notifications report an
`approved` or `rejected` status and include rejection information when applicable.

See [Create Address Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/create-address-verification.html) and [Callbacks
Details](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/callbacks-details.html).

```
POST /v3/address_verifications
```

## Update Address Verification

Updates the `external_reference_id` of an existing Address Verification.

No other Address Verification attributes or relationships can be changed with this
endpoint. The external reference ID is optional and has a maximum length of 100 characters.

See [Update Address Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/update-address-verification.html).

```
PATCH /v3/address_verifications/{id}
```

## Data reference

See [Address Verifications Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/address-verifications-object.html) for all attributes
and relationships returned by the resource.

## Verification statuses

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `pending` | The verification has been submitted and is awaiting compliance review. |
| `approved` | The submitted registration data has been approved. |
| `rejected` | The submitted registration data was not approved. Inspect `reject_reasons` and `reject_comment` for details. |

## Sandbox testing

In the sandbox environment, you can simulate the result by setting `id_number` on the
Identity linked through the Address:

| Result | `id_number` value |
| --- | --- |
| Approve | `11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111` |
| Reject | `22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222` |

See the testing instructions on [Create Address Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/create-address-verification.html).

## Common Address Verification use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Submit DID registration data | Link purchased DIDs to the prepared Address and submit them for compliance review. |
| Provide one-time documents | Link completed and encrypted one-time forms when the Address Requirement calls for them. |
| Provide a service description | Describe the intended DID service when `service_description_required` is `true`. |
| Monitor verification progress | Filter tasks by status or reference, or retrieve a specific task by its ID. |
| Resolve a rejection | Inspect `reject_reasons` and `reject_comment` to determine which data or documents must be corrected before creating a new submission. |
| Receive status notifications | Configure a callback to receive the approved or rejected result without polling. |
| Reconcile external records | Create, filter, sort, or update tasks using `external_reference_id`. |
| Test an integration | Simulate approval and rejection outcomes in the sandbox environment. |

## Related resources

- [Address Requirements](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/index.html) - Determine which Identity, Address,
  Proofs, supporting documents, and service description are required.
- [Addresses](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/addresses/index.html) - Retrieve or create the Address linked to the
  verification task.
- [Identities](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/index.html) - Manage the end-user Identity connected through
  the Address.
- [DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html) - Retrieve purchased numbers and check
  `awaiting_registration`.
- [Encrypted Files](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/index.html) - Upload encrypted one-time supporting
  documents before creating the verification.
- [Proofs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/proofs/index.html) - Link accepted evidence to the Identity or Address.
- [Permanent Supporting Documents](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/permanent-documents/index.html) - Link reusable
  supporting documents to the Identity.
- [Callbacks Details](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/callbacks-details.html) - Process Address Verification status
  notifications.

item.description:
Use the Supporting Document Templates resource to retrieve forms that may be required for
DID registration.

A Supporting Document Template provides the form name, a download URL, and a `permanent`
attribute that determines how the completed document is used. Address Requirements can
reference separate templates for personal and business Identities and for permanent and
one-time documents.

Supporting Document Templates are read-only. Start with the applicable Address Requirement
to determine whether a template is required. Download and complete that specific form, then
encrypt and upload the completed document before linking it to the registration workflow.

> **Note**
>
> For the complete registration workflow, see [Regulation Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/index.html). For
> an end-to-end purchasing and verification example, see [Buy a DID Number That
> Requires Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/examples/buy-dids-with-verification.html).

## Permanent and one-time templates

An Address Requirement can reference the following template relationships:

| Relationship | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `personal_permanent_document` | Permanent form required for a personal Identity. |
| `business_permanent_document` | Permanent form required for a business Identity. |
| `personal_onetime_document` | One-time form required for a personal Identity. |
| `business_onetime_document` | One-time form required for a business Identity. |

Use the template's `permanent` value to continue the correct workflow:

- When `permanent` is `true`, create a Permanent Supporting Document that links the
  completed Encrypted File, the template, and the Identity. The document can be reused with
  that Identity where the same permanent document is required.
- When `permanent` is `false`, pass the completed Encrypted File in the `onetime_files`
  relationship when creating the Address Verification. Do not create a Permanent Supporting
  Document for a one-time form.

> **Important**
>
> Upload completed forms through [Create Encrypted File](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/create-encrypted-files.html). The endpoint accepts one encrypted
> `.pdf`, `.jpg`, or `.png` file per request. The file must not exceed 20 MB and
> expires 24 hours after upload, so use its ID before it expires.

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retrieve all Supporting Document Templates | `GET` | `/v3/supporting_document_templates` |
| Retrieve Supporting Document Template | `GET` | `/v3/supporting_document_templates/{id}` |

## Retrieve all Supporting Document Templates

Retrieves all Supporting Document Templates available in the DIDWW compliance catalog.

Use this endpoint to find templates by exact name, partial name, or permanent status. The
`url` attribute in each result provides the form to download.

See [Retrieve All Supporting Document Templates](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/supporting-document-templates/get-supporting-document-templates.html).

```
GET /v3/supporting_document_templates
```

## Retrieve Supporting Document Template

Retrieves a specific Supporting Document Template by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint when an Address Requirement identifies the template and you need its
name, download URL, or permanent status before preparing the document.

See [Retrieve Supporting Document Template](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/supporting-document-templates/get-supporting-document-template.html).

```
GET /v3/supporting_document_templates/{id}
```

## Data reference

See [Supporting Document Template Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/supporting-document-templates/supporting-document-templates-object.html) for
all attributes returned by the resource.

## Common Supporting Document Template use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Retrieve a required form | Follow the template relationship from an Address Requirement and use `url` to download the required form. |
| Search templates by name | Filter by an exact name or use `name_contains` to find templates containing a search term. |
| Separate permanent and one-time forms | Filter by `permanent` or inspect the attribute to determine how the completed form must be linked. |
| Prepare a reusable document | Complete a permanent form, upload it as an Encrypted File, and create a Permanent Supporting Document for the Identity. |
| Prepare a one-time document | Complete a one-time form, upload it as an Encrypted File, and link the file when creating the Address Verification. |
| Avoid unnecessary documents | Create a supporting document only when the applicable Address Requirement references its template. |

## Related resources

- [Address Requirements](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/index.html) - Determine whether a personal or
  business permanent or one-time template is required.
- [Encrypted Files](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/index.html) - Encrypt and upload completed forms.
- [Permanent Supporting Documents](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/permanent-documents/index.html) - Link a completed
  permanent form to an Identity.
- [Address Verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/index.html) - Attach completed one-time
  forms through the `onetime_files` relationship.
- [Identities](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/index.html) - Manage the personal or business Identity linked
  to a Permanent Supporting Document.

item.description:
Use the Encrypted Files resource to upload protected documents for DID registration and
verification.

An Encrypted File is a temporary uploaded document that can be linked to a Proof, a
Permanent Supporting Document, or an Address Verification. The API returns metadata such
as the file description and `expires_at` value. It does not return the original document
content through the Encrypted Files retrieval endpoints.

Before uploading a document, retrieve the current DIDWW RSA public keys and encrypt the
file. Submit the matching encryption fingerprint with the encrypted file so DIDWW can
validate which key was used.

> **Note**
>
> For the complete registration workflow, see [Regulation Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/index.html). For
> an end-to-end purchasing and verification example, see [Buy a DID Number That
> Requires Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/examples/buy-dids-with-verification.html).

## Upload requirements

- Retrieve the current key through [Get Public Keys](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/public-keys.html) before encrypting
  the document.
- Follow [Encryption Details](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/encryption-details.html) to encrypt the file and calculate
  the required fingerprint. Browser-side encryption using `@didww/encrypt` is the
  recommended approach. Server-side examples are also available for supported SDKs.
- Send the upload as `multipart/form-data` with
  `encrypted_files[encryption_fingerprint]` and `encrypted_files[file]`.
- `encrypted_files[description]` is optional.
- The accepted file formats are `.pdf`, `.jpg`, and `.png`.
- Upload one file per request. Each file must not exceed 20 MB.
- An uploaded Encrypted File expires after 24 hours. Link its ID to the required resource
  before the `expires_at` time.
- Legacy batch parameters such as `encrypted_files[items][][file]` are not supported in
  API version `2026-11-19` and return `400 Bad Request`.
- An outdated encryption fingerprint returns `422 Unprocessable Entity`. Retrieve the
  current public keys, encrypt the file again, and retry with the new fingerprint.

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retrieve public keys | `GET` | `/v3/public_keys` |
| Retrieve all Encrypted Files | `GET` | `/v3/encrypted_files` |
| Retrieve Encrypted File | `GET` | `/v3/encrypted_files/{id}` |
| Create Encrypted File | `POST` | `/v3/encrypted_files` |
| Delete Encrypted File | `DELETE` | `/v3/encrypted_files/{id}` |

## Retrieve public keys

Retrieves the DIDWW RSA public keys used to encrypt documents.

Use a current key to encrypt the source document and calculate the fingerprint supplied
with the upload. Retrieving the keys immediately before encryption helps avoid an outdated
fingerprint error.

See [Get Public Keys](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/public-keys.html) and [Encryption Details](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/encryption-details.html).

```
GET /v3/public_keys
```

## Retrieve all Encrypted Files

Retrieves metadata for all Encrypted Files associated with the account.

Use this endpoint to find uploaded file IDs and check their descriptions or expiration
times. Results can be sorted by `description` or `expires_at`.

See [Retrieve All Encrypted Files](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/get-encrypted-files.html).

```
GET /v3/encrypted_files
```

## Retrieve Encrypted File

Retrieves the metadata for a specific Encrypted File by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint to check the file description and `expires_at` time before linking the
file to another regulation resource.

See [Retrieve Encrypted File](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/get-encrypted-file.html).

```
GET /v3/encrypted_files/{id}
```

## Create Encrypted File

Uploads one encrypted document to the account.

Use `multipart/form-data` and provide the encrypted file and current encryption
fingerprint. The successful `201 Created` response is a JSON:API document
(`application/vnd.api+json`) that returns the Encrypted File ID and its `expires_at` time. Use that ID within 24 hours to create a Proof or Permanent Supporting
Document, or to attach a one-time document to an Address Verification.

See [Create Encrypted File](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/create-encrypted-files.html).

```
POST /v3/encrypted_files
```

## Delete Encrypted File

Deletes an Encrypted File by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint to remove an uploaded file that is no longer needed.

See [Delete Encrypted File](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/delete-encrypted-files.html).

```
DELETE /v3/encrypted_files/{id}
```

## Data reference

See [Encrypted Files Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/encrypted-files-object.html) for the returned metadata and
upload fields. See [Encryption Details](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/encryption-details.html) for the encryption and
fingerprint process.

## How an uploaded file is used

| Target resource | Use |
| --- | --- |
| [Proof](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/proofs/index.html) | Link the Encrypted File with an accepted Proof Type and the relevant Identity or Address. |
| [Permanent Supporting Document](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/permanent-documents/index.html) | Link one or more Encrypted Files with a permanent Supporting Document Template and an Identity. |
| [Address Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/index.html) | Pass the Encrypted File ID in `onetime_files` when the Address Requirement calls for a one-time supporting document. |

## Common Encrypted File use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Encrypt a registration document | Retrieve a current public key and encrypt a supported source file before upload. |
| Upload identity evidence | Upload a passport, identification document, or other accepted evidence before creating a Proof linked to an Identity. |
| Upload address evidence | Upload a bill, receipt, or other accepted evidence before creating a Proof linked to an Address. |
| Upload a completed regulatory form | Upload a completed Supporting Document Template for permanent or one-time use. |
| Check expiration | Retrieve file metadata and confirm that the file can be linked before it expires. |
| Remove an unused upload | Delete an Encrypted File that should not be used in the registration workflow. |

## Related resources

- [Public Keys](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/public-keys.html) - Retrieve the RSA keys required before encrypting a
  document.
- [Encryption Details](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/encryption-details.html) - Implement file encryption and
  fingerprint calculation.
- [Proofs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/proofs/index.html) - Link an uploaded file as accepted evidence for an
  Identity or Address.
- [Supporting Document Templates](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/supporting-document-templates/index.html) - Retrieve
  regulatory forms that must be completed and uploaded.
- [Permanent Supporting Documents](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/permanent-documents/index.html) - Link reusable
  completed forms to an Identity.
- [Address Verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/index.html) - Submit one-time encrypted
  files with a verification task.

item.description:
Use the Proofs resource to retrieve and manage evidence required for DID registration.

A Proof links one or more Encrypted Files to an accepted Proof Type and to the entity being
verified. The `entity` can be a personal or business Identity, or an Address. A Proof also
provides its creation time, optional expiration time, and optional external reference ID.

Create Proofs only when the applicable Address Requirement specifies a proof quantity
greater than zero. The requirement also identifies which Proof Types are accepted for the
selected Identity type or Address.

> **Note**
>
> For the complete registration workflow, see [Regulation Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/index.html). For
> an end-to-end purchasing and verification example, see [Buy a DID Number That
> Requires Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/examples/buy-dids-with-verification.html).

## Selecting the required proof

Inspect the applicable [Address Requirement](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/index.html) before uploading
documents:

| Entity | Required quantity | Accepted Proof Types |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Personal Identity | `personal_proof_qty` | `personal_proof_types` |
| Business Identity | `business_proof_qty` | `business_proof_types` |
| Address | `address_proof_qty` | `address_proof_types` |

When a required quantity is greater than zero:

1. Select one of the accepted Proof Types returned by the Address Requirement. You can use
   [Retrieve Proof Type](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/proof-types/get-proof-type.html) when you need its name and
   entity type.
2. Retrieve the current RSA public key, encrypt the supporting document, and [create an
   Encrypted File](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/create-encrypted-files.html).
3. Create the Proof before the Encrypted File expires. Link the uploaded file or files, the
   accepted `proof_type`, and the relevant Identity or Address as `entity`.

The Proof Type's `entity_type` must correspond to the entity being verified. Its possible
values are `personal`, `business`, and `address`.

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retrieve all Proofs | `GET` | `/v3/proofs` |
| Retrieve Proof | `GET` | `/v3/proofs/{id}` |
| Create Proof | `POST` | `/v3/proofs` |
| Update Proof | `PATCH` | `/v3/proofs/{id}` |
| Delete Proof | `DELETE` | `/v3/proofs/{id}` |

## Retrieve all Proofs

Retrieves all Proofs associated with the account.

Use this endpoint to find existing evidence before creating another Proof. Results can be
filtered by `external_reference_id` and sorted by `created_at`, `expires_at`, or
`external_reference_id`. The related Proof Type and Identity or Address entity can be
included in the response.

See [Retrieve All Proofs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/proofs/get-proofs.html).

```
GET /v3/proofs
```

## Retrieve Proof

Retrieves a specific Proof by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint to inspect the Proof's creation and expiration metadata, external
reference, accepted Proof Type, and related Identity or Address.

See [Retrieve Proof](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/proofs/get-proof.html).

```
GET /v3/proofs/{id}
```

## Create Proof

Creates a Proof for an Identity or Address.

Link from 1 to 5 unexpired Encrypted Files, one accepted `proof_type`, and one `entity`.
More than 5 files returns `422 Unprocessable Entity`. The entity's JSON:API type must be `identities` or `addresses`. You may also set
`external_reference_id` to associate the Proof with an external system. Its maximum
length is 100 characters.

See [Create Proof](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/proofs/create-proof.html).

```
POST /v3/proofs
```

## Update Proof

Updates the `external_reference_id` of a Proof.

Only `external_reference_id` can be changed through this endpoint. To replace the
document, delete the Proof and create a new one.

See [Update Proof](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/proofs/update-proof.html).

```
PATCH /v3/proofs/{id}
```

## Delete Proof

Deletes a Proof by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint to remove evidence that should no longer be linked to an Identity or
Address. To replace an incorrect Proof, delete it and create the correct record.

See [Delete Proof](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/proofs/delete-proof.html).

```
DELETE /v3/proofs/{id}
```

## Data reference

See [Proofs Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/proofs/proofs-object.html) for all attributes and relationships returned by
the resource.

## Common Proof use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Add personal identity evidence | Link an accepted personal Proof Type and encrypted evidence to a personal Identity. |
| Add business identity evidence | Link an accepted business Proof Type and encrypted evidence to a business Identity. |
| Add address evidence | Link an accepted Address Proof Type and encrypted evidence to an Address. |
| Meet proof quantity requirements | Create the number of Proofs specified by the applicable personal, business, or address proof quantity. |
| Review existing evidence | Retrieve Proofs with their Proof Types and entities before validating registration data. |
| Check Proof expiration | Sort or inspect Proofs by `expires_at` to identify time-limited evidence. |
| Reconcile external records | Create, update, and filter Proofs using `external_reference_id`. |
| Replace incorrect evidence | Delete an incorrect Proof and create a new Proof with the accepted type, entity, and Encrypted Files. |

## Related resources

  required and which Proof Types are accepted.
- [Proof Types](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/proof-types/index.html) - Retrieve the names and entity types of
  available evidence categories.
- [Encrypted Files](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/index.html) - Encrypt and upload the document files
  linked to a Proof.
- [Identities](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/index.html) - Manage the personal or business entity linked
  to the Proof.
- [Addresses](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/addresses/index.html) - Manage the Address entity linked to the Proof.
- [Address Requirement Validation](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/address-requirement-validations.html) - Check the prepared Identity,
  Address, and Proofs against the requirement.
- [Address Verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/index.html) - Submit the prepared
  compliance records for review.

item.description:
Use the Permanent Supporting Documents resource to retrieve and manage reusable regulatory
documents linked to an Identity.

A Permanent Supporting Document links one or more completed Encrypted Files to a permanent
Supporting Document Template and a personal or business Identity. Once prepared, the same
document can be reused with that Identity where the same permanent document is required.

Create a Permanent Supporting Document only when the applicable Address Requirement
references `personal_permanent_document` or `business_permanent_document`. One-time
forms follow a different workflow and must be linked to an Address Verification through
`onetime_files`.

> **Note**
>
> For the complete registration workflow, see [Regulation Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/index.html). For
> an end-to-end purchasing and verification example, see [Buy a DID Number That
> Requires Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/examples/buy-dids-with-verification.html).

## Preparing a permanent document

1. Retrieve the applicable [Address Requirement](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/index.html) and inspect
   the personal or business permanent-document relationship.
2. Retrieve the referenced [Supporting Document Template](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/supporting-document-templates/get-supporting-document-template.html), confirm that
   `permanent` is `true`, and download the form from its `url`.
3. Complete the form, encrypt it with a current DIDWW public key, and [create an
   Encrypted File](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/create-encrypted-files.html).
4. Create the Permanent Supporting Document before the Encrypted File expires. Link the
   completed file or files, the referenced template, and the Identity that owns the
   document.

> **Important**
>
> Do not create a Permanent Supporting Document for a template where `permanent` is
> `false`. Attach the completed Encrypted File through `onetime_files` when
> [creating the Address Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/create-address-verification.html).

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retrieve all Permanent Supporting Documents | `GET` | `/v3/permanent_supporting_documents` |
| Retrieve Permanent Supporting Document | `GET` | `/v3/permanent_supporting_documents/{id}` |
| Create Permanent Supporting Document | `POST` | `/v3/permanent_supporting_documents` |
| Update Permanent Supporting Document | `PATCH` | `/v3/permanent_supporting_documents/{id}` |
| Delete Permanent Supporting Document | `DELETE` | `/v3/permanent_supporting_documents/{id}` |

## Retrieve all Permanent Supporting Documents

Retrieves all Permanent Supporting Documents associated with the account.

Use this endpoint to find an existing reusable document before creating another one.
Results can be filtered by `external_reference_id` and sorted by `created_at` or
`external_reference_id`. The related Supporting Document Template and Identity can be
included in the response.

See [Retrieve All Permanent Supporting Documents](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/permanent-documents/get-permanent-documents.html).

```
GET /v3/permanent_supporting_documents
```

## Retrieve Permanent Supporting Document

Retrieves a specific Permanent Supporting Document by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint to inspect the creation time, external reference, template, and Identity
associated with a reusable document.

See [Retrieve Permanent Supporting Document](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/permanent-documents/get-permanent-document.html).

```
GET /v3/permanent_supporting_documents/{id}
```

## Create Permanent Supporting Document

Creates a reusable supporting document for an Identity.

The `files`, `template`, and `identity` relationships are required. Link from 1 to 5
unexpired Encrypted Files containing the completed form, the permanent Supporting Document
Template, and the Identity that will reuse the document. More than 5 files returns
`422 Unprocessable Entity`. You may also set
`external_reference_id` to associate the record with an external system. Its maximum
length is 100 characters.

See [Create Permanent Supporting Document](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/permanent-documents/create-permanent-document.html).

```
POST /v3/permanent_supporting_documents
```

## Update Permanent Supporting Document

Updates the `external_reference_id` of a Permanent Supporting Document.

Only `external_reference_id` can be changed through this endpoint. The `files`,
`template`, `identity`, and `created_at` values cannot be updated; sending any of
them returns an HTTP `400` error with code `105`, and the document is left unchanged.
To replace the document content, template, or identity, create a new Permanent Supporting
Document - creating one for the same template and identity supersedes the previous
document.

See [Update Permanent Supporting Document](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/permanent-documents/update-permanent-document.html).

```
PATCH /v3/permanent_supporting_documents/{id}
```

## Delete Permanent Supporting Document

Deletes a Permanent Supporting Document by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint when a reusable document should no longer be linked to an Identity.
Content, template, and identity changes are made by creating a new Permanent Supporting
Document rather than by updating the existing one.

See [Delete Permanent Supporting Document](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/permanent-documents/delete-permanent-document.html).

```
DELETE /v3/permanent_supporting_documents/{id}
```

## Data reference

See [Permanent Supporting Documents Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/permanent-documents/permanent-documents-object.html) for all
attributes and relationships returned by the resource.

## Common Permanent Supporting Document use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Prepare a personal regulatory form | Link a completed personal permanent template and its Encrypted Files to a personal Identity. |
| Prepare a business regulatory form | Link a completed business permanent template and its Encrypted Files to a business Identity. |
| Reuse an approved Identity | Use the permanent document already linked to the Identity where the same permanent document is required. |
| Find an existing document | Retrieve records with their templates and Identities before creating a duplicate. |
| Reconcile external records | Update, create, filter, and sort records using `external_reference_id`. |
| Replace document content | Create a new Permanent Supporting Document for the same template and Identity; it supersedes the previous document. Delete a record directly when no replacement is needed. |

## Related resources

- [Address Requirements](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/index.html) - Determine which personal or
  business permanent template is required.
- [Supporting Document Templates](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/supporting-document-templates/index.html) - Retrieve
  and download the permanent form referenced by the requirement.
- [Encrypted Files](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/index.html) - Encrypt and upload the completed form
  before creating the Permanent Supporting Document.
- [Identities](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/index.html) - Manage the personal or business Identity that
  owns the reusable document.
- [Address Requirement Validation](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/address-requirement-validations.html) - Check the Identity and Address after
  all required records have been prepared.
- [Address Verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/index.html) - Submit the prepared DIDs
  and compliance records for review.

item.description:
Use the Proof Types resource to retrieve the evidence categories available for personal
Identities, business Identities, and Addresses.

A Proof Type provides a `name` and an `entity_type`. The entity type determines whether
the category applies to a personal Identity, business Identity, or Address. Proof Type
records are linked to Address Requirements and are selected when creating Proofs.

Proof Types are read-only. The complete Proof Types catalog can be filtered by entity type,
but the applicable Address Requirement determines which specific Proof Types are accepted
and how many Proofs are required for a registration.

> **Note**
>
> For the complete registration workflow, see [Regulation Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/index.html). For
> an end-to-end purchasing and verification example, see [Buy a DID Number That
> Requires Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/examples/buy-dids-with-verification.html).

## How Proof Types are selected

Inspect the applicable [Address Requirement](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/index.html) and use the
relationship that matches the entity being verified:

| Entity Type | Address Requirement relationship | Proof entity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `personal` | `personal_proof_types` | Personal Identity |
| `business` | `business_proof_types` | Business Identity |
| `address` | `address_proof_types` | Address |

The corresponding `personal_proof_qty`, `business_proof_qty`, or
`address_proof_qty` value specifies how many Proofs are required. When the quantity is
zero, do not create a Proof for that entity. When it is greater than zero, select a Proof
Type from the matching relationship rather than choosing any catalog entry with the same
entity type.

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retrieve all Proof Types | `GET` | `/v3/proof_types` |
| Retrieve Proof Type | `GET` | `/v3/proof_types/{id}` |

## Retrieve all Proof Types

Retrieves all Proof Types available in the DIDWW compliance catalog.

Use this endpoint to list evidence categories or filter them by `entity_type`. The
supported entity types are `personal`, `business`, and `address`.

See [Retrieve All Proof Types](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/proof-types/get-proof-types.html).

```
GET /v3/proof_types
```

## Retrieve Proof Type

Retrieves a specific Proof Type by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint when an Address Requirement identifies an accepted Proof Type and you
need to inspect its name and entity type before creating a Proof.

See [Retrieve Proof Type](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/proof-types/get-proof-type.html).


## Data reference

resource.

## Common Proof Type use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| List personal evidence categories | Filter by `personal` to retrieve Proof Types intended for personal Identities. |
| List business evidence categories | Filter by `business` to retrieve Proof Types intended for business Identities. |
| List address evidence categories | Filter by `address` to retrieve Proof Types intended for Addresses. |
| Resolve an accepted type ID | Retrieve a Proof Type referenced by an Address Requirement to inspect its name and confirm the correct entity type. |
| Prepare a Proof | Use an accepted Proof Type ID with Encrypted Files and the relevant Identity or Address when creating a Proof. |

  a Proof can be linked.
- [Addresses](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/addresses/index.html) - Manage the Address entity to which a Proof can be

item.description:
Use the Areas resource to retrieve regulatory geographic areas used by DID registration
requirements.

An Area represents a locality or region within a country for regulatory purposes. It
provides a name and a country relationship. When an Address Requirement has
`address_area_level` set to `area`, the Address used for verification must be within the
locality or region covered by the DID phone number's prefix.

Areas are read-only and are separate from the Regions resource in Coverage Resources. Use
Areas to interpret registration restrictions. Use Coverage Regions to search DID inventory
by geographic subdivision.

> **Note**
>
> For the complete registration workflow, see [Regulation Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/index.html). For
> an end-to-end purchasing and verification example, see [Buy a DID Number That
> Requires Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/examples/buy-dids-with-verification.html).

## When to use Areas

Inspect the applicable [Address Requirement](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/index.html) before selecting
an Address:

| Address area level | Address restriction |
| --- | --- |
| `world_wide` | An Address from any country can be used. An Area lookup is not required. |
| `country` | The Address must be within the requirement country. An Area lookup is not required. |
| `area` | The Address must be within the locality or region covered by the DID prefix. Use the Areas resource to identify the regulatory area. |
| `city` | The Address must be from the same City as the DID. Use the Cities resource instead. |

For an area-level requirement, identify the DID's country and prefix from its DID Group,
then retrieve Areas by country ID and name. Prepare an Address within the matching
regulatory area and validate it against the Address Requirement before creating an Address
Verification.

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retrieve all Areas | `GET` | `/v3/areas` |
| Retrieve Area | `GET` | `/v3/areas/{id}` |

## Retrieve all Areas

Retrieves all regulatory Areas available through the DIDWW API.

Use this endpoint to find Areas by ID, case-insensitive name, or country ID. Results can be
sorted by name and can include the related country. Both the default and maximum page size
are 1,000 records.

See [Retrieve All Areas](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/areas/get-areas.html).

```
GET /v3/areas
```

## Retrieve Area

Retrieves a specific regulatory Area by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint when the Area ID is already known and you need to inspect its name or
include its related country.

See [Retrieve Area](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/areas/get-area.html).

```
GET /v3/areas/{id}
```

## Data reference

See [Area Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/areas/area-object.html) for all attributes and relationships returned by the
resource.

## Common Area use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Satisfy an area-level requirement | Identify the locality or region in which an Address must be located when `address_area_level` is `area`. |
| Find Areas in a country | Filter by `country.id` to retrieve regulatory Areas for the requirement country. |
| Find an Area by name | Use the case-insensitive `name` filter to resolve a regulatory Area and its ID. |
| Confirm an Area's country | Include the related country when retrieving one or more Areas. |
| Review an Address relationship | Use an Area ID when filtering Addresses or inspect the Area included with an Address. |
| Prepare registration data | Select an Address within the required Area before running an Address Requirement Validation. |

## Related resources

- [Address Requirements](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/index.html) - Determine whether the Address must
  be within the DID's regulatory Area.
- [DID Groups](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/did-group/index.html) - Identify the DID country,
  area name, and prefix associated with the registration requirement.
- [Addresses](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/addresses/index.html) - Create or retrieve an Address that satisfies the
  area-level restriction.
- [Countries](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/countries/index.html) - Retrieve country records
  related to Areas.
- [Cities](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/city/index.html) - Retrieve coverage Cities for
  requirements where `address_area_level` is `city`.
- [Regions](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/regions/index.html) - Retrieve coverage Regions used
  for DID inventory searches rather than regulatory Area restrictions.
- [Address Requirement Validation](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/address-requirement-validations.html) - Check the prepared Identity and
  Address against the selected requirement.
- [Address Verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/index.html) - Submit the prepared DIDs
  and Address for compliance review.

Use Regulation Resources to identify and satisfy end-user registration requirements for
DID phone numbers through the DIDWW API.

Registration requirements depend on the country and number type. A DID Group indicates
whether registration is required through `meta.needs_registration` (filter with
`filter[needs_registration]`), while a purchased DID may remain in the
`awaiting_registration` state until its registration is approved.

Start with the endpoint that matches your current task:

- To discover what is required, [retrieve Address Requirements](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/get-address-requirements.html).
- To prepare compliance data, [create an Identity](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/create-identity.html) and
  [create an Address](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/addresses/create-address.html), or retrieve records that can be
  reused.
- To check the prepared records before submission, create an
  [Address Requirement Validation](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/address-requirement-validations.html).
- To submit DIDs for compliance review, [create an Address Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/create-address-verification.html).
- To monitor a submission, [retrieve the Address Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/get-address-verification.html) or configure a callback when creating
  it.

## Resource overview

| Resource | Use it to |
| --- | --- |
| [Address Requirements](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/index.html) | Determine the identity, location, proof, supporting-document, and service-description requirements for a country and number type. |
| [Areas](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/areas/index.html) | Retrieve regulatory areas when a requirement restricts an address to the locality or region covered by a DID prefix. |
| [Identities](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/index.html) | Create and manage personal or business identity records for the end user. |
| [Addresses](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/addresses/index.html) | Create and manage addresses linked to an identity and country. |
| [Proof Types](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/proof-types/index.html) | Retrieve proof categories accepted for personal identities, business identities, and addresses. |
| [Public Keys](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/public-keys.html) | Retrieve the RSA public keys and fingerprint needed to encrypt documents before upload. |
| [Encrypted Files](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/index.html) | Upload temporary encrypted files for proofs and supporting documents. |
| [Proofs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/proofs/index.html) | Link encrypted files and an accepted Proof Type to an Identity or Address. |
| [Supporting Document Templates](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/supporting-document-templates/index.html) | Retrieve forms required by a regulation and identify whether each form is permanent or one-time. |
| [Permanent Supporting Documents](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/permanent-documents/index.html) | Link completed reusable supporting documents to an Identity. |
| [Address Requirement Validations](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/address-requirement-validations.html) | Check an Identity and Address against an Address Requirement before creating a verification task. |
| [Address Verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/index.html) | Submit DIDs and compliance records for review, then retrieve their status and any rejection details. |

## Common workflow

A typical registration workflow starts with the DID Group and narrows the applicable
requirement before any compliance records or documents are submitted.

```
DID Group (meta.needs_registration = true)
 └─ Address Requirement (Country + Number Type)
    ├─ Identity
    │  ├─ Address
    │  ├─ Proofs, when required
    │  └─ Permanent Supporting Documents, when required
    ├─ One-time Supporting Documents, when required
    ├─ Address Requirement Validation
    └─ Address Verification
       └─ pending → approved or rejected
```

> **Note**
>
> For a complete step-by-step example that covers discovering inventory, ordering a DID,
> preparing compliance records, and submitting the verification, see [Buy a DID
> Number That Requires Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/examples/buy-dids-with-verification.html).

### 1. Identify the applicable requirement

Use [Retrieve All DID Groups](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/did-group/get-did-groups.html) to
check `meta.needs_registration`. For purchased numbers, use [Retrieve All DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/get-dids.html) to check `awaiting_registration`.

Use [Retrieve Address Requirements](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/get-address-requirements.html) and filter
the results by the DID Group's `country.id` and `number_type`. Inspect the
returned requirement before creating any dependent records, especially:

- `identity_type` and the personal or business area level.
- `address_area_level` and any related regulatory area.
- `personal_proof_qty`, `business_proof_qty`, or `address_proof_qty`.
- The related personal, business, and address Proof Types.
- `personal_mandatory_fields` or `business_mandatory_fields`.
- Permanent and one-time Supporting Document Template relationships.
- `service_description_required` and `restriction_message`.

> **Note**
>
> Proofs, supporting documents, and a service description are not required by every
> regulation. Create or submit them only when the applicable Address Requirement calls for
> them.

### 2. Create or reuse the Identity and Address

Use [Retrieve All Identities](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/get-identities.html) and [Retrieve All
Addresses](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/addresses/get-addresses.html) to find records that can be reused. If suitable records
do not exist, [create a personal or business Identity](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/create-identity.html),
then [create an Address](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/addresses/create-address.html) linked to that Identity and the
required country. Supply every field listed in the applicable requirement's mandatory field
arrays.

In API version `2026-11-19`, assigning `country` to an Identity does not automatically
assign `birth_country`. Set `birth_country` explicitly when the requirement needs it.

Once approved, an Identity and Address may be reused for other DID types that have the same
level of restrictions.

### 3. Add proofs when required

Use the proof quantities and related Proof Types in the Address Requirement to determine
how many proofs are needed and which types are accepted. Use [Retrieve All Proof Types](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/proof-types/get-proof-types.html) when you need the details of an accepted type. For every
required proof:

1. [Retrieve the current Public Keys](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/public-keys.html) and encrypt the
   source document as described in [Encryption Details](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/encryption-details.html).
2. [Create an Encrypted File](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/create-encrypted-files.html) with the file
   and its encryption fingerprint.
3. [Create a Proof](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/proofs/create-proof.html) that links the Encrypted File, the accepted
   Proof Type, and the relevant Identity or Address.

> **Important**
>
> `POST /v3/encrypted_files` accepts one encrypted `.pdf`, `.jpg`, or `.png` file
> per request. The file must not exceed 20 MB and expires 24 hours after upload, so use the
> returned Encrypted File ID before it expires.

### 4. Add supporting documents when required

An Address Requirement may reference a personal or business Supporting Document Template.
Use [Retrieve All Supporting Document Templates](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/supporting-document-templates/get-supporting-document-templates.html), download the required
form from its `url`, complete it, encrypt it, and [upload it as an Encrypted File](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/create-encrypted-files.html).

- For a **permanent** template, [create a Permanent Supporting Document](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/permanent-documents/create-permanent-document.html) that links the Encrypted File, template,
  and Identity. It can be reused with that Identity where the same permanent document is
  required.
- For a **one-time** template, pass the Encrypted File ID in the `onetime_files`
  relationship when [creating the Address Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/create-address-verification.html). Do not create a Permanent Supporting
  Document for a one-time file.

### 5. Validate the prepared records

[Create an Address Requirement Validation](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/requirements/address-requirement-validations.html) with the Address Requirement, Identity, and
Address IDs. A successful response confirms that those records satisfy the selected
requirement. A `422 Unprocessable Entity` response identifies missing or invalid
information that should be corrected before submission.

### 6. Submit and monitor the verification

[Create an Address Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/create-address-verification.html)
that links the DIDs and Address. Include one-time Encrypted Files and a service description
only when required. The Identity is connected through the Address.

All Address Verifications are reviewed by the DIDWW Compliance Team. The verification status
can be `pending`, `approved`, or `rejected`. Use [Retrieve Address Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/get-address-verification.html) to inspect the status, `reject_reasons`,
and `reject_comment`, or use [Retrieve All Address Verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/address-verifications/get-address-verifications.html) to monitor multiple submissions. You can
also set `callback_url` and `callback_method` when creating the verification to receive
approved or rejected status notifications. See [Callbacks Details](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/callbacks-details.html).

## Requirement scope

Address Requirements can restrict where the Identity or Address must be located.

### Identity location

The `personal_area_level` and `business_area_level` attributes support:

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `world_wide` | An Identity from any country can be used. |
| `country` | The Identity must be from the requirement country. |

### Address location

The `address_area_level` attribute supports:

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `world_wide` | An Address from any country can be used. |
| `country` | The Address must be within the requirement country. |
| `area` | The Address must be within the locality or region covered by the DID prefix. |
| `city` | The Address must be from the same city as the DIDs. |

## Related resources

- [Coverage Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/index.html) - Find DID Groups, determine
  whether registration is required, and identify the country and number type.
- [Inventory Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/index.html) - Create orders and retrieve
  purchased DIDs that may be awaiting registration.
- [Emergency Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/index.html) - Manage the separate
  verification workflow for emergency calling services.
- [Callbacks Details](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/callbacks-details.html) - Handle Address Verification status
  notifications.

item.description:
Use the Emergency Requirements resource to retrieve the emergency calling registration
conditions available for DID phone numbers in the DIDWW coverage catalog.

An Emergency Requirement applies to a particular country and number type. It defines
the permitted Identity type, Identity and Address location scopes, mandatory fields,
estimated activation time, additional restrictions, and emergency calling pricing.

Emergency Requirements are read-only. Retrieve the applicable requirement before creating
or reusing an Identity and Address. After preparing those records, use an Emergency
Requirement Validation to check them before creating an Emergency Verification.

> **Note**
>
> For the complete registration and service-management workflow, see [Emergency
> Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/index.html). For an end-to-end example, see [Register Emergency Calling
> Service](https://doc.didww.com/api3/examples/register-emergency-calling-service.html).

## Selecting the applicable requirement

Use [Retrieve All DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/get-dids.html) to select active DIDs
whose DID Groups support the `emergency` feature. The DIDs submitted together must have
the same country and number type.

Use the country ID and the DID Group `number_type` to filter Emergency Requirements by
`country.id` and `number_type`. Inspect the selected requirement before creating any
dependent records:

- `number_type` identifies the number type the requirement applies to: `local`, `national`, `mobile`, `toll_free`, `shared_cost`, or `global`.
- `identity_type` determines whether a personal Identity, business Identity, or either
  type can be used.
- `personal_area_level` and `business_area_level` determine whether the applicable
  Identity can be worldwide or must be from the requirement country. A value can be
  `null` when that Identity type does not apply.
- `address_area_level` determines whether the Address must be in the requirement country,
  the locality or region covered by the DID prefix, or the same city as the DID.
- `personal_mandatory_fields` and `business_mandatory_fields` identify additional
  Identity data that must be supplied. An array is empty when none are mandatory. The
  company VAT number is listed as `tax_id`: supply it as the Identity `vat_id` attribute.
- `address_mandatory_fields` identifies additional Address data that must be supplied.
- `estimate_setup_time` provides the estimated service activation time.
- `requirement_restriction_message` provides additional instructions for the selected
  country and number type.
- `meta.setup_price` and `meta.monthly_price` provide the applicable emergency service
  pricing.

If a selected DID already has approved end-user registration, use an Address linked to the
same Identity for emergency registration. Include the DID's `identity` and
`address_verification` relationships when retrieving it to identify this condition.

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retrieve all Emergency Requirements | `GET` | `/v3/emergency_requirements` |
| Retrieve Emergency Requirement | `GET` | `/v3/emergency_requirements/{id}` |
| Validate an Identity or Address | `POST` | `/v3/emergency_requirement_validations` |

## Retrieve all Emergency Requirements

Retrieves all Emergency Requirements available to the account.

Use this endpoint to find the requirement that applies to the selected DIDs. Results can be
filtered by Emergency Requirement ID, country ID, or `number_type`. The country record
can be included in the response.

See [Retrieve All Emergency Requirements](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-requirements/get-emergency-requirements.html).

```
GET /v3/emergency_requirements
```

## Retrieve Emergency Requirement

Retrieves a specific Emergency Requirement by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint when the applicable requirement is already known and you need to inspect
its attributes, pricing, country, or number type before validation or submission.

See [Retrieve Emergency Requirement](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-requirements/get-emergency-requirement.html).

```
GET /v3/emergency_requirements/{id}
```

## Validate an Identity or Address

Checks whether an Identity, Address, or both satisfy a selected Emergency Requirement.

Use this endpoint after preparing the required records and before creating an Emergency
Verification. Link the Emergency Requirement and the applicable Identity, Address, or both
to be checked. A successful request returns `201 Created`. A `422 Unprocessable Entity`
response lists missing or invalid data that should be corrected before submission.

See [Validate an Emergency Requirement](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-requirements/emergency-requirement-validations.html).

```
POST /v3/emergency_requirement_validations
```

## Access and pricing

Access to these endpoints requires an emergency calling plan assigned to the account. A
request returns `403 Forbidden` when no plan is assigned.

The pricing values are returned in the resource's `meta` object:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `setup_price` | One-time setup price as a decimal string. The value is always `0.0` when a matching rate exists because activation is not charged through this API. It can be `null` when no matching emergency plan rate exists. |
| `monthly_price` | Monthly price from the account's matching emergency plan rate as a decimal string. It can be `null` when no matching rate exists. |

## Requirement scope

### Identity type

The `identity_type` attribute can contain:

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `personal` | A personal Identity is required. |
| `business` | A business Identity is required. |
| `any` | A personal or business Identity can be used. |

### Identity location

The applicable `personal_area_level` or `business_area_level` attribute can contain:

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `world_wide` | An Identity from any country can be used. |
| `country` | The Identity must be from the requirement country. |

### Address location

The `address_area_level` attribute can contain:

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `country` | The Address must be within the requirement country. |
| `area` | The Address must be within the locality or region covered by the DID prefix. |
| `city` | The Address must be from the same city as the registered DIDs. |

## Data reference

See [Emergency Requirement Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-requirements/emergency-requirement-object.html) for all attributes,
metadata, relationships, and supported values returned by the resource. See
[Emergency Requirement Validations](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-requirements/emergency-requirement-validations.html) for the
validation request relationships and response examples.

## Common Emergency Requirement use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Find a requirement for selected DIDs | Filter Emergency Requirements by the common country ID and `number_type` of the selected DIDs. |
| Select an Identity type | Use `identity_type` to determine whether a personal Identity, business Identity, or either type can be used. |
| Apply location restrictions | Use the Identity and Address area-level attributes to select records from an accepted country, locality, region, or city. |
| Prepare mandatory data | Supply every field listed in the applicable personal, business, and Address mandatory field arrays. |
| Show activation guidance | Present `estimate_setup_time` and `requirement_restriction_message` before the customer submits emergency registration data. |
| Show service pricing | Present the setup and monthly prices returned for the account's matching emergency plan rate. |
| Check submission readiness | Create an Emergency Requirement Validation to find missing or invalid Identity and Address data before creating an Emergency Verification. |

## Related resources

- [Emergency Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/index.html) - Follow the complete emergency calling
  registration and service-management workflow.
- [DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html) - Select active emergency-capable
  numbers and retrieve their country, DID Group, and existing registration
  relationships.
- [DID Groups](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/did-group/index.html) - Check whether the DID Group
  supports the `emergency` feature and retrieve its `number_type`.
- [Countries](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/countries/index.html) - Retrieve the country used to
  filter Emergency Requirements.
- [Identities](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/index.html) - Create or retrieve the
  personal or business Identity required by the selected requirement.
- [Addresses](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/addresses/index.html) - Create or retrieve the
  emergency location linked to the selected Identity.
- [Emergency Verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-verifications/index.html) - Submit the validated
  Address and selected DIDs for review.
