item.description:
Use the Emergency Calling Services resource to retrieve and cancel emergency calling
services associated with DID phone numbers in the account.

An Emergency Calling Service represents an emergency calling subscription and its assigned
DIDs. It provides the service name, reference, status, activation and renewal details,
pricing, number type, and relationships to its country, Order, Emergency Requirement, latest
Emergency Verification, and DIDs.

Emergency Calling Services cannot be created directly. A service is created automatically
when an [Emergency Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-verifications/index.html) is submitted in
**New Calling Service** mode. Use **Existing Calling Service** mode to submit a replacement
address for an existing service.

> **Note**
>
> For the complete registration and service-management workflow, see [Emergency
> Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/index.html). For complete examples, see [Register Emergency Calling
> Service](https://doc.didww.com/api3/examples/register-emergency-calling-service.html) and [Update
> Emergency Calling Service](https://doc.didww.com/api3/examples/update-emergency-calling-service.html).

Choose the operation that matches your task:

- To find and monitor services, [retrieve all Emergency Calling Services](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-calling-services/get-emergency-calling-services.html).
- To inspect one service and its related records, [retrieve an Emergency Calling
  Service](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-calling-services/get-emergency-calling-service.html).
- To change a registered address, [create an Emergency Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-verifications/create-emergency-verification.html) in **Existing Calling
  Service** mode.
- To add or remove an assigned number, [update the DID](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/update-did.html).
- To cancel the entire service, [delete the Emergency Calling Service](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-calling-services/delete-emergency-calling-service.html).

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retrieve all Emergency Calling Services | `GET` | `/v3/emergency_calling_services` |
| Retrieve Emergency Calling Service | `GET` | `/v3/emergency_calling_services/{id}` |
| Delete Emergency Calling Service | `DELETE` | `/v3/emergency_calling_services/{id}` |

## Retrieve all Emergency Calling Services

Retrieves all Emergency Calling Services in the account.

Use this endpoint to find services by status, country, number type, registered Address,
Identity, name, or reference. The Address and Identity filters use the records from the last
Emergency Verification linked to each service.

Results can be sorted by name, status, country name, renewal date, or creation time. Canceled
services have no `renew_date` and are sorted by it as `null` values.

The response can include the related country, Order, Emergency Requirement, Emergency
Verification, and DIDs.

See [Retrieve All Emergency Calling Services](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-calling-services/get-emergency-calling-services.html).

```
GET /v3/emergency_calling_services
```

## Retrieve Emergency Calling Service

Retrieves a specific Emergency Calling Service by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint to inspect the current service status, activation and renewal dates,
pricing, assigned DIDs, applicable Emergency Requirement, latest verification, and related
Order. Include the required relationships when the linked records are needed in the same
response.

See [Retrieve Emergency Calling Service](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-calling-services/get-emergency-calling-service.html).

```
GET /v3/emergency_calling_services/{id}
```

## Delete Emergency Calling Service

Cancels a specific Emergency Calling Service.

Cancellation is allowed when the service status is `new`, `changes_required`,
`active`, or `pending_update`. A successful request returns `204 No Content` and the
service becomes permanently canceled.

See [Delete Emergency Calling Service](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-calling-services/delete-emergency-calling-service.html).

```
DELETE /v3/emergency_calling_services/{id}
```

## Service lifecycle

### Create a service

To create a service, first select eligible DIDs and satisfy the applicable Emergency
Requirement. Then [create an Emergency Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-verifications/create-emergency-verification.html) in **New Calling Service** mode
with the validated `address` and one or more `dids` relationships. Do not provide an
`emergency_calling_service` relationship in this mode.

The verification creates the Emergency Calling Service automatically. The DIDWW Emergency
Team reviews the submission. When the verification is approved and the service status
becomes `active`, emergency routing is enabled for the assigned DIDs.

> **Important**
>
> Do not create an Order to purchase emergency calling. DIDWW creates the related Order
> automatically when the Emergency Calling Service is activated. This activation also
> triggers the related Order callback.

### Update the registered address

An address update can be submitted when the service status is `new`,
`changes_required`, or `active`. Prepare and validate the replacement Address against
the service's Emergency Requirement. Then create an Emergency Verification in **Existing
Calling Service** mode with the new `address` and existing
`emergency_calling_service` relationships. Do not provide a `dids` relationship in this
mode.

For an active service, the status becomes `pending_update` while the new address is
reviewed. Emergency routing remains enabled with the current address during the review. The
replacement address takes effect only after approval, when the service returns to
`active`.

An update request returns `422 Unprocessable Entity` when the service is `in_process`,
`pending_update`, or `canceled`. If the verification is rejected, inspect its
`reject_reasons` and `reject_comment`, correct the data, and submit another verification.

### Manage assigned DIDs

Adding or removing DIDs is handled through [Update DID](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/update-did.html), not through Emergency Verification creation.
Use the DID's `emergency_calling_service` relationship to manage its assignment.

Unassigning a DID does not immediately cancel its Emergency Calling Service. A service with
no remaining DIDs is automatically canceled within a few hours, and DIDWW notifies the
customer.

## Status values

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `new` | The service has been created but is not yet active. |
| `in_process` | The service verification is under review by the DIDWW Emergency Team. |
| `changes_required` | The verification was rejected and a corrected verification must be submitted. |
| `pending_update` | An update to an active service is under review. |
| `active` | The service is approved and emergency calling is operational. |
| `canceled` | The service has been permanently canceled. |

## Service data

The service provides:

- `name` and `reference` for identifying the service.
- `status` for tracking its lifecycle.
- `activated_at` and `canceled_at` timestamps. These can be `null` when the
  corresponding event has not occurred.
- `renew_date` for the next service renewal. This can be `null`.
- `created_at` for the service creation time.
- `meta.setup_price` and `meta.monthly_price` for its pricing.

See [Emergency Calling Service Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-calling-services/emergency-calling-service-object.html) for all
attributes, metadata, and relationships.

## Common Emergency Calling Service use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Monitor activation | Filter services by status and retrieve the related Emergency Verification to track review and activation. |
| Find services by coverage | Filter services by country ID or `number_type`. |
| Find a customer's service | Filter by the Identity or Address used in the last Emergency Verification. |
| Review assigned numbers | Include the related DIDs to see which phone numbers use the service. |
| Review registration rules | Include the related Emergency Requirement to inspect the rules that apply to the service and any future address update. |
| Review billing information | Include the automatically created Order and inspect the service's setup and monthly price metadata. |
| Update the emergency address | Submit an Emergency Verification in Existing Calling Service mode and monitor the service while it is `pending_update`. |
| Cancel emergency calling | Delete an eligible service when emergency routing and future renewal are no longer required. |

## Related resources

- [Emergency Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/index.html) - Follow the complete emergency calling
  registration and service-management workflow.
- [Emergency Requirements](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-requirements/index.html) - Determine the Identity,
  Address, restriction, and pricing rules that apply to the service.
- [Emergency Verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-verifications/index.html) - Create a service,
  submit an address update, and inspect approval or rejection details.
- [DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html) - Retrieve assigned numbers and manage
  their Emergency Calling Service relationships.
- [Orders](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/order/index.html) - Retrieve the Order created
  automatically when the service is activated.
- [Outbound Trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/index.html) - Configure
  outbound routing for emergency-enabled DIDs after activation.
- [Callbacks Details](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/callbacks-details.html) - Handle Emergency Verification and
  related Order status notifications.

item.description:
Use the Emergency Verifications resource to submit emergency calling registration data for
review and monitor the result.

An Emergency Verification links a validated Address either to one or more DIDs for a new
Emergency Calling Service or to an existing service whose registered address must be
replaced. The verification records its reference, review status, rejection details,
callback settings, creation time, external reference ID, and related resources.

All Emergency Verifications are reviewed by the DIDWW Emergency Team. A newly created
verification has a `pending` status and later becomes `approved` or `rejected`. You
can retrieve the verification to monitor its status or configure a callback when creating
it.

> **Note**
>
> For the complete registration and service-management workflow, see [Emergency
> Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/index.html). For complete examples, see [Register Emergency Calling
> Service](https://doc.didww.com/api3/examples/register-emergency-calling-service.html) and [Update
> Emergency Calling Service](https://doc.didww.com/api3/examples/update-emergency-calling-service.html).

## Before creating a verification

- Confirm that the account has an emergency calling plan. Creation returns
  `403 Forbidden` when no plan is assigned.
- Use [Retrieve All DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/get-dids.html) to select active
  DIDs whose DID Groups support the `emergency` feature.
- For a new service, confirm that the selected DIDs use the same country and number type
  and are not assigned to another Emergency Calling Service.
- Retrieve the applicable [Emergency Requirement](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-requirements/get-emergency-requirements.html) using the selected country ID and
  `number_type`.
- Create or reuse an Identity and Address that satisfy the Emergency Requirement. If a DID
  already has approved end-user registration, use an Address linked to the same Identity.
- Use [Emergency Requirement Validation](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-requirements/emergency-requirement-validations.html) to identify missing or
  invalid Identity and Address data before submission.
- Choose either **New Calling Service** or **Existing Calling Service** mode. Do not combine
  the relationships used by the two modes.

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retrieve all Emergency Verifications | `GET` | `/v3/emergency_verifications` |
| Retrieve Emergency Verification | `GET` | `/v3/emergency_verifications/{id}` |
| Create Emergency Verification | `POST` | `/v3/emergency_verifications` |
| Update Emergency Verification | `PATCH` | `/v3/emergency_verifications/{id}` |

## Retrieve all Emergency Verifications

Retrieves all Emergency Verifications associated with the account.

Use this endpoint to monitor multiple verification tasks. Results can be filtered by
status, Emergency Calling Service ID, or external reference ID and sorted by creation time
or external reference ID. The related Address, Emergency Calling Service, and DIDs can be
included in the response.

See [Retrieve All Emergency Verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-verifications/get-emergency-verifications.html).

```
GET /v3/emergency_verifications
```

## Retrieve Emergency Verification

Retrieves a specific Emergency Verification by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint to inspect the current status and reference. For a rejected verification,
review `reject_reasons` and `reject_comment` to determine what must be corrected. The
related Address, Emergency Calling Service, and DIDs can be included in the response.

See [Retrieve Emergency Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-verifications/get-emergency-verification.html).

```
GET /v3/emergency_verifications/{id}
```

## Create Emergency Verification

Creates an Emergency Verification and submits it for review. A successful request returns
`201 Created` with a verification whose initial status is `pending`.

Choose the creation mode from the action you need to perform:

| Mode | Relationships to provide | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New Calling Service | Provide `address` and one or more `dids`. Do not provide `emergency_calling_service`. | Creates a new Emergency Calling Service automatically and submits its registration for review. |
| Existing Calling Service | Provide `address` and `emergency_calling_service`. Do not provide `dids`. | Resubmits a rejected service or submits a replacement address for an existing service. |

You can also provide:

- `external_reference_id` to associate the verification with a record in an external
  system. Its maximum length is 100 characters.
- `callback_url` to receive the final review result.
- `callback_method` set to `get` or `post`. It is required when `callback_url` is
  provided.

See [Create Emergency Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-verifications/create-emergency-verification.html).

```
POST /v3/emergency_verifications
```

## Update Emergency Verification

Updates the `external_reference_id` of a specific Emergency Verification.

No other verification attributes or relationships can be changed with this endpoint. The
external reference ID is optional and has a maximum length of 100 characters.

See [Update Emergency Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-verifications/update-emergency-verification.html).

```
PATCH /v3/emergency_verifications/{id}
```

## Creation modes and service effects

### New Emergency Calling Service

Use this mode when the selected DIDs are not assigned to an Emergency Calling Service.
Provide the validated Address and at least one DID. The service is created automatically
and is linked in the successful verification response.

If the verification is approved, the Emergency Calling Service becomes `active` and
emergency routing is enabled for its DIDs. If it is rejected, the service becomes
`changes_required`. Correct the rejected data and create a new verification in **Existing
Calling Service** mode.

> **Important**
>
> Do not create an Order to purchase emergency calling. When the Emergency Calling Service
> is activated, DIDWW creates its related Order automatically and triggers the related
> Order callback.

### Existing Emergency Calling Service

Use this mode to resubmit a service in `changes_required` or to replace the registered
address of a service whose status is `new` or `active`. Provide the replacement Address
and existing Emergency Calling Service. Do not provide DIDs in this mode.

For an active service, its status becomes `pending_update` during review. Emergency
routing remains enabled with the current address. The replacement address takes effect
only if the verification is approved and the service returns to `active`.

The request returns `422 Unprocessable Entity` if the service status is `in_process`,
`pending_update`, or `canceled`.

## Common creation errors

A `422 Unprocessable Entity` response can identify one or more issues that must be fixed,
including:

- No DIDs were supplied in New Calling Service mode.
- A matching emergency plan rate was not found.
- The selected DIDs do not share the same number type.
- A DID does not support the `emergency` feature.
- A DID that requires city-level data is not linked to a City ID.
- A DID is already assigned to another Emergency Calling Service.
- The Address or its Identity does not satisfy the applicable Emergency Requirement.
- A DID with approved end-user registration is submitted with an Address linked to a
  different Identity.

Use [Emergency Requirement Validation](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-requirements/emergency-requirement-validations.html) before creation to detect
Identity and Address problems early. DID-specific and rate checks are still applied when
the Emergency Verification is created.

## Verification statuses

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `pending` | The verification has been submitted and is awaiting a decision from the DIDWW Emergency Team. |
| `approved` | The submitted emergency registration data has been approved. |
| `rejected` | The submitted data was not approved. Inspect `reject_reasons` and `reject_comment` for details. |

## Callbacks

When a callback is configured, DIDWW sends a notification after the verification becomes
`approved` or `rejected`. The payload contains the verification ID, resource type,
status, rejection information, and related Emergency Calling Service ID.

A `get` callback sends the payload as query parameters. A `post` callback sends it as
`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` data. See [Callbacks Details](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/callbacks-details.html) for all parameters and request-signature validation.

## Data reference

See [Emergency Verification Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-verifications/emergency-verification-object.html) for all attributes
and relationships returned by the resource.

## Common Emergency Verification use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Create an emergency service | Submit a validated Address and compatible DIDs in New Calling Service mode. |
| Resubmit rejected data | Correct the reported problems and create a new verification for the service in `changes_required`. |
| Replace a registered address | Submit a validated replacement Address for an existing service and monitor its `pending_update` state. |
| Monitor review progress | Filter verifications by status or Emergency Calling Service ID, or retrieve a specific verification. |
| Resolve a rejection | Inspect `reject_reasons` and `reject_comment` to determine which data must be corrected before resubmission. |
| Receive status notifications | Configure a callback to receive the approved or rejected result without polling. |
| Reconcile external records | Create, filter, sort, or update verifications using `external_reference_id`. |

## Related resources

- [Emergency Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/index.html) - Follow the complete emergency calling
  registration and service-management workflow.
- [Emergency Requirements](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-requirements/index.html) - Determine and validate
  the Identity and Address rules for the selected DIDs.
- [Emergency Calling Services](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-calling-services/index.html) - Retrieve the
  service created or updated by the verification.
- [Addresses](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/addresses/index.html) - Create or retrieve the
  emergency location submitted for review.
- [Identities](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/index.html) - Manage the Identity
  linked through the submitted Address.
- [DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html) - Select compatible phone numbers and
  manage their Emergency Calling Service assignments.
- [Orders](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/order/index.html) - Retrieve the Order created
  automatically when the Emergency Calling Service is activated.
- [Callbacks Details](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/callbacks-details.html) - Process Emergency Verification and
  related Order status notifications.

Use Emergency Resources to register DID phone numbers for emergency calling services,
including E911 and E112, through the DIDWW API.

Emergency calling requirements depend on the country and number type. Customers must
provide valid Identity and Address information for the emergency location before routing
can be activated. This emergency workflow is separate from the end-user registration
workflow described in [Regulation Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/index.html).

Start with the endpoint that matches your current task:

- To find eligible numbers, [retrieve DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/get-dids.html) and
  select active DIDs whose DID Groups support the `emergency` feature.
- To discover the applicable rules and pricing, [retrieve Emergency Requirements](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-requirements/get-emergency-requirements.html).
- To check an Identity and Address before submission, create an
  [Emergency Requirement Validation](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-requirements/emergency-requirement-validations.html).
- To register DIDs or submit a replacement address, [create an Emergency Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-verifications/create-emergency-verification.html).
- To monitor a submission, [retrieve the Emergency Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-verifications/get-emergency-verification.html) or configure a callback when
  creating it.
- To inspect or cancel the resulting service, [retrieve an Emergency Calling Service](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-calling-services/get-emergency-calling-service.html) or [delete the Emergency
  Calling Service](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-calling-services/delete-emergency-calling-service.html).

## Resource overview

| Resource | Use it to |
| --- | --- |
| [Emergency Requirements](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-requirements/index.html) | Determine the Identity type, geographic scope, mandatory fields, estimated setup time, restrictions, and pricing for a country and number type. |
| [Emergency Requirement Validations](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-requirements/emergency-requirement-validations.html) | Check whether an Identity and Address satisfy an Emergency Requirement before creating an Emergency Verification. |
| [Identities](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/index.html) | Create or reuse the personal or business Identity required for the emergency registration. |
| [Addresses](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/addresses/index.html) | Create or reuse the emergency location linked to the selected Identity. |
| [Emergency Verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-verifications/index.html) | Submit a new service or address update for review, monitor its status, and inspect rejection details. |
| [Emergency Calling Services](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-calling-services/index.html) | Retrieve the service created by a verification, monitor activation and renewal, or cancel the service. |
| [DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html) | Find emergency-capable numbers and manage their Emergency Calling Service assignments. |

## Common workflow

A typical emergency calling workflow starts by selecting compatible DIDs and finding the
single Emergency Requirement that applies to their country and number type.

```
Eligible DID or DIDs
 └─ Emergency Requirement (Country + Number Type)
    ├─ Identity
    ├─ Address
    ├─ Emergency Requirement Validation
    └─ Emergency Verification
       ├─ New Calling Service → Emergency Calling Service
       └─ Existing Calling Service → replacement address review
          └─ pending → approved or rejected
```

> **Note**
>
> For complete examples, see [Register Emergency Calling Service](https://doc.didww.com/api3/examples/register-emergency-calling-service.html) and [Update Emergency Calling
> Service](https://doc.didww.com/api3/examples/update-emergency-calling-service.html).

### 1. Select compatible DIDs

Use [Retrieve All DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/get-dids.html) with
`filter[did_group.features]=emergency` to find DIDs whose DID Groups support emergency
calling. You can also use `filter[emergency_enabled]=false` to find DIDs where emergency
routing is not active.

Before continuing, confirm that:

- Every selected DID is active and supports the `emergency` feature.
- The selected DIDs have the same country and number type.
- The `emergency_calling_service` relationship is empty for each DID that will be used to
  create a new service.

> **Important**
>
> `emergency_enabled=false` does not guarantee that a DID is available for a new
> Emergency Calling Service. Always inspect its `emergency_calling_service` relationship.
> A DID already assigned to another Emergency Calling Service cannot be submitted for a
> new service.

If a DID already has an approved end-user registration, the emergency registration must
use an Address linked to the same Identity. Include the `identity` and
`address_verification` relationships when retrieving DIDs so that this condition can be
identified before submission.

### 2. Identify the applicable requirement

Use [Retrieve All Emergency Requirements](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-requirements/get-emergency-requirements.html) and filter the results by the selected
DIDs' `country.id` and DID Group `number_type`. Inspect the returned requirement before
creating or selecting the Identity and Address, especially:

- `identity_type` and the personal or business area level.
- `address_area_level` and any required geographic scope.
- `personal_mandatory_fields`, `business_mandatory_fields`, and
  `address_mandatory_fields`.
- `estimate_setup_time` and `requirement_restriction_message`.
- `meta.setup_price` and `meta.monthly_price`.

Access to Emergency Resources requires an emergency calling plan. Requests return
`403 Forbidden` when the account does not have one assigned. When a matching plan rate
exists, `meta.monthly_price` shows the recurring price and `meta.setup_price` is
`0.0` because an emergency service setup fee is not charged through the API. A `null`
price means that no matching rate was found.

### 3. Create or reuse the Identity and Address

Emergency Requirements support personal and business Identities. Use [Retrieve All
Identities](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/get-identities.html) and [Retrieve All
Addresses](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/addresses/get-addresses.html) to find records that satisfy
the applicable requirement. If suitable records do not exist, [create an Identity](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/identities/create-identity.html) and then [create an Address](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/addresses/create-address.html) linked to that Identity and the required
country.

Supply every field listed in the requirement's mandatory field arrays. If the DID already
has approved end-user registration, reuse that registration's Identity and select or create
an Address linked to it.

### 4. Validate the prepared records

[Create an Emergency Requirement Validation](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-requirements/emergency-requirement-validations.html) with the Emergency Requirement,
Identity, and Address IDs. A `201 Created` response confirms that the records satisfy the
selected requirement. A `422 Unprocessable Entity` response identifies missing or invalid
information that should be corrected before the verification is submitted.

### 5. Create a new Emergency Calling Service

[Create an Emergency Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-verifications/create-emergency-verification.html) in **New Calling Service** mode.
Provide the validated `address` relationship and at least one DID in the `dids`
relationship. Do not provide an `emergency_calling_service` relationship in this mode.

The Emergency Calling Service is created automatically from this verification. It cannot be
created directly. All Emergency Verifications are reviewed by the DIDWW Emergency Team.
When the verification is approved and the service status becomes `active`, emergency
routing is enabled for the associated DIDs.

> **Important**
>
> Do not create an Order to purchase emergency calling. When the Emergency Calling Service
> is activated, DIDWW creates the related Order automatically. If an Order callback is
> configured, that activation also triggers it.

### 6. Monitor the verification and service

Use [Retrieve Emergency Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-verifications/get-emergency-verification.html) to inspect `status`,
`reject_reasons`, and `reject_comment`. Use [Retrieve Emergency Calling Service](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-calling-services/get-emergency-calling-service.html) to confirm that the associated
service becomes `active`.

You can set `callback_url` and `callback_method` when creating a verification to receive
an `approved` or `rejected` notification. When `callback_url` is supplied,
`callback_method` must be `get` or `post`. See [Callbacks Details](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/callbacks-details.html) for the payload and signature-validation guidance.

If the verification is rejected, review its rejection details, correct the data, and create
another Emergency Verification in **Existing Calling Service** mode for the service whose
status is `changes_required`.

### 7. Update an existing service address

First, [retrieve the Emergency Calling Service](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-calling-services/get-emergency-calling-service.html) and confirm that its status is
`new`, `changes_required`, or `active`. Address updates are rejected with
`422 Unprocessable Entity` when the service is `in_process`, `pending_update`, or
`canceled`.

Prepare and validate the replacement Address against the service's Emergency Requirement.
Then [create an Emergency Verification](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-verifications/create-emergency-verification.html) in **Existing Calling Service**
mode with the new `address` and existing `emergency_calling_service` relationships. Do
not provide the `dids` relationship in this mode.

For an active service, its status becomes `pending_update` while the replacement address
is reviewed. Emergency routing remains enabled with the current address during the review.
The new address takes effect only after approval, when the service returns to `active`. If
the update is rejected, inspect `reject_reasons` and `reject_comment`, correct the data,
and submit another verification.

### 8. Manage assigned DIDs or cancel the service

Add or remove DIDs through [Update DID](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/update-did.html) rather
than by creating an address-update verification. Unassigning a DID does not immediately
cancel its Emergency Calling Service. A service with no remaining DIDs is automatically
canceled within a few hours, and DIDWW notifies the customer.

To cancel the entire service explicitly, use [Delete Emergency Calling Service](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/emergency-resources/emergency-calling-services/delete-emergency-calling-service.html). A service can be canceled
when its status is `new`, `changes_required`, `active`, or `pending_update`.

## Requirement scope

Emergency Requirements can restrict where the Identity and Address must be located and can
make otherwise optional fields mandatory.

### Identity location

The `personal_area_level` and `business_area_level` attributes support:

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `world_wide` | An Identity from any country can be used. |
| `country` | The Identity must be from the requirement country. |

### Address location

The `address_area_level` attribute supports:

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `country` | The Address must be within the requirement country. |
| `area` | The Address must be within the locality or region covered by the DID prefix. |
| `city` | The Address must be from the same city as the registered DIDs. |

### Mandatory fields

The `personal_mandatory_fields` and `business_mandatory_fields` arrays may contain the
values below. An array is empty when none are mandatory.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `birth_date` | Birth date of a person or of the company representative. |
| `personal_tax_id` | Personal tax number. |
| `id_number` | Proof of ID number. |
| `tax_id` | VAT or tax number of a company. Business only. Supply it as the Identity `vat_id` attribute. |
| `company_reg_number` | Company registration number. Business only. |
| `contact_email` | Contact email address. |
| `country` | Country of tax residence. |

The `address_mandatory_fields` array may contain `area`, which represents the state,
province, or region. It is empty when none are mandatory.

## Status values

### Emergency Verification statuses

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `pending` | The verification has been submitted and is awaiting a decision. |
| `approved` | The submitted emergency information has been approved. |
| `rejected` | The submission was rejected. Inspect `reject_reasons` and `reject_comment`. |

### Emergency Calling Service statuses

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `new` | The service has been created but is not yet active. |
| `in_process` | The service verification is under review by the DIDWW Emergency Team. |
| `changes_required` | The verification was rejected and a corrected verification must be submitted. |
| `pending_update` | An update to an active service is under review. |
| `active` | The service is approved and emergency calling is operational. |
| `canceled` | The service has been permanently canceled. |

## Related resources

- [Regulation Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/index.html) - Create and manage the
  Identities and Addresses reused by emergency registration.
- [Coverage Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/index.html) - Find DID Groups that support
  emergency calling and identify their country and number type.
- [DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html) - Find eligible phone numbers and manage
  their Emergency Calling Service assignments.
- [Outbound Trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/index.html) - Configure
  outbound routing after the Emergency Calling Service becomes active.
- [Orders](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/order/index.html) - Retrieve the Order that DIDWW creates
  automatically when the Emergency Calling Service is activated.
- [Callbacks Details](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/callbacks-details.html) - Handle Emergency Verification and
  related Order status notifications.

## Request

HTTP Method: `GET`

URI Path: `/v3/exports`

> **Note**
>
> For all returned data attributes, see [Export Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/export-object.html).

### URI Query Parameters

| Name | Type | Is Required? | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| filter[<filter\_name>] | `string` | No | [Filtering](https://doc.didww.com/api3/specification/filtering.html#api-filters) |
| fields[exports] | `string` | No | [Sparse fieldsets](https://doc.didww.com/api3/specification/sparse-fieldsets.html#api-sparse-fieldsets) |
| sort | `string` | No | [Sorting](https://doc.didww.com/api3/specification/sorting.html#api-sorting) |
| page[number] | `integer` | No | [Page number](https://doc.didww.com/api3/specification/pagination.html#api-pagination). |
| page[size] | `integer` | No | [Page size](https://doc.didww.com/api3/specification/pagination.html#api-pagination). Pagination defaults to `50` records per page. The maximum is `100`. |

### Filters

The collection includes Exports of every type, including Exports created with earlier API
versions. A filter on `export_type` also matches those earlier Exports of the same type.

| Filter Name | Type | Allow Blank | Allow Array | Filters by: |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id | `string` | No | Yes | The Export ID. |
| external\_reference\_id | `string` | No | No | The `external_reference_id` field. |
| export\_type | `string` | No | Yes | The `export_type` field. Possible values: `cdr_in`, `cdr_out`, `sms_in`, `sms_out`. |
| status | `string` | No | Yes | The `status` field. Possible values: `pending`, `processing`, `completed`. |
| created\_at\_gteq | `string` | No | No | Exports created on or after the specified date and time. |
| created\_at\_lteq | `string` | No | No | Exports created on or before the specified date and time. |

Filters that allow an array accept a comma-separated list of values, for example
`filter[export_type]=sms_in,sms_out`. An Export matches when it matches any listed value.

### Sorting

| Value | Description |

## Exported File Format

The exported file contains call detail records (CDRs) or SMS records in CSV format,
depending on the `export_type` of the Export. The first line of the file contains the
column names listed below, in the listed order.

The columns below are those of an Export created with this API version. The file of an Export
created with an earlier API version keeps the columns of that version.

### Inbound CDRs

Columns of a `cdr_in` Export.

[`Inbound CDR sample`](https://doc.didww.com/_downloads/4652acaa8351c4dd7c4109f2482caa56/inbound_cdr_sample.csv)

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Date/Time Start (UTC) | `string` | Call start timestamp in UTC. |
| Date/Time Connect (UTC) | `string` | Call answer timestamp in UTC. |
| Date/Time End (UTC) | `string` | Call end timestamp in UTC. |
| Status | `string` | Call status. |
| Source Number | `string` | Caller number, as it reached DIDWW. |
| Source Number Out | `string` | Caller number, as delivered to the trunk. |
| Source Name | `string` | Caller name. |
| Source Country | `string` | Country of the caller number. |
| Source Network | `string` | Network of the caller number. |
| Destination DID | `string` | Destination DID number. |
| Duration (sec) | `integer` | Call duration in seconds. |
| Attempt | `integer` | Call attempt number. |
| Disconnect Code | `string` | Disconnect code. |
| Response | `string` | SIP response or system response. |
| Disconnect Initiator | `string` | Entity that initiated call termination. |
| Voice IN Trunk | `string` | Inbound trunk identifier or name. |
| Destination | `string` | Destination number. |
| Trunk Group | `string` | Associated trunk group. |
| Capacity Group | `string` | Associated capacity group. |
| Toll-free (USD) | `string` | Toll-free cost in USD. |
| PSTN (USD) | `string` | PSTN cost in USD. |

Every other filter is optional and matched exactly unless its description says otherwise.
A filter that is sent must not be blank, and only the filters listed for the selected
export type are accepted. Filters that accept several values take a single value or an
array of values.

**cdr\_in**

| Name | Type | Is Required? | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| from | `string` | Yes | Start date and time of the CDR range. |
| to | `string` | Yes | End date and time of the CDR range. |
| did\_number | `string` | No | CDR export for a specified DID number. If the 'did\_number' parameter is not used, CDRs are exported for all owned DID numbers. |
| source\_number | `string` | No | CDR export for calls from this caller number, as it reached DIDWW. |
| source\_number\_out | `string` | No | CDR export for calls from this caller number, as delivered to the trunk. |
| source\_country\_iso | `string` | No | CDR export for calls from the country with this upper-case ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, for example `GB`. |

**cdr\_out**

| to | `string` | Yes | End date and time of the CDR range. |
| voice\_out\_trunk.id | `string` | No | ID of outbound trunk. |
| source | `string` | No | CDR export for calls from this source number. |
| cli | `string` | No | CDR export for calls presenting this caller ID (CLI). |
| destination | `string` | No | CDR export for calls to this destination number. |

**sms\_in**

| to | `string` | Yes | End date and time of the SMS record range. |

| status | `string` | No | Messages in this state. Possible values: `success`, `failed`, `queued`. |
| trunk\_type | `string` or Array of `strings` | No | Messages delivered through SMS trunks of this type, or of any of these types. Possible values: `smpp_smsc`, `smpp_esme`, `sms_to_email`, `http_in`. |
| sms\_trunk.id | `string` or Array of `strings` | No | Messages delivered through this SMS trunk of the account, or any of these SMS trunks. |
| sms\_id | `string` | No | The message with this SMS ID. |

**sms\_out**

| Name | Type | Is Required? | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| from | `string` | Yes | Start date and time of the SMS record range. |
| to | `string` | Yes | End date and time of the SMS record range. |
| source\_address\_eq | `string` | No | Messages from exactly this sender address. |
| source\_address\_cont | `string` | No | Messages whose sender address contains this value. |
| destination\_address\_eq | `string` | No | Messages to exactly this recipient address. |
| destination\_address\_cont | `string` | No | Messages whose recipient address contains this value. |
| status | `string` | No | Messages in this state. Possible values: `routing_error`, `in_progress`, `queued`, `failed`, `success`. |
| sms\_trunk.id | `string` or Array of `strings` | No | Messages sent through this SMS trunk of the account, or any of these SMS trunks. |

item.description:
Use the Export resource to generate and download non-real-time reports of call and message
records through the DIDWW API.

An Export is an asynchronous request for inbound or outbound call detail records (CDRs) or
inbound or outbound SMS records. It records the export type, selected filters, processing
status, creation time, callback settings, external reference ID, and the download URL that
becomes available after processing is complete.

Four export types are supported:

| Export type | Use it to |
| --- | --- |
| `cdr_in` | Export inbound CDRs for a required date and time range. The results can optionally be limited by DID number, caller number, or caller country. |
| `cdr_out` | Export outbound CDRs for a required date and time range. The results can optionally be limited by Outbound Trunk, source number, CLI, or destination number. |
| `sms_in` | Export inbound SMS records for a required date and time range. The results can optionally be limited by address, status, SMS trunk, trunk type, or SMS ID. |
| `sms_out` | Export outbound SMS records for a required date and time range. The results can optionally be limited by address, status, SMS trunk, service type, sender ID verification, or SMS ID. |

> **Attention**
>
> Records of every export type can be exported only for the current month and the
> previous two months. DIDWW automatically deletes a completed Export one month after
> completion.

> **Note**
>
> Use [Call Events](https://doc.didww.com/call-events/index.html#cdr-streaming) when your application needs near-real-time or
> continuous CDR delivery instead of occasional report files.

Start with the endpoint that matches your current task:

- To request a new report, [create an Export](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/create-export.html).
- To monitor several requests, [retrieve all Exports](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/get-exports.html).
- To check one request and obtain its download URL, [retrieve the Export](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/get-export.html).
- To download a completed report, [retrieve its compressed CSV file](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/get-csv-file-of-export.html).

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retrieve all Exports | `GET` | `/v3/exports` |
| Retrieve Export | `GET` | `/v3/exports/{id}` |
| Create Export | `POST` | `/v3/exports` |
| Update Export | `PATCH` | `/v3/exports/{id}` |
| Download completed Export | `GET` | `/v3/exports/{filename}.csv.gz` |

## Create Export

Creates an Export and starts asynchronous report generation.

Set `export_type` to `cdr_in`, `cdr_out`, `sms_in`, or `sms_out` and provide the
required `filters` object. Every type requires `from` and `to` values for the date and
time range. You can also provide callback settings and an `external_reference_id` of up to
100 characters.

A successful request returns `201 Created` with status `pending`. The `url` remains
`null` until the export reaches `completed`.

See [Create Export](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/create-export.html).

```
POST /v3/exports
```

## Retrieve all Exports

Retrieves all Exports associated with the account, including Exports created with earlier
API versions.

Use this endpoint to monitor requests or find a previously created export. Results can be
filtered by `id`, `external_reference_id`, `export_type`, `status`, and creation
time (`created_at_gteq`, `created_at_lteq`). The `export_type` and `status` filters
accept a comma-separated list of values.

Results can be sorted by `status`, `created_at`, or `external_reference_id` and
support pagination and sparse fieldsets.

See [Retrieve All Exports](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/get-exports.html).

```
GET /v3/exports
```

## Retrieve Export

Retrieves a specific Export by its unique ID.

Use this endpoint to monitor asynchronous processing. When `status` becomes `completed`,
the `url` attribute contains the endpoint for downloading the generated `.csv.gz` file.

See [Retrieve Export](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/get-export.html).

```
GET /v3/exports/{id}
```

## Update Export

Updates the `external_reference_id` of an Export. No other attribute of an Export can be
changed.

See [Update Export](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/update-export.html).

```
PATCH /v3/exports/{id}
```

## Download a completed Export

Downloads the compressed CSV file generated for a completed Export.

Use the filename from the completed Export's `url` attribute. The filename is not the
Export resource ID. Send an authenticated `GET` request to the returned URL with an
access token in the `Authorization` header. This download also accepts an API key in the
`Api-Key` header.

The response is a download-only `.csv.gz` archive rather than a JSON:API document or an
uncompressed CSV response. Download and decompress the archive to read the enclosed CSV
data. The file page documents the columns of every export type and provides sample CSV
files.

See [Download Export File](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/get-csv-file-of-export.html).

```
GET /v3/exports/{filename}.csv.gz
```

## Export filters

Every filter value is matched exactly unless its description says otherwise. A filter that
is sent must not be blank. Only the filters listed for the selected export type are
accepted; any other key is rejected.

### Inbound CDR filters

Set `export_type` to `cdr_in` and provide:

| Filter | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | Yes | Start date and time of the CDR range. |
| `to` | Yes | End date and time of the CDR range. |
| `did_number` | No | Limit the report to a specific owned DID number. Omit it to export inbound CDRs for all owned DIDs. |
| `source_number` | No | Limit the report to calls from this caller number, as it reached DIDWW. |
| `source_number_out` | No | Limit the report to calls from this caller number, as delivered to the trunk. |
| `source_country_iso` | No | Limit the report to calls from the country with this ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, for example `GB`. |

### Outbound CDR filters

Set `export_type` to `cdr_out` and provide:

| Filter | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | Yes | Start date and time of the CDR range. |
| `to` | Yes | End date and time of the CDR range. |
| `voice_out_trunk.id` | No | Limit the report to a specific Outbound Trunk. |
| `source` | No | Limit the report to calls from this source number. |
| `cli` | No | Limit the report to calls presenting this caller ID (CLI). |
| `destination` | No | Limit the report to calls to this destination number. |

### Inbound SMS filters

Set `export_type` to `sms_in` and provide:

| Filter | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | Yes | Start date and time of the SMS record range. |
| `to` | Yes | End date and time of the SMS record range. |
| `source_address_eq` | No | Limit the report to messages from exactly this sender address. |
| `source_address_cont` | No | Limit the report to messages whose sender address contains this value. |
| `destination_address_eq` | No | Limit the report to messages to exactly this recipient address. |
| `destination_address_cont` | No | Limit the report to messages whose recipient address contains this value. |
| `status` | No | Limit the report to messages in this state: `success`, `failed`, or `queued`. |
| `trunk_type` | No | Limit the report to messages delivered through SMS trunks of this type, or of any of these types: `smpp_smsc`, `smpp_esme`, `sms_to_email`, `http_in`. |
| `sms_trunk.id` | No | Limit the report to messages delivered through this SMS trunk of the account, or any of these SMS trunks. |
| `sms_id` | No | Limit the report to the message with this SMS ID. |

### Outbound SMS filters

Set `export_type` to `sms_out` and provide:

| Filter | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | Yes | Start date and time of the SMS record range. |
| `to` | Yes | End date and time of the SMS record range. |
| `source_address_eq` | No | Limit the report to messages from exactly this sender address. |
| `source_address_cont` | No | Limit the report to messages whose sender address contains this value. |
| `destination_address_eq` | No | Limit the report to messages to exactly this recipient address. |
| `destination_address_cont` | No | Limit the report to messages whose recipient address contains this value. |
| `status` | No | Limit the report to messages in this state: `routing_error`, `in_progress`, `queued`, `failed`, or `success`. |
| `sms_trunk.id` | No | Limit the report to messages sent through this SMS trunk of the account, or any of these SMS trunks. |
| `sms_id` | No | Limit the report to the message with this SMS ID. |
| `service_type` | No | Limit the report to person-to-person (`p2p`) or application-to-person (`a2p`) traffic. |
| `sender_id_verification.id` | No | Limit the report to messages sent under this sender ID verification of the account, or any of these sender ID verifications. |

See [Export Filters Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/export-filters-object.html) for the filter data model.

## Export statuses

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `pending` | The export request has been accepted and is waiting to be processed. |
| `processing` | DIDWW is generating the report. |
| `completed` | Report generation is complete and the `url` is available for download. |

## Callbacks

Set `callback_url` and `callback_method` when creating an Export to receive a
notification when processing is complete. Send both attributes together. The callback
method can be `get` or `post`.

The completion payload contains the Export ID, resource type `exports`, status
`completed`, and the direct file-download `url`. The payload is the same for every
export type. A `get` callback sends these values as query parameters. A `post` callback
sends them as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` data.

See [Callbacks Details](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/callbacks-details.html) for the payload and request-signature
validation guidance.

## Data reference

See [Export Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/export/export-object.html) for all status, callback, file, reference, type,
and filter attributes returned by the resource.

## Common Export use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Export inbound CDRs | Generate a report for all owned DIDs or limit it to one DID number, caller number, or caller country. |
| Export outbound CDRs | Generate a report for all outbound traffic or limit it to one Outbound Trunk, source number, CLI, or destination number. |
| Export inbound SMS records | Generate a report of messages received on owned DIDs, optionally limited to selected SMS trunks or trunk types. |
| Export outbound SMS records | Generate a report of sent messages, optionally limited to selected SMS trunks, a service type, or sender ID verifications. |
| Monitor report generation | Retrieve the Export until its status becomes `completed` and its download URL is available. |
| Receive completion notifications | Configure a callback to receive the completed status and direct download URL without polling. |
| Reconcile external reports | Set and filter by `external_reference_id` to associate API exports with an external reporting system. |
| Process reports offline | Download and decompress the `.csv.gz` file for billing, analytics, or archival processing. |
| Receive continuous CDR data | Use Call Events instead of report exports when near-real-time delivery is required. |

## Related resources

- [DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html) - Retrieve the owned DID numbers that can
  be used to limit an inbound CDR export.
- [Outbound Trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/index.html) - Retrieve the
  Outbound Trunk ID that can be used to limit an outbound CDR export.
- [SMS Trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/index.html) - Retrieve the SMS trunk IDs
  that can be used to limit an SMS export.
- [Callbacks Details](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/callbacks-details.html) - Receive completion notifications and
  validate callback signatures.
- [Call Events](https://doc.didww.com/call-events/index.html#cdr-streaming) - Receive near-real-time inbound or outbound CDRs
  instead of generating report files.
- [Call Logs](https://doc.didww.com/logs-analytics/call-logs/index.html) - Review inbound and outbound
  call activity in the DIDWW documentation.
- [SMS Logs](https://doc.didww.com/logs-analytics/sms-logs/index.html) - Review inbound and outbound
  SMS activity in the DIDWW documentation.
- [Sender ID Verifications](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sender-id-verifications/index.html) -
  Retrieve the sender ID verification IDs that can be used to limit an outbound SMS export.
- [Sender ID Verifications overview](https://doc.didww.com/sms/sender-id-verifications/index.html) - Learn
  how sender ID verifications work.

item.name: Prices
Inbound Call Prices

header.description: The `Last-Modified` date of the copy you hold. The file (or, for `HEAD`, its headers) is sent only if it changed after that date. Otherwise the response is `304 Not Modified`. Ignored when the request also carries `If-None-Match`.

request.description:
Returns the inbound call price file of the plan assigned to the account, or only its headers.

`GET` downloads the prices of the plan as a gzipped CSV file named
`voice_in_prices.csv.gz`. `HEAD` returns the headers of the file without its body, so you
can check whether your copy is current before you download it.

## File Format

The file is a CSV file (UTF-8, LF line endings, a header row) compressed with gzip. Each row
is one price of the plan. Prices are in USD, VAT excluded. They are printed as the lookup
returns them: never rounded, with trailing zeros dropped and at least one decimal kept
(`0.0`, `1.5`, `0.002`).

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Country | Destination country, by name. Empty for a price of the plan's global country. Same as `country` in the [Inbound Call Price Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/inbound-call-prices/inbound-call-price-object.html). |
| Src country name | Source country of the call, by name. Empty for a price that applies to calls from any country. Same as `src_country_name`. |
| Source type | Calling party category, such as `cellular` or `fixed`. Same as `source_type`. |
| Destination | Destination prefix. Same as `destination`. |
| Rate | Per-minute rate. Empty when the plan rejects calls to the destination. Same as `rate`. |
| Connection fee | Fee charged once per call. Empty when the plan rejects calls to the destination. Same as `connection_fee`. |
| Initial interval | First billing increment, in seconds. Same as `initial_interval`. |
| Next interval | Each following billing increment, in seconds. Same as `next_interval`. |
| Reject calls | `true` when the plan rejects calls to the destination, otherwise `false`. Same as `reject_calls`. |

Example of the file content:

```
Country,Src country name,Source type,Destination,Rate,Connection fee,Initial interval,Next interval,Reject calls
United Kingdom,,cellular,44800,,,60,60,true
United Kingdom,United Kingdom,fixed,4480012,0.0125,0.0,60,60,false
United States,,cellular,1800,0.025,0.0,60,60,false
United States,,fixed,1800,0.018,0.0,60,60,false
```

## Request

Host: `api-vin.didww.com` (Sandbox: `api-vin-sandbox.didww.com`)

HTTP Method: `GET` or `HEAD`

URI Path: `/v3/prices.csv.gz`

The access token must list `api-vin.didww.com` in its `aud`. The `read` scope is
enough.

### Request Headers

| Name | Type | Is Required? | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| If-Modified-Since | `string` | No | The `Last-Modified` date of the copy you hold. The file (or, for `HEAD`, its headers) is sent only if it changed after that date. Otherwise the response is `304 Not Modified`. Ignored when the request also carries `If-None-Match`. |

### Response Headers

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Content-Disposition | `attachment` with the file name `voice_in_prices.csv.gz`. |
| Last-Modified | HTTP date of the later of the last change of the file content and the last change of the account's plan assignment. Send it back in `If-Modified-Since`. |
| Cache-Control | Always `private`. |
| Accept-Ranges | Always `none`. The file is served whole, without byte ranges. |
| Vary | Always `Authorization`. One URL returns each account the file of its own plan. |
| Content-Length | Size of the gzipped file in bytes. Not sent with `304 Not Modified`. |

No `ETag` is sent. A request that carries `If-None-Match` is always answered in full.

## Other Responses

Error responses to `GET` are JSON:API error documents. Responses to `HEAD` carry no body.

| Code | Success | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 304 | Yes | The file has not changed since the `If-Modified-Since` date. The response carries the headers of the `200` response except `Content-Length`, and no body. |
| 401 | No | [Unauthorized](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/authentication.html#authentication-v35). The bearer token was refused. The response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"`. |
| 403 | No | The token does not carry the `read` scope (title `Insufficient scope`). The response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope"`. |
| 404 | No | No price plan is assigned to the account (`price_plan_not_assigned`). |
| 429 | No | The request budget of the account on this service for the current window is spent (`too_many_requests`). `Retry-After` gives the number of seconds to wait. |
| 503 | No | The file could not be served, for example because the assigned plan has no generated file yet (`serving_failure`). `Retry-After` gives the number of seconds to wait. |

query.description: `string` Required. The number to price: `8` to `15` digits with a non-zero first digit, in international format without a `+` or a dialling prefix. Pattern: `^[1-9][0-9]{7,14}$`.

`string` The country the call comes from, as its upper-case ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (pattern `^[A-Z]{2}$`). A price that the plan sets for calls from that country then answers ahead of the any-source price. Without this filter, only any-source prices answer.

request.description:
Returns the inbound call prices that cover one number in the plan assigned to the account.

The number is matched against the destination prefixes of the plan. For every source type
and destination country that the plan prices, the longest prefix covering the number
answers, so the collection contains one price per such pair. The collection is never empty:
a number that no prefix covers returns `404` with the error code `price_not_found`.

- Without `filter[src_country_iso]`, only the prices that apply to a call from any country
  take part.
- With `filter[src_country_iso]`, a price that the plan sets for calls from that country
  ranks above the any-source price of the same source type and destination country,
  whatever their prefix lengths. The any-source price answers where the plan sets no price
  for that country. `src_country_name` names the country whose price answered, and is
  `null` when the any-source price answered.
- A destination that the plan rejects is still returned: `reject_calls` is `true`, and
  `rate` and `connection_fee` are `null`.

## Request

Host: `api-vin.didww.com` (Sandbox: `api-vin-sandbox.didww.com`)

HTTP Method: `GET`

URI Path: `/v3/lookup/prices`

> **Note**
>
> For all returned data attributes, see [Inbound Call Price Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/inbound-call-prices/inbound-call-price-object.html).

The access token must list `api-vin.didww.com` in its `aud`. The `read` scope is
enough. `filter` is the only query parameter read: `sort`, `page`, `fields`,
`include` and any unrecognised parameter return `400 Bad Request`.

### URI Query Parameters

| Name | Type | Is Required? | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| filter[number] | `string` | Yes | The number to price: `8` to `15` digits with a non-zero first digit, in international format without a `+` or a dialling prefix. Pattern: `^[1-9][0-9]{7,14}$`. |
| filter[src\_country\_iso] | `string` | No | The country the call comes from, as its upper-case ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (pattern `^[A-Z]{2}$`). A price that the plan sets for calls from that country then answers ahead of the any-source price. Without this filter, only any-source prices answer. |

## Other Responses

| Code | Success | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

item.description:
Use the Inbound Call Prices resource to read what inbound calls to your toll-free, shared-cost
and metered numbers cost, as priced by the inbound call pricing plan assigned to your DIDWW account.

Inbound call prices are served by the Inbound Call Rates service:

| Environment | Base URL |
| --- | --- |
| Production | `https://api-vin.didww.com/v3` |
| Sandbox | `https://api-vin-sandbox.didww.com/v3` |

The access token must list `api-vin.didww.com` in its `aud`, on the sandbox host as well.
A token with the `read` scope is enough. See [Prices Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/index.html) for
authentication, common rules and errors.

An inbound call price depends on the destination prefix of the called number, the destination
country, the calling party category (`source_type`, such as `cellular` or `fixed`)
and, for some prices, the country the call comes from. Prices are in USD, VAT excluded.

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Look up inbound call prices | `GET` | `/v3/lookup/prices` |
| Download inbound call price file | `GET` | `/v3/prices.csv.gz` |
| Check inbound call price file | `HEAD` | `/v3/prices.csv.gz` |

## Look up inbound call prices

Returns the prices that cover one number: for every source type and destination country
that the plan prices, the price of the longest prefix covering the number.

`filter[number]` is required. Add `filter[src_country_iso]` to include the prices that
the plan sets for calls from a specific country.

See [Look up Inbound Call Prices](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/inbound-call-prices/lookup-inbound-call-prices.html).

```
GET /v3/lookup/prices?filter[number]=18005550123
```

## Download inbound call price file

Downloads the whole price list of the plan as `voice_in_prices.csv.gz`. Use `HEAD` or
`If-Modified-Since` to check whether your copy is current.

See [Get Inbound Call Price File](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/inbound-call-prices/get-inbound-call-price-file.html).

```
GET /v3/prices.csv.gz
HEAD /v3/prices.csv.gz
```

## Data reference

See [Inbound Call Price Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/inbound-call-prices/inbound-call-price-object.html) for all attributes returned by a
lookup.

## Common inbound call pricing use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Estimate the cost of inbound calls to a number | Look up the number and compare the prices of each source type. |
| Price calls from a specific country | Add `filter[src_country_iso]` to see the price the plan sets for calls from that country. |
| Check rejected destinations | Find prices where `reject_calls` is `true`. |
| Keep a local price list | Download the price file and refresh it when `Last-Modified` changes. |

## Related resources

| Resource | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html) | DID phone numbers owned by the account. |

request.description:
Returns the outbound call price file of the plan assigned to the account, or only its headers.

`GET` downloads the prices of the plan as a gzipped CSV file named
`voice_out_prices.csv.gz`. `HEAD` returns the headers of the file without its body, so
you can check whether your copy is current before you download it.

## File Format

The file is a CSV file (UTF-8, LF line endings, a header row) compressed with gzip. Each row
is one price of the plan. The columns carry what the lookup attributes of the matching names
carry (see [Outbound Call Price Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/outbound-call-prices/outbound-call-price-object.html)). Prices are in USD, VAT
excluded. They are printed as the lookup returns them: never rounded, with trailing zeros
dropped and at least one decimal kept (`0.0`, `1.5`, `0.002`).

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Category | `International`, `Origin based` or `Local`. Same as `category`. |
| Country | Destination country of the prefix, by name. Same as `country`. |
| Network | Destination network of the prefix, by name. Same as `network`. |
| Prefix | Destination prefix. Same as `prefix`. |
| Rate | Current per-minute rate. Empty when the plan rejects calls to the destination or no price is in effect. Same as `rate`. |
| Connection fee | Current fee charged once per call. Empty when the plan rejects calls to the destination or no price is in effect. Same as `connection_fee`. |
| Initial increment | First billing increment, in seconds. Empty when no price is in effect. Same as `initial_increment`. |
| Recurring increment | Each following billing increment, in seconds. Empty when no price is in effect. Same as `recurring_increment`. |
| Reject calls | `true` when the plan rejects calls to the destination, otherwise `false`. Same as `reject_calls`. |
| Next rate | Per-minute rate from the Effective date on. Same as `next_rate`. |
| Next connection fee | Fee charged once per call from the Effective date on. Same as `next_connection_fee`. |
| Next initial increment | First billing increment, in seconds, from the Effective date on. Same as `next_initial_increment`. |
| Next recurring increment | Each following billing increment, in seconds, from the Effective date on. Same as `next_recurring_increment`. |
| Effective date | When the scheduled change takes effect, in UTC, for example `2026-11-01T00:00:00Z`. Same as `effective_at`. |
| Comment | The scheduled change of the price. Same as `comment`. |

The file leaves out some settings of a price, so two rows can look alike or show one prefix
at different prices.

### New Breakout and Removed

The file looks 30 days ahead:

- A prefix that has no price in effect, but whose next price starts within 30 days, is
  listed with the Comment `New Breakout`. Its Rate, Connection fee, Initial increment and
  Recurring increment are empty, and its Next columns carry the price it opens with.
- A prefix that rejects calls, and whose next price starts within 30 days, is listed with
  the Comment `New Breakout` too. It keeps its own increments, and its Next columns carry
  the price it opens with.
- A price that ends within 30 days, with no price of the same prefix taking over when it
  ends, is listed with the Comment `Removed`. The Effective date is the end of the price.

Example of the file content:

```
Category,Country,Network,Prefix,Rate,Connection fee,Initial increment,Recurring increment,Reject calls,Next rate,Next connection fee,Next initial increment,Next recurring increment,Effective date,Comment
International,Germany,Fixed,4930,0.0045,0.0,1,1,false,0.005,0.0,1,1,2026-11-01T00:00:00Z,Increase
International,Germany,Mobile,49151,0.021,0.0,1,1,false,,,,,,
International,Germany,Mobile,49152,0.024,0.0,1,1,false,,,,,2026-11-05T00:00:00Z,Removed
International,Germany,Mobile,49153,,,,,false,0.024,0.0,1,1,2026-11-05T00:00:00Z,New Breakout
International,Germany,Mobile,49155,,,30,30,true,0.024,0.0,1,1,2026-11-05T00:00:00Z,New Breakout
Origin based,Germany,Fixed,4930,0.0012,0.0,1,1,false,,,,,,
```

## Request

Host: `api-vout.didww.com` (Sandbox: `api-vout-sandbox.didww.com`)

HTTP Method: `GET` or `HEAD`

URI Path: `/v3/prices.csv.gz`

The access token must list `api-vout.didww.com` in its `aud`. The `read` scope is
enough.

### Request Headers

| Name | Type | Is Required? | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| If-Modified-Since | `string` | No | The `Last-Modified` date of the copy you hold. The file (or, for `HEAD`, its headers) is sent only if it changed after that date. Otherwise the response is `304 Not Modified`. Ignored when the request also carries `If-None-Match`. |

| Cache-Control | Always `private`. |

| Vary | Always `Authorization`. One URL returns each account the file of its own plan. |

No `ETag` is sent. A request that carries `If-None-Match` is always answered in full.

Use the Outbound Call Prices resource to read what outbound calls to each destination cost, as
priced by the outbound call pricing plan assigned to your DIDWW account, together with the price changes
that are already scheduled.

authentication, common rules and errors.

An outbound call price applies to a destination prefix under a set of routing conditions. Each
price has a `category` (`International`, `Origin based` or `Local`). Prices are in
USD, VAT excluded. The outbound call pricing service is the only prices service that also returns the next price of
a destination: the `next_` attributes, `effective_at` and `comment` describe a change
that is already scheduled.

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Look up outbound call prices | `GET` | `/v3/lookup/prices` |
| Download outbound call price file | `GET` | `/v3/prices.csv.gz` |
| Check outbound call price file | `HEAD` | `/v3/prices.csv.gz` |

Returns the prices that cover one number: for every set of routing conditions that the plan
prices, the price of the longest prefix covering the number.

`filter[number]` is the only supported filter.

See [Look up Outbound Call Prices](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/outbound-call-prices/lookup-outbound-call-prices.html).

```
GET /v3/lookup/prices?filter[number]=493012345678
```

## Download outbound call price file

Downloads the whole price list of the plan as `voice_out_prices.csv.gz`, including the
prefixes that open or are removed within the next 30 days. Use `HEAD` or
`If-Modified-Since` to check whether your copy is current.

See [Get Outbound Call Price File](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/outbound-call-prices/get-outbound-call-price-file.html).

```
GET /v3/prices.csv.gz
HEAD /v3/prices.csv.gz
```

## Data reference

See [Outbound Call Price Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/outbound-call-prices/outbound-call-price-object.html) for all attributes returned by a
lookup, and the `comment` and `category` values.

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Show the price of a call before it is made | Look up the number and read `rate`, `connection_fee` and the billing increments. |
| Track scheduled price changes | Read `next_rate`, `next_connection_fee`, `next_initial_increment`, `next_recurring_increment`, `effective_at` and `comment`. |

| filter[dst\_number] | `string` | Required unless `filter[dst_country_iso]` is sent | The number to price: `8` to `15` digits with a non-zero first digit, in international format without a `+` or a dialling prefix. Pattern: `^[1-9][0-9]{7,14}$`. |
| filter[dst\_country\_iso] | `string` | Required unless `filter[dst_number]` is sent | The destination country, as its upper-case ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (pattern `^[A-Z]{2}$`). Alone, every price of the plan for that country is returned. With a number, only the prices of that country take part in the match. |

| Code | Success | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | No | Malformed request: neither `filter[dst_number]` nor `filter[dst_country_iso]` is sent; `filter[dst_number]` is not `8` to `15` digits with a non-zero first digit; `filter[dst_country_iso]` is not the upper-case code of a known country; another filter is sent, `filter[id]` included; or another query parameter is sent (`sort`, `page`, `fields`, `include` or an unrecognised one). |
| 401 | No | [Unauthorized](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/authentication.html#authentication-v35). The bearer token was refused. The response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"`. |
| 403 | No | The token does not carry the `read` scope (title `Insufficient scope`). The response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope"`. |
| 404 | No | The account holds no price plan of the service in this domain, either no plan at all or a plan for which the service publishes no prices (`price_plan_not_assigned`), or no price of the plan matches the filters (`price_not_found`). |
| 406 | No | The `Accept` header admits neither `application/vnd.api+json` nor `*/*`. |
| 429 | No | The request budget of the account on this service for the current window is spent (`too_many_requests`). `Retry-After` gives the number of seconds to wait. |
