request.description:
Returns the SMS OUT price file of the plan assigned to the account in an SMS OUT domain (A2P,
P2P or OTP), or only its headers.

`GET` downloads the prices of the plan as a gzipped CSV file. `HEAD` returns the headers
of the file without its body, so you can check whether your copy is current before you
download it. The three domains have the same file format; the path selects the domain.

## File Format

The file is a CSV file (UTF-8, LF line endings, a header row) compressed with gzip. Each row
is one price of the plan. Prices are in USD, VAT excluded. They are printed as the lookup
returns them: never rounded, with trailing zeros dropped and at least one decimal kept
(`0.0`, `1.5`, `0.0525`).

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Source prefix | Prefix of the sending number. Empty when the price applies to an SMS from any number. Same as `source_prefix` in the [SMS OUT Price Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/sms-prices/sms-out-price-object.html). |
| Destination prefix | Destination prefix. Empty when the price applies to any destination. Same as `destination_prefix`. |
| Country | Destination country, by name. Same as `country`. |
| MCC | Mobile country code of the destination network. Empty when the price applies to any network. Same as `mcc`. |
| MCC name | Name of the mobile country code. Same as `mcc_name`. |
| MNC | Mobile network code of the destination network. Empty when the price applies to any network of the country. Same as `mnc`. |
| MNC name | Name of the mobile network. Same as `mnc_name`. |
| Reject SMS | `true` when the plan rejects SMS to the destination, otherwise `false`. Same as `reject_sms`. |
| Price | Price per SMS. Empty when Reject SMS is `true`. Same as `price`. |

The file leaves out some settings of a price, so two rows can look alike or show one
destination at different prices.

Example of the file content:

```
Source prefix,Destination prefix,Country,MCC,MCC name,MNC,MNC name,Reject SMS,Price
,336,France,208,France,,,false,0.0525
,338,France,,,,,true,
,49151,Germany,262,Germany,1,Telekom Deutschland,false,0.075
,49151,Germany,262,Germany,2,Vodafone,false,0.078
```

## Request

Host: `api-sms.didww.com` (Sandbox: `api-sms-sandbox.didww.com`)

HTTP Method: `GET` or `HEAD`

URI Path:

| Domain | URI Path | File name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SMS OUT A2P | `/v3/sms_out/a2p/prices.csv.gz` | `sms_out_a2p_prices.csv.gz` |
| SMS OUT P2P | `/v3/sms_out/p2p/prices.csv.gz` | `sms_out_p2p_prices.csv.gz` |
| SMS OUT OTP | `/v3/sms_out/otp/prices.csv.gz` | `sms_out_otp_prices.csv.gz` |

The access token must list `api-sms.didww.com` in its `aud`. The `read` scope is
enough.

### Request Headers

| Name | Type | Is Required? | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| If-Modified-Since | `string` | No | The `Last-Modified` date of the copy you hold. The file (or, for `HEAD`, its headers) is sent only if it changed after that date. Otherwise the response is `304 Not Modified`. Ignored when the request also carries `If-None-Match`. |

### Response Headers

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Content-Disposition | `attachment` with the file name of the domain, for example `sms_out_a2p_prices.csv.gz`. |
| Last-Modified | HTTP date of the later of the last change of the file content and the last change of the account's plan assignment in this domain. Send it back in `If-Modified-Since`. |
| Cache-Control | Always `private`. |
| Accept-Ranges | Always `none`. The file is served whole, without byte ranges. |
| Vary | Always `Authorization`. One URL returns each account the file of its own plan. |
| Content-Length | Size of the gzipped file in bytes. Not sent with `304 Not Modified`. |

No `ETag` is sent. A request that carries `If-None-Match` is always answered in full.

## Other Responses

Error responses to `GET` are JSON:API error documents. Responses to `HEAD` carry no body.

| Code | Success | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 304 | Yes | The file has not changed since the `If-Modified-Since` date. The response carries the headers of the `200` response except `Content-Length`, and no body. |
| 401 | No | [Unauthorized](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/authentication.html#authentication-v35). The bearer token was refused. The response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"`. |
| 403 | No | The token does not carry the `read` scope (title `Insufficient scope`). The response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope"`. |
| 404 | No | The account holds no price plan of the service in this domain, either no plan at all or a plan for which the service publishes no prices (`price_plan_not_assigned`). |
| 429 | No | The request budget of the account on this service for the current window is spent (`too_many_requests`). `Retry-After` gives the number of seconds to wait. |
| 503 | No | The file could not be served, for example because the assigned plan has no generated file yet (`serving_failure`). `Retry-After` gives the number of seconds to wait. |

request.description:
Returns the SMS OUT prices of one number or one country in the plan assigned to the account
in an SMS OUT domain: A2P, P2P or OTP. The three domains have the same request and response
format; the path selects the domain.

- With `filter[dst_number]`, the number is matched against the destination prefixes of the
  plan. The longest prefix covering the number wins, and every price of the plan under that
  prefix is returned.
- With `filter[dst_country_iso]` alone, every price of the plan for that country is
  returned, under every prefix.
- With both filters, the country narrows the prices before the prefixes are ranked.

At least one of the two filters is required. The collection is never empty: a number that no
price of the plan covers, or a country that the plan does not price, returns `404` with the
error code `price_not_found`.

Prices under one prefix can differ by the sending number they apply to (`source_prefix`),
by the destination network (`mcc` and `mnc`, which only the delivery decides) and by plan
settings that the API does not return. The collection is therefore the prices of the plan
that apply, not the one price that is charged. A destination that the plan rejects is still
returned: `reject_sms` is `true` and `price` is `null`.

enough. `filter` is the only query parameter read: any other filter, including

Alone, every price of the plan for that country is returned. With a number, only the prices of that country take part in the match. |

item.description:
> **Note**
>
> For more information about SMS services in DIDWW, see [Messaging](https://doc.didww.com/sms/index.html).

Use the SMS Prices resource to read what SMS cost, as priced by the SMS plans assigned to
your DIDWW account.

SMS prices are served by the SMS Rates service:

| Environment | Base URL |
| --- | --- |
| Production | `https://api-sms.didww.com/v3` |
| Sandbox | `https://api-sms-sandbox.didww.com/v3` |

The access token must list `api-sms.didww.com` in its `aud`, on the sandbox host as well.
A token with the `read` scope is enough. See [Prices Resources](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/index.html) for
authentication, common rules and errors.

SMS prices are split into four price domains. The account is assigned a plan in each domain
separately, and each domain has its own lookup and its own price file:

| Domain | Prices | Path prefix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SMS OUT A2P | SMS sent through the account's A2P plan, per destination. | `/v3/sms_out/a2p` |
| SMS OUT P2P | SMS sent through the account's P2P plan, per destination. | `/v3/sms_out/p2p` |
| SMS OUT OTP | SMS sent through the account's OTP plan, per destination. | `/v3/sms_out/otp` |
| SMS IN | SMS arriving on one of the account's numbers. | `/v3/sms_in` |

Prices are in USD, VAT excluded, and are never rounded. When the account holds no price plan
of the service in a domain (no plan at all, or a plan for which the service publishes no
prices), every operation of that domain returns `404` with the error code
`price_plan_not_assigned`.

## Endpoints

| Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Look up SMS OUT prices | `GET` | `/v3/sms_out/a2p/lookup/prices` `/v3/sms_out/p2p/lookup/prices` `/v3/sms_out/otp/lookup/prices` |
| Download SMS OUT price file | `GET`, `HEAD` | `/v3/sms_out/a2p/prices.csv.gz` `/v3/sms_out/p2p/prices.csv.gz` `/v3/sms_out/otp/prices.csv.gz` |
| Look up SMS IN prices | `GET` | `/v3/sms_in/lookup/prices` |
| Download SMS IN price file | `GET`, `HEAD` | `/v3/sms_in/prices.csv.gz` |

## Look up SMS prices

Returns the prices of one number or one country in the plan of the domain. Send
`filter[dst_number]`, `filter[dst_country_iso]`, or both. At least one of them is
required.

- With `filter[dst_number]`, the longest destination prefix of the plan covering the number
  wins, and every price of the plan under that prefix is returned.
- With `filter[dst_country_iso]` alone, every price of the plan for that country is
  returned, under every prefix.
- With both, the country narrows the prices before the prefixes are ranked.

See [Look up SMS OUT Prices](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/sms-prices/lookup-sms-out-prices.html) and
[Look up SMS IN Prices](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/sms-prices/lookup-sms-in-prices.html).

```
GET /v3/sms_out/a2p/lookup/prices?filter[dst_number]=4915123456789
GET /v3/sms_in/lookup/prices?filter[dst_country_iso]=US
```

## Download SMS price files

Downloads the whole price list of the plan of a domain as a gzipped CSV file. Use `HEAD`
or `If-Modified-Since` to check whether your copy is current.

| Domain | File name |
| --- | --- |
| SMS OUT A2P | `sms_out_a2p_prices.csv.gz` |
| SMS OUT P2P | `sms_out_p2p_prices.csv.gz` |
| SMS OUT OTP | `sms_out_otp_prices.csv.gz` |
| SMS IN | `sms_in_prices.csv.gz` |

See [Get SMS OUT Price File](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/sms-prices/get-sms-out-price-file.html) and
[Get SMS IN Price File](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/sms-prices/get-sms-in-price-file.html).

```
GET /v3/sms_out/a2p/prices.csv.gz
HEAD /v3/sms_in/prices.csv.gz
```

## Data reference

- [SMS OUT Price Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/sms-prices/sms-out-price-object.html) - attributes returned by the SMS OUT
  lookups.
- [SMS IN Price Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/sms-prices/sms-in-price-object.html) - attributes returned by the SMS IN
  lookup.

## Common SMS prices use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Check what an outbound SMS to a number may cost | Look up the number in the SMS OUT domain you send through and compare the prices of each network. |
| Compare the prices of a destination country | Look up the country with `filter[dst_country_iso]`. |
| Check rejected destinations | Find SMS OUT prices where `reject_sms` is `true`. |
| Estimate the cost of inbound SMS | Look up one of your numbers in the SMS IN domain. |
| Keep a local price list | Download the price file of a domain and refresh it when `Last-Modified` changes. |

## Related resources

| Resource | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [SMS Trunks](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/index.html) | Trunks that receive inbound SMS and send outbound SMS. |
| [DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html) | DID phone numbers owned by the account. |
| [Inbound Call Prices](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/inbound-call-prices/index.html) | Prices of inbound calls. |
| [Outbound Call Prices](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/outbound-call-prices/index.html) | Prices of outbound calls. |

Use Prices Resources to read the prices of the plans assigned to your DIDWW account. You can
look up what one number costs (for SMS, also every price of one country), or download the
whole price list of a plan as a compressed CSV file.

Prices are served by three dedicated services, each on its own host. They are not served by
`api.didww.com`: send each request to the host of the service whose prices you need.

| Service | Prices | Production | Sandbox |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Inbound Call Rates | Inbound calls to toll-free, shared-cost and metered numbers. | `https://api-vin.didww.com/v3` | `https://api-vin-sandbox.didww.com/v3` |
| Outbound Call Rates | Outbound calls to each destination, including scheduled price changes. | `https://api-vout.didww.com/v3` | `https://api-vout-sandbox.didww.com/v3` |
| SMS Rates | SMS IN, and SMS OUT for the A2P, P2P and OTP plans. | `https://api-sms.didww.com/v3` | `https://api-sms-sandbox.didww.com/v3` |

All prices are the values of the plan assigned to the account, in USD, VAT excluded.

## Resource overview

| Resource | Use it to |
| --- | --- |
| [Inbound Call Prices](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/inbound-call-prices/index.html) | Look up the inbound call prices of a number, or download the inbound call price file. |
| [Outbound Call Prices](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/outbound-call-prices/index.html) | Look up the current and next outbound call prices of a number, or download the outbound call price file. |
| [SMS Prices](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/sms-prices/index.html) | Look up the SMS IN or SMS OUT prices of a number or a country, or download the SMS price files. |

## Endpoints

| Service | Action | Method | Endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Inbound Call Rates | Look up prices | `GET` | `/v3/lookup/prices` |
| Inbound Call Rates | Download price file | `GET`, `HEAD` | `/v3/prices.csv.gz` |
| Outbound Call Rates | Look up prices | `GET` | `/v3/lookup/prices` |
| Outbound Call Rates | Download price file | `GET`, `HEAD` | `/v3/prices.csv.gz` |
| SMS Rates | Look up SMS IN prices | `GET` | `/v3/sms_in/lookup/prices` |
| SMS Rates | Download SMS IN price file | `GET`, `HEAD` | `/v3/sms_in/prices.csv.gz` |
| SMS Rates | Look up SMS OUT prices | `GET` | `/v3/sms_out/{a2p\|p2p\|otp}/lookup/prices` |
| SMS Rates | Download SMS OUT price file | `GET`, `HEAD` | `/v3/sms_out/{a2p\|p2p\|otp}/prices.csv.gz` |

Inbound Call Rates and Outbound Call Rates use the same paths. The host of the request selects the
service.

## Authentication

Every request is authenticated with a bearer access token in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer [access token]
```

Mint the token with `POST /token` on the token service of the environment you call
(`https://auth.didww.com/token` for Production, `https://auth-sandbox.didww.com/token`
for Sandbox), with an API key of that environment. A token minted in one environment is
refused by the other. See [Authentication](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/authentication.html#authentication-v35).

A service accepts a token only when the token's `aud` lists the audience of that service.
The audience is the production host name of the service, on the production and on the
sandbox host alike:

| Service | Audience (`aud`) |
| --- | --- |
| Inbound Call Rates | `api-vin.didww.com` |
| Outbound Call Rates | `api-vout.didww.com` |
| SMS Rates | `api-sms.didww.com` |

These audiences apply to the price lookup, download and file-header endpoints listed
above. To configure phone numbers or voice and SMS trunks, use `api.didww.com`.
See [Audiences](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/authentication.html#authentication-audiences-v35) for the complete service mapping.

Mint one token per service, or one token that lists every service you call. Every prices
operation only reads, so a token minted with the `read` scope is enough. For example, the
body of a `POST /token` request for a read-only token accepted by all three services:

```
1{
2  "aud": ["api-vin.didww.com", "api-vout.didww.com", "api-sms.didww.com"],
3  "scope": "read"
4}
```

## Price lookups

A lookup is a JSON:API `GET` request that returns a collection of resources of type
`prices`.

- Send `Accept: application/vnd.api+json`. A request whose `Accept` header admits
  neither `application/vnd.api+json` nor `*/*` returns `406 Not Acceptable`.
- `filter` is the only query parameter a lookup reads. `sort`, `page`, `fields`,
  `include`, a filter the lookup does not support and any unrecognised parameter return
  `400 Bad Request`.
- `data` is never empty. When nothing in the plan matches the filters, the response is
  `404` with the error code `price_not_found`.
- `meta.total_records` is the number of resources in `data`. Lookups are not paginated.
- Each resource has a UUID `id` that names the answering price. It is a name, not an
  address: there is no endpoint that returns a single price by its ID.
- Prices are decimal strings. In inbound call, outbound call, and SMS OUT lookups, a destination
  that the plan rejects is still returned: its `reject_calls` or `reject_sms` attribute
  is `true` and its current price (`rate` and `connection_fee`, or `price`) is `null`.

## Price files

A price file contains the whole price list of the plan assigned to the account.

- `GET` returns the file as a gzipped CSV (`Content-Type: application/gzip`): UTF-8, LF
  line endings, and a header row. The file is served whole, without byte ranges.
- `HEAD` returns the same headers without the body, so you can check whether your copy is
  current before you download the file.
- The file belongs to the account. One URL returns each account the file of its own plan.

A successful response carries these headers:

| Header | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Content-Disposition | `attachment` with the file name of the price domain, for example `voice_in_prices.csv.gz`. |
| Last-Modified | HTTP date of the later of the last change of the file content and the last change of the account's plan assignment. Send it back in `If-Modified-Since`. |
| Cache-Control | Always `private`. The file is served per account. |
| Accept-Ranges | Always `none`. The file is served whole. |
| Vary | Always `Authorization`. A cache keyed by the URL alone must not return the file to another account. |
| Content-Length | Size of the gzipped file in bytes. A `HEAD` response returns the size that the download sends. |

### Conditional requests

Conditional requests use `Last-Modified` and `If-Modified-Since` only:

- Send the `Last-Modified` value of the copy you hold in the `If-Modified-Since` request
  header. If the file has not changed since that date, the response is `304 Not Modified`
  with the headers of the `200` response except `Content-Length`, and no body.
- No `ETag` is sent. A request that carries `If-None-Match` is always answered in full,
  and its `If-Modified-Since` header is ignored.
- Because `Last-Modified` also reflects changes of the plan assignment, an account that is
  moved to another plan never receives `304` for the prices of the plan it left.

When the file cannot be served, for example because the assigned plan has no generated file
yet, the response is `503 Service Unavailable` with the error code `serving_failure` and a
`Retry-After` header.

## Errors

Errors are returned as JSON:API error documents (see [Error objects](https://doc.didww.com/api3/specification/errors/index.html#api-error-objects)).
Responses to `HEAD` requests carry no body. Each prices service counts the requests of
an account in its own budget; once it is spent, that service returns `429 Too Many Requests`.

| Status | Error code | Returned when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | Numeric JSON:API code, for example `102` | Lookups only. A filter is missing or malformed, a filter is not supported, or the request carries another query parameter (`sort`, `page`, `fields`, `include` or an unrecognised one). |
| 401 | `401` | The bearer token was refused: absent, malformed, expired, signed by a key this service does not hold, minted for another audience or environment, presented from an address outside the IP allowlist of the API key it was minted with, or naming an account this service has no record of. The response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"`. |
| 403 | `403` | The token does not carry the `read` scope (title `Insufficient scope`). The response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope"`. |
| 404 | `price_plan_not_assigned` | No price plan is assigned to the account. For SMS Rates, the account holds no price plan of the service in the requested domain. |
| 404 | `price_not_found` | Lookups only. Nothing in the plan matches the filters. |
| 406 |  | Lookups only. The `Accept` header admits neither `application/vnd.api+json` nor `*/*`. |
| 429 | `too_many_requests` | The request budget of the account on this service for the current window is spent. `Retry-After` gives the number of seconds to wait. |
| 503 | `serving_failure` | Price files only. The file could not be served. `Retry-After` gives the number of seconds to wait. |

Example of an error response:

```
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json

{
  "errors": [
    {
      "title": "Price plan not assigned",
      "detail": "No price plan is assigned to this account.",
      "code": "price_plan_not_assigned",
      "status": "404"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Common prices use cases

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Show the price of a call before it is made | Look up a number on Outbound Call Rates and read `rate`, `connection_fee` and the billing increments. |
| Track upcoming outbound call price changes | Read the `next_` attributes, `effective_at` and `comment` of a lookup, or the Next, Effective date and Comment columns of the outbound call price file. |
| Estimate the cost of inbound toll-free traffic | Look up a toll-free number on Inbound Call Rates, optionally for a given source country. |
| Compare SMS prices of a destination country | Look up the SMS OUT prices of a country with `filter[dst_country_iso]`. |
| Keep a local copy of a price list | Download a price file, then check it periodically with `HEAD` or a conditional `GET` that sends `If-Modified-Since`. |

## Related resources

- [Authentication](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/authentication.html#authentication-v35) - Mint the access token that the prices services
  accept.
- [Download Pricelists](https://doc.didww.com/phone-numbers/buy-numbers/download-pricelists.html) -
  Download price lists from the user panel.
- [DIDWW Pricing](https://doc.didww.com/billing/billing-and-prices/didww-pricing.html) - Overview of DIDWW
  pricing models.

item.name: Definitions
Common Definitions
item.description:
Common Definitions describe embedded objects that are referenced by DIDWW API resource
documentation.

These objects are not standalone API endpoints. They appear inside responses from other
resources and are used to describe reusable or separately documented data structures,
such as inventory pricing and capacity pricing tiers.

Some definitions may be used by multiple resources. Others are documented here because
they are referenced as embedded objects from a resource relationship.

Common Definitions should not be used for endpoint-specific request attributes. Request
schemas such as `did_order_items` and `capacity_order_items` are documented in the
Orders section.

## Definitions

### Stock Keeping Unit Object

A Stock Keeping Unit Object describes an inventory unit that can be selected when
ordering DID phone numbers or related services.

In DID ordering flows, retrieve Stock Keeping Unit objects from inventory resources
such as DID Groups or Available DIDs, then use the selected Stock Keeping Unit `id`
as `sku_id` when creating an order.

Attributes

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `setup_price` | `string` | Price for order creation. |
| `monthly_price` | `string` | Monthly price for order renewal. |
| `channels_included_count` | `integer` | Included channel capacity for each DID. |

Example

```
1{
2  "id": "e2406add-fd8a-475c-b959-81e9619d7a4b",
3  "type": "stock_keeping_units",
4  "attributes": {
5    "setup_price": "4.0",
6    "monthly_price": "4.0",
7    "channels_included_count": 2
8  }
9}
```

Common usage

| Used with | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [DID Groups](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/did-group/index.html) | Returned as related SKU options for DID ordering and pricing. |
| [Available DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/available-did/index.html) | May be returned through included DID Group SKU data when selecting a specific DID phone number. |
| [Orders](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/order/index.html) | The selected Stock Keeping Unit `id` is sent as `sku_id` in `did_order_items`. |

> **Note**
>
> `channels_included_count` is part of the Stock Keeping Unit Object. It describes
> the included channel capacity for each DID when that SKU is selected.
>
> It is not sent directly in the Create Order request. To order a DID phone number
> with a specific included channel option, select the matching Stock Keeping Unit and
> send its `id` as `sku_id`.

### Channel Quantity Based Price Object

A Channel Quantity Based Price Object describes quantity-based pricing tiers for
channels in a Capacity Pool.

In the API documentation, this object is referenced by the Capacity Pool Object
through the `qty_based_pricings` relationship.

It is not a standalone endpoint and it is not sent directly in `POST /v3/orders`.

Attributes

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `setup_price` | `string` | Price for order creation per channel. |
| `monthly_price` | `string` | Monthly price for order renewal based on the Capacity Pool billing cycle date, also known as `renew_date`. |
| `qty` | `integer` | Quantity of channels from which the price per channel applies with a discount. |

Example

```
1{
2  "id": "3f1c9e5a-7b2d-4c8e-9a61-2d5b8f0e4c17",
3  "type": "qty_based_pricings",
4  "attributes": {
5    "qty": 10,
6    "setup_price": "0.0",
7    "monthly_price": "1.5"
8  }
9}
```

Common usage

| Used with | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [Capacity Pool Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/capacity-pool/capacity-pool-object.html) | Returned through the `qty_based_pricings` relationship to describe quantity-based pricing tiers for the Capacity Pool. |

> **Note**
>
> This object describes pricing tiers returned for a Capacity Pool.
>
> Capacity orders are created separately with `POST /v3/orders` using
> `capacity_order_items`.
>
> The capacity order request uses attributes such as `capacity_pool_id` and `qty`.
> It does not send the Channel Quantity Based Price Object.
>
> A capacity order item uses request attributes such as:
>
> | Name | Type | Required | Description |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | `capacity_pool_id` | `string` | Yes | Capacity Pool ID. |
> | `qty` | `integer` | No | Quantity of channels to order. |

## When to use these definitions

Use these definitions when reading API responses that include the documented embedded
objects.

| Definition | Commonly used with |
| --- | --- |
| `Stock Keeping Unit Object` | [DID Groups](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/did-group/index.html), [Available DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/available-did/index.html), and DID order preparation. |
| `Channel Quantity Based Price Object` | [Capacity Pool Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/capacity-pool/capacity-pool-object.html) only. Returned through the `qty_based_pricings` relationship to describe quantity-based pricing tiers for the Capacity Pool. |

## Related resources

- [DID Groups](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/did-group/index.html) - DID Groups can include
  Stock Keeping Unit data for DID ordering and pricing.
- [Available DIDs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/coverage-resources/available-did/index.html) - Available DID flows
  may include DID Group and Stock Keeping Unit data.
- [Orders](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/order/index.html) - Orders use `sku_id` for DID order
  items and `capacity_pool_id` for capacity order items.
- [Capacity Pools](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/capacity-pool/index.html) - Capacity Pools can
  include quantity-based channel pricing through `qty_based_pricings`.

item.name: DID Group Object
item.description:
DID Group Object attributes and meta attributes.

Meta attributes are not available through [includes](https://doc.didww.com/api3/specification/includes.html#api-includes).

> **Note**
>
> In version `2026-11-19`, the `number_type` attribute replaces the `did_group_type`
> relationship. Requests that include `did_group_type`, filter by `did_group_type.id`, sort
> by `did_group_type.name`, or request `did_group_type` in sparse fieldsets return
> `400 Bad Request`.

## Attributes

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| area\_name | `string` | DID Group area name. This will be the name of the city, or a designation applicable to the area code such as **National**. |
| prefix | `string` | DID Group prefix (city or area calling code). |
| features | Array of `strings` | Features available for the DID Group. Supported values are `voice_in`, `voice_out`, `t38`, `sms_in`, `p2p`, `a2p`, `emergency`, and `cnam_out`. A DID Group may have multiple features. |
| is\_metered | `boolean` | Defines if the DID Group supports metered services (per-minute billing). |
| allow\_additional\_channels | `boolean` | Defines if channel capacity may be added to this DID Group. |
| service\_restrictions | `string` or `null` | Service restrictions message for the DID Group, if any restrictions apply. |
| number\_type | `string` | Number type offered by the DID Group. Possible values are `local`, `national`, `mobile`, `toll_free`, `shared_cost`, and `global`. |
| is\_demo | `boolean` | Defines if the DID Group is flagged as a demo group. |

item.name: Voice In Trunk Object
Codecs
item.description:
The `codecs` attribute of a SIP configuration lists the codecs offered on calls to an
Inbound Trunk, in priority order: the first has the highest priority.

The list holds at least one codec, without repeats. An empty list, a repeated value, or a
value not listed below returns `422 Unprocessable Entity`. Values are lowercase.

A trunk created without `codecs` uses the default list, in this order: `pcmu`, `pcma`, `g729`, `g723`, `telephone_event`.

| Value | Codec | Former `codec_ids` value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `telephone_event` | telephone-event | 6 |
| `g723` | G723 | 7 |
| `g729` | G729 | 8 |
| `pcmu` | PCMU | 9 |
| `pcma` | PCMA | 10 |
| `speex` | speex | 12 |
| `gsm` | GSM | 13 |
| `g726_32` | G726-32 | 14 |
| `g721` | G721 | 15 |
| `g726_24` | G726-24 | 16 |
| `g726_40` | G726-40 | 17 |
| `g726_16` | G726-16 | 18 |
| `l16` | L16 | 19 |
| `amr` | AMR | - |
| `amr_wb` | AMR-WB | - |

## Request

### Data Attributes

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| priority | `integer` | The priority of this target host. DIDWW will attempt to contact the target trunk with the lowest-numbered priority; target trunk with the same priority will be tried in an order defined by the weight field. The range is 0-65535. See [RFC 2782](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2782) for more details. |
| weight | `integer` | A trunk selection mechanism. The weight field specifies a relative weight for entries with the same priority. Larger weights will be given a proportionately higher probability of being selected. The range of this number is 0-65535. In the presence of records containing weights greater than 0, records with weight 0 will have a very small chance of being selected. See [RFC 2782](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2782) for more details. |
| capacity\_limit | `integer` | Maximum number of simultaneous calls for the trunk. |
| ringing\_timeout | `integer` | Ring time in seconds. Supported values are integers from 1 to 32. Null uses the platform default. If the call is not connected within this time, the transaction is ended with the disconnect code **Ringing timeout**. |
| name | `string` | Friendly name of the trunk. Unique among the trunks and trunk groups of the account - they share one name space. |
| external\_reference\_id | `string` | Optional identifier for the inbound trunk in the customer's external system. Maximum length is 100 characters. |
| cli\_format | `string` | **raw** - Do not alter CLI. **e164** - Attempt to convert CLI to E.164 format (default). **local** - Attempt to convert CLI to Localized format. **CLI format conversion may not work correctly for phone calls originating from outside the country of that specific DID**. |
| cli\_prefix | `string` | You may prefix the CLI with an optional `+` sign followed by up to 6 characters, including digits and `#`. |
| description | `string` | Optional description of the trunk. |
| pop | `string` | Point of Presence the trunk is pinned to. Possible values: `nyc`, `fra`, `lac`, `mia`, `sg`, `hk`, `ams`. `null` lets DIDWW choose. |
| configuration | One of [sip\_configurations](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-in-trunks/create-voice-in-trunk.html#trunk-attributes-v35), [pstn\_configurations](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-in-trunks/create-voice-in-trunk.html#trunk-attributes-v35) | Trunk configuration complex object. |
| created\_at | DateTime | Trunk created at DateTime |

### Object Relationships

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| voice\_in\_trunk\_group | to-one | [Trunk Group Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-in-trunk-groups/trunk-group-object.html#voice-in-trunk-group-object-v35) |

**SIP**

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| attributes | [sip\_configuration\_attributes](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-in-trunks/create-voice-in-trunk.html#trunk-attributes-v35) | No | SIP configuration attributes object. |

| Name | Type | Nullable | Description |

### Configuration Attributes

**SIP**

| Name | Type | Nullable | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| username | `string` | Yes | User part of R-URI in INVITE request. You also may use "{DID}" pattern which will be replaced by called DID number in E164 format. For example, you can set Username to "+{DID}"; if you wish to have it in +E164 format |
| host | `string` | Yes | Host part of R-URI in INVITE request. Required while `enabled_sip_registration` is `false`, and rejected while it is `true`. |
| port | `integer` | Yes | Port part of R-URI in INVITE request (is not mandatory). If port is null, SRV record will be resolved (or A record if SRV is unavailable). Must be empty while `enabled_sip_registration` is `true`. |
| codecs | Array of `strings` | No | Codecs offered on calls to the trunk, in priority order: the first has the highest priority. Holds at least one value, without repeats. Possible values: `telephone_event`, `g723`, `g729`, `pcmu`, `pcma`, `speex`, `gsm`, `g726_32`, `g721`, `g726_24`, `g726_40`, `g726_16`, `l16`, `amr`, `amr_wb`. Defaults to `pcmu`, `pcma`, `g729`, `g723`, `telephone_event`. See [Codecs](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-in-trunks/codecs.html#trunk-codecs-v35). |
| rx\_dtmf\_format\_id | `integer` | No | The method id for receiving DTMF signals from customers equipment. Possible values: `1` - RFC 2833; `2` - SIP INFO `application/dtmf-relay` or `application/dtmf`; `3` - RFC 2833 or SIP INFO. |
| tx\_dtmf\_format\_id | `integer` | No | The method of sending DTMF signals to the customer's equipment. Possible values: `0` - Disable sending; `1` - RFC 2833; `2` - SIP INFO `application/dtmf-relay`; `4` - SIP INFO `application/dtmf`. |
| resolve\_ruri | `boolean` | No | Replace host part of the R-URI by resolved IP address. |
| auth\_enabled | `boolean` | No | Enable authorization for the SIP server. |
| auth\_user | `string` | Yes | Authorization user for the SIP server. Required while `auth_enabled` is `true`, and rejected while it is `false`. |
| auth\_password | `string` | Yes | Authorization password for the SIP server. Required while `auth_enabled` is `true`, and rejected while it is `false`. |
| auth\_from\_user | `string` | Yes | Specify user in a **from** field instead of CallerID (overrides CallerID). Some equipment require **from**; to be equivalent to **Auth user**. |
| auth\_from\_domain | `string` | Yes | Sets default **from** domain in SIP messages. Some equipment may require specific **From** Domain. |
| sst\_enabled | `boolean` | No | Enable SIP Session timers customization. SIP session timers are used to make sure that a session (dialog) is still alive, even though there may have been a long time since the last in-dialog message. If the other end is not responding, the dialog will be hung up automatically. SIP session timers need to be supported by all end points for it to work. It's a SIP extension, standardized by the IETF. See [RFC 4028](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4028) for more details. |
| sst\_min\_timer | `integer` | Yes | Minimal SIP Session timer value (Default 600 seconds). See [RFC 4028](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4028) for more details. |
| sst\_max\_timer | `integer` | Yes | Maximal SIP Session timer value (Default 900 seconds). See [RFC 4028](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4028) for more details. |
| sst\_accept\_501 | `boolean` | No | Do not drop the call after receiving SIP 501 response for non-critical messages. |
| sip\_timer\_b | `integer` | No | INVITE transaction timeout (Default 8000ms). See [RFC 3261 Section 17.1.1.2](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3261#section-17.1.1.2) for more details. |
| dns\_srv\_failover\_timer | `integer` | Yes | Invite transaction timeout for each of gateways with DNS SRV rerouting (Default 2000ms). |
| rtp\_ping | `boolean` | Yes | Use RTP PING when connecting a call. After establishing the call, DIDWW will send empty RTP packet **RTP PING**. It is necessary if both parties operate in Symmetric RTP / Comedia mode and expect the other party to start sending RTP first. |
| rtp\_timeout | `integer` | No | Disconnect the call if the RTP packets do not arrive within the specified time. |
| force\_symmetric\_rtp | `boolean` | Yes | Forced to work in Symmetric RTP / COMEDIA mode. |
| symmetric\_rtp\_ignore\_rtcp | `boolean` | Yes | Avoid switching RTP session based on RTCP packet while working in Symmetric RTP / COMEDIA. Only RTP packets will be considered. |
| rerouting\_disconnect\_code\_ids | `array` | Yes | [Rerouting disconnect codes](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-in-trunks/rerouting-disconnect-codes.html#disconnect-codes-v35). |
| sst\_session\_expires | `integer` | Yes | Session-Expires header value. Optional, should be in range with **sst\_min\_timer** and **sst\_max\_timer**. See [RFC 4028](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4028) for more details. |
| sst\_refresh\_method\_id | `integer` | No | SIP method which will be used for session update. See [RFC 4028](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4028) for more details. Possible values: `1` - Invite; `2` - Update; `3` - Update fallback Invite. |
| transport\_protocol\_id | `integer` | No | Transport protocol ID. Possible values: `1` - UDP; `2` - TCP; `3` - TLS. |
| max\_transfers | `integer` | No | Max count of the **REFER** requests. |
| max\_30x\_redirects | `integer` | No | Max count of 301/302 redirects. |
| media\_encryption\_mode | `string` | No | Media encryption mode. See [RFC4568 about SRTP SDES](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4568), [RFC5764 about SRTP DTLS](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5764), and [RFC6189 about ZRTP](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6189) for more details. Possible values: `disabled` - Disabled; `srtp_sdes` - SRTP SDES; `srtp_dtls` - SRTP DTLS; `zrtp` - ZRTP. |
| ice\_mode | `string` | No | ICE (Interactive Connectivity Establishment) for calls to the trunk: not used, accepted when the trunk offers it, or initiated by DIDWW. Possible values: `disabled`, `accept`, `initiate`. Defaults to `disabled`. |
| rtcp\_mux\_mode | `string` | No | RTP and RTCP multiplexed on one port: not used, accepted when the trunk offers it, or initiated by DIDWW. Possible values: `disabled`, `accept`, `initiate`. Defaults to `disabled`. |
| rtcp\_feedback\_mode | `string` | No | RTCP feedback (AVPF): not used, accepted when the trunk offers it, or initiated by DIDWW. Possible values: `disabled`, `accept`, `initiate`. Defaults to `disabled`. |
| stir\_shaken\_mode | `string` | No | Stir/Shaken mode. See [STIR/SHAKEN](https://doc.didww.com/voice/inbound-trunks/sip-trunks/call-information/stir-shaken-headers.html#service-did-stir-shaken) for more details. Possible values: `disabled` - Do not send identity; `original` - Transit Identity header as is; `pai` - Add PAI, P-Attestation-Indicator, P-Origination-ID; `original_pai` - Transit Identity header as is and add PAI, P-Attestation-Indicator, P-Origination-ID; `verstat` - Add P-Stir-Verstat, P-Attestation-Indicator, P-Origination-ID. |
| allowed\_rtp\_ips | Array of `strings` | Yes | The allowed RTP IPs: IPv4 or IPv6, single or subnet. Up to 10 items. Null means no restriction. |
| network\_protocol\_priority | `string` | No | Network protocol priority for SIP routing. Possible values: `force_ipv4` - Use IPv4 exclusively. `force_ipv6` - Use IPv6 exclusively. `any` - Use either IPv4 or IPv6. `prefer_ipv4` - Prefer IPv4 but fall back to IPv6. `prefer_ipv6` - Prefer IPv6 but fall back to IPv4. |
| enabled\_sip\_registration | `boolean` | No | Enables SIP registration for the trunk. Enabling it generates `incoming_auth_username` and `incoming_auth_password`. |
| use\_did\_in\_ruri | `boolean` | No | Uses the called DID in the R-URI. Can be `true` only while `enabled_sip_registration` is `true`: a request that would leave it `true` with SIP registration disabled returns `422 Unprocessable Entity`. |
| incoming\_auth\_username | `string` | Yes | Generated SIP registration username. Read-only: sending it is rejected. |
| incoming\_auth\_password | `string` | Yes | Generated SIP registration password. Read-only: sending it is rejected. |
| diversion\_relay\_policy | `string` | No | Controls how Diversion information is relayed. Possible values: `none` - Do not relay the Diversion header. `as_is` - Relay the Diversion header as received. `sip` - Relay the Diversion header as a SIP URI. `tel` - Relay the Diversion header as a TEL URI. |
| diversion\_inject\_mode | `string` | No | Controls how Diversion information is injected. Possible values: `none` - Do not add a Diversion header. `did_number` - Add a Diversion header using the DID number in E.164 format. |
| cnam\_lookup | `boolean` | No | Enables inbound CNAM lookup. |

**PSTN**

| Name | Type | Nullable | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| dst | `string` | No | Number calls are forwarded to, in E.164 without the leading `+`. Digits only, up to 15 digits. |

item.name: Voice OUT Trunk Object
item.description:
JSON:API object with type `voice_out_trunks`.

Authentication data is returned only inside `data.attributes.authentication_method`.

## Request

### URI Parameters

| Name | Type | Is Required? | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id | `string` | Yes | Unique identifier of the outbound trunk. |

### Data Attributes

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| name | `string` | The outbound trunk name. |
| external\_reference\_id | `string` | Optional identifier for the outbound trunk in the customer's external system. Maximum length is 100 characters. |
| allowed\_rtp\_ips | Array of `strings` | Allowed RTP IP addresses for media traffic. |
| on\_cli\_mismatch\_action | `string` | The action applied when the CLI does not match the allowed DID list. Possible values: `send_original_cli` - pass the original `From` header value from your system to the destination without modification. `reject_call` - reject the call if the `From` header value does not match any DID allowed on the trunk. `replace_cli` - replace the CLI with one of the DIDs allowed on the trunk. `randomize_cli` - replace the CLI with a random DID allowed on the trunk. |
| capacity\_limit | `integer` | The capacity limit of the outbound trunk. |
| allow\_any\_did\_as\_cli | `boolean` | When set to `true`, any eligible DID can be used as CLI for the trunk. |
| status | `string` | The status of the outbound trunk. Possible values: `active` - the trunk can be used for outbound traffic. `blocked` - outbound traffic on the trunk is blocked. |
| threshold\_reached | `boolean` | Indicates whether the 24-hour threshold amount has been reached. |
| threshold\_amount | `string` | The 24-hour threshold limit. |
| default\_dst\_action | `string` | The default destination action. Possible values: `allow_all` - allow calls to all destinations except the prefixes listed in `dst_prefixes`. `reject_all` - reject calls to all destinations except the prefixes listed in `dst_prefixes`. |
| dst\_prefixes | Array of `strings` | The destination prefixes allowed or rejected based on `default_dst_action`. Each prefix is digits only, without a leading `+` or separators. Repeated prefixes are stored once. |
| emergency\_enable\_all | `boolean` | When set to `true`, all eligible DIDs of the account can be used for emergency calling on this trunk. |
| media\_encryption\_mode | `string` | Media encryption mode. Possible values: `disabled` - media encryption is turned off. `srtp_sdes` - use SRTP encryption with SDES key exchange. `srtp_dtls` - use SRTP encryption with DTLS key exchange. `zrtp` - use SRTP encryption with ZRTP key exchange. |
| ice\_mode | `string` | ICE (Interactive Connectivity Establishment) for calls from the trunk: not used, accepted when the trunk offers it, or initiated by DIDWW. Possible values: `disabled`, `accept`, `initiate`. Defaults to `accept`. |
| rtcp\_mux\_mode | `string` | RTP and RTCP multiplexed on one port: not used, accepted when the trunk offers it, or initiated by DIDWW. Possible values: `disabled`, `accept`, `initiate`. Defaults to `accept`. |
| rtcp\_feedback\_mode | `string` | RTCP feedback (AVPF): not used, accepted when the trunk offers it, or initiated by DIDWW. Possible values: `disabled`, `accept`, `initiate`. Defaults to `accept`. With `disabled`, a call whose SDP offer uses a feedback profile (`RTP/AVPF` or `UDP/TLS/RTP/SAVPF`) is rejected with SIP `500 No suitable media`. WebRTC clients always offer such a profile, so use `accept` or `initiate` for them. |
| codecs | Array of `strings` | Codecs offered on calls from the trunk, in priority order: the first has the highest priority. Holds at least one value, without repeats. Possible values: `telephone_event`, `g723`, `g729`, `pcmu`, `pcma`, `gsm`, `g722`, `opus`, `amr`, `amr_wb`. Defaults to `pcma`, `pcmu`, `telephone_event`. |
| callback\_url | `string` | The callback URI. Can be `null` or a valid HTTP(S) URL. |
| force\_symmetric\_rtp | `boolean` | Enables symmetric RTP / COMEDIA mode. |
| rtp\_ping | `boolean` | When enabled, DIDWW sends an empty RTP packet after call establishment. |
| rtp\_timeout | `integer` | Disconnects the call if RTP packets do not arrive within the specified time. Supported values are from 30 to 600 seconds. |
| created\_at | `date&time` | The date and time when the outbound trunk was created. |
| authentication\_method | `object` | Authentication method object. See [Authentication Method](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/voice-out-trunks/voice-out-trunk-object.html#outbound-trunk-authentication-method-v35). |

### Authentication Method

The outbound trunk authentication is returned in the `authentication_method` attribute.

Supported authentication method types:

- `credentials_and_ip` - uses SIP credentials together with allowed IP addresses.
- `ip_only` - uses allowed IP addresses only.
- `twilio` - uses a Twilio Account SID for authentication.

### Authentication Method Attributes by Type

The following attributes are part of the `authentication_method` object:

**credentials\_and\_ip**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| allowed\_sip\_ips | Array of `strings` | The allowed originating SIP IPs. |
| tech\_prefix | `string` | Prefix stripped from the dialled number before routing. The maximum length is 8 characters and only digits and `#` are supported. |
| username | `string` | The digest authentication username. |
| password | `string` | The digest authentication password. |

**ip\_only**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| allowed\_sip\_ips | Array of `strings` | The allowed originating SIP IPs. |
| tech\_prefix | `string` | Prefix stripped from the dialled number before routing. The maximum length is 8 characters and only digits and `#` are supported. |

**twilio**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| twilio\_account\_sid | `string` | The Twilio Account SID. It is a 34-character identifier of the Twilio account. |

### Object Relationships

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dids | to-many | [DID Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/did-object.html#did-object-v35) |
| emergency\_dids | to-many | DIDs assigned for emergency calling on the outbound trunk. |

### Object Meta

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| spent\_amount | `string` | Amount spent on this trunk over the last 24 hours, as a decimal string. |

item.name: SMS Trunk Object
item.description:
JSON:API object with type `sms_trunks`.

The trunk type is defined by `data.attributes.configuration.type`. The configuration
attributes depend on the type. See [Configuration](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/sms-trunk-object.html#sms-trunk-configuration-v35).

## Request

### URI Parameters

| Name | Type | Is Required? | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id | `string` | Yes | Unique identifier of the SMS trunk. |

### Data Attributes

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| name | `string` | Friendly name of the SMS trunk. Must be unique among the SMS trunks and SMS trunk groups of the account. |
| external\_reference\_id | `string` | Optional identifier for the SMS trunk in the customer's external system. Maximum length is 100 characters. Can be `null`. |
| blocked | `boolean` | When `true`, the trunk does not handle messages. Default value is `false`. |
| priority | `integer` | Routing priority of the trunk within its [SMS Trunk Group](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunk-groups/sms-trunk-group-object.html#sms-trunk-group-object-v35). The range is 0-32767. Defaults to `100` on the trunk types that can join a group (`sms_to_email`, `http_in`, `smpp_esme`, `smpp_smsc`). Always `null` on `http_out` trunks, which cannot join a group. Inbound messages are offered to the trunk with the higher `priority` value first. See [SMS Trunk Groups](https://doc.didww.com/sms/sms-trunks/trunk-groups/sms-trunk-groups.html#user-panel-sms-trunk-group) for how priority is applied. |
| allow\_any\_did\_as\_source | `boolean` | When `true`, any DID of the account can be used as the source address of messages sent through the trunk, and `outgoing_dids` is empty. Can be enabled only on `http_out`, `smpp_esme`, and `smpp_smsc` trunks. Default value is `false`. |
| allow\_in | `boolean` | Read-only. `true` when the trunk handles inbound messages. Derived from the configuration type. |
| allow\_out | `boolean` | Read-only. `true` when the trunk can send messages. Derived from the configuration type. |
| configuration | `object` | Trunk configuration object with `type` and `attributes`. See [Configuration](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/sms-trunk-object.html#sms-trunk-configuration-v35). |
| created\_at | `DateTime` | Read-only. The date and time when the SMS trunk was created. |
| updated\_at | `DateTime` | Read-only. The date and time when the SMS trunk was last updated. |

### Object Relationships

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| outgoing\_dids | to-many | [DID Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/did-object.html#did-object-v35). DIDs allowed as the source address of messages sent through the trunk. Empty while `allow_any_did_as_source` is `true`. |
| incoming\_dids | to-many | [DID Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/did-object.html#did-object-v35). Read-only. DIDs routed to the trunk for inbound messages. A DID is routed to a trunk through the `sms_trunk` relationship of the [DID](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/did/index.html). |
| sms\_trunk\_group | to-one | [SMS Trunk Group Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunk-groups/sms-trunk-group-object.html#sms-trunk-group-object-v35). The group the trunk belongs to. Can be `null`. |
| sender\_id\_verifications | to-many | [Sender ID Verification Object](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sender-id-verifications/sender-id-verification-object.html#sender-id-verification-object-v35). Read-only. Sender ID verifications routed through the trunk. A verification is routed through a trunk with its `sms_trunk` relationship. |

### Object Meta

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| host | `string` | Full URL of the endpoint to which outbound messages are submitted, for example `https://us.sms-out.didww.com/outbound_messages`. Returned for `http_out` trunks only. The other endpoints listed in the [SMS OUT HTTP specification](https://doc.didww.com/sms/outbound-sms-api/outbound-sms-api-reference.html#sms-out-spec-endpoints-headers) also accept the trunk's messages. |

### Configuration

The `configuration` object contains:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| type | `string` | Configuration type. Possible values: `sms_to_email` - DIDWW forwards inbound messages as email. `http_in` - DIDWW delivers inbound messages as an HTTP request. `http_out` - the customer submits outbound messages to DIDWW over HTTP. `smpp_esme` - the customer connects to DIDWW as an SMPP ESME. `smpp_smsc` - DIDWW connects to the customer's SMSC as an SMPP client. The type cannot be changed after the trunk is created. |
| attributes | `object` | Configuration attributes. Their set depends on `type`. |

The configuration type defines what the trunk can do:

| Type | `allow_in` | `allow_out` | Can join a group | Generated credentials |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sms_to_email` | `true` | `false` | Yes | None |
| `http_in` | `true` | `false` | Yes | None |
| `http_out` | `false` | `true` | No | `auth_name`, `auth_password` |
| `smpp_esme` | `true` | `true` | Yes | `system_id`, `password` |
| `smpp_smsc` | `true` | `true` | Yes | None |

Read-only attributes are generated by DIDWW and cannot be sent in requests. Generated
credentials can be replaced with
[Regenerate SMS Trunk Credentials](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/inventory-resources/sms-trunks/sms-trunk-regenerate-credentials.html).

#### sms\_to\_email

DIDWW forwards inbound messages as email. See
[SMS to Email trunk](https://doc.didww.com/sms/sms-trunks/sms-to-email/sms-to-email-trunk.html#user-panel-sms-to-email-trunk).

| Name | Type | Nullable | Read-only | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| send\_to | `string` | No | No | Recipient email address. |
| subject | `string` | No | No | Email subject template. |
| message | `string` | No | No | Email body template. |

#### http\_in

DIDWW delivers inbound messages as an HTTP request. The query parameters, headers, and body
can use the placeholders `{SMS_TEXT}`, `{SMS_TEXT_BASE64_ENCODED}`, `{SMS_SRC_ADDR}`,
`{SMS_DST_ADDR}`, and `{SMS_TIME}`. See [SMS IN HTTP specification](https://doc.didww.com/sms/sms-trunks/technical-data/http-specification.html#sms-in-specification)
and [SMS to HTTP IN trunk](https://doc.didww.com/sms/sms-trunks/http-in/http-in-trunk.html#user-panel-sms-to-http-in-trunk).

| Name | Type | Nullable | Read-only | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| url | `string` | No | No | Endpoint the request is sent to. |
| http\_method | `string` | No | No | HTTP method of the request. Possible values: `get`; `post`; `put`. |
| query\_parameters | `object` | Yes | No | Query parameters added to the request, as an object of string names and string values. |
| headers | `object` | Yes | No | Headers added to the request, as an object of string names and string values. |
| body\_type | `string` | Yes | No | How `body` is encoded. Possible values: `json`; `html_multipart`; `html_url_encoded`; `raw`. `null` when `http_method` is `get`. |
| body | `string` or `object` | Yes | No | Request body template. A JSON object encoded as a string when `body_type` is `json`. An object of string names and string values when `body_type` is `html_multipart` or `html_url_encoded`. A string when `body_type` is `raw`. `null` when `http_method` is `get`. |
| follow\_redirect | `boolean` | No | No | When `true`, DIDWW follows 3xx responses. Default value is `false`. |
| validate\_https\_certificate | `boolean` | No | No | When `true`, DIDWW rejects an untrusted TLS certificate of the endpoint. Default value is `true`. |

#### http\_out

The customer submits outbound messages to DIDWW over HTTP, to the endpoint URL returned in
`meta.host`. See [SMS OUT HTTP specification](https://doc.didww.com/sms/outbound-sms-api/index.html#sms-out-specification) and
[SMS to HTTP OUT trunk](https://doc.didww.com/sms/sms-trunks/http-out/http-out-trunk.html#user-panel-sms-out).

| Name | Type | Nullable | Read-only | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| callback\_url | `string` | Yes | No | HTTP(S) URL to which DIDWW sends the status events of messages submitted through the trunk. See [SMS OUT callbacks](https://doc.didww.com/sms/outbound-sms-api/status-callbacks-and-delivery-receipts.html#sms-out-spec-callbacks). |
| allowed\_ips | Array of `strings` | Yes | No | IP addresses from which messages are accepted, in the format (IPv4\|IPv6)[/mask]. Up to 15 unique entries. Single addresses are returned as /32 (IPv4) or /128 (IPv6) networks; IPv6 addresses are returned in full (uncompressed) notation. When empty, messages are accepted from any address. |
| auth\_name | `string` | Yes | Yes | Generated HTTP authentication username. See [SMS OUT authentication](https://doc.didww.com/sms/outbound-sms-api/outbound-sms-api-reference.html#sms-out-spec-authentication). |
| auth\_password | `string` | Yes | Yes | Generated HTTP authentication password. |

#### smpp\_esme

The customer connects and binds to DIDWW as an SMPP ESME. See
[SMPP specification](https://doc.didww.com/sms/sms-trunks/technical-data/smpp-specification.html#service-smpp-specification), [SMPP over TLS](https://doc.didww.com/sms/sms-trunks/technical-data/smpp-specification.html#smpp-tls),
and [SMPP ESME trunk](https://doc.didww.com/sms/sms-trunks/smpp-esme/smpp-esme-trunk.html#user-panel-sms-smpp-esme).

| Name | Type | Nullable | Read-only | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| system\_type | `string` | Yes | No | SMPP `system_type`. Maximum length is 12 characters. |
| allowed\_ips | Array of `strings` | Yes | No | IP addresses from which the ESME may bind, in the format (IPv4\|IPv6)[/mask]. Up to 15 unique entries. Single addresses are returned as /32 (IPv4) or /128 (IPv6) networks; IPv6 addresses are returned in full (uncompressed) notation. When empty, binding is allowed from any address. |
| server\_location | `string` | No | No | Location of the DIDWW SMPP server the trunk is served from. Possible values: `nyc` - US, NY. `ams` - NL, AMS. In the sandbox environment only `nyc` is accepted. See [Server locations and IP addresses](https://doc.didww.com/sms/sms-trunks/technical-data/smpp-specification.html#smpp-endpoints). |
| system\_id | `string` | No | Yes | Generated SMPP `system_id` to bind with. |
| password | `string` | No | Yes | Generated SMPP bind password. |

#### smpp\_smsc

DIDWW connects and binds to the customer's SMSC as an SMPP client. See
[SMPP specification](https://doc.didww.com/sms/sms-trunks/technical-data/smpp-specification.html#service-smpp-specification) and
[SMPP SMSC trunk](https://doc.didww.com/sms/sms-trunks/smpp-smsc/smpp-smsc-trunk.html#user-panel-sms-smpp-smsc).

| Name | Type | Nullable | Read-only | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| host | `string` | No | No | SMSC host DIDWW binds to. |
| tx\_port | `integer` | No | No | Transmitter port. Default value is `2775`. |
| rx\_port | `integer` | No | No | Receiver port. Default value is `2776`. |
| transceiver\_mode | `boolean` | No | No | When `true`, DIDWW binds as a transceiver instead of separate transmitter and receiver binds. Default value is `false`. |
| connection\_timeout | `integer` | No | No | Bind timeout in seconds. Default value is `20`. |
| use\_ssl | `boolean` | No | No | When `true`, the connection is wrapped in TLS. Default value is `false`. |
| system\_id | `string` | No | No | SMPP `system_id` DIDWW binds with. Maximum length is 15 characters. |
| system\_type | `string` | Yes | No | SMPP `system_type`. Maximum length is 12 characters. |
| password | `string` | No | No | SMPP bind password. Maximum length is 8 characters. |
| server\_location | `string` | No | No | Location of the DIDWW SMPP server that connects to the SMSC. Possible values: `nyc` - US, NY. `ams` - NL, AMS. In the sandbox environment only `nyc` is accepted. See [Server locations and IP addresses](https://doc.didww.com/sms/sms-trunks/technical-data/smpp-specification.html#smpp-endpoints). |

item.name: Export Object
Export Filters Object
item.description:
Export Filters keys. The accepted keys depend on the `export_type` of the Export.
`from` and `to` are returned as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC.

An Export created with an earlier API version keeps the filter keys of that version, for
example `year`, `month`, and `day`.

**cdr\_in**

| Name | Type | Nullable | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| from | `string` | False | Start date and time of the CDR range. |
| to | `string` | False | End date and time of the CDR range. |
| did\_number | `string` | False | Filters CDRs by DID number. |
| source\_number | `string` | False | Filters CDRs by caller number, as it reached DIDWW. |
| source\_number\_out | `string` | False | Filters CDRs by caller number, as delivered to the trunk. |
| source\_country\_iso | `string` | False | Filters CDRs by caller country, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. |

| source | `string` | False | Filters CDRs by source number. |
| cli | `string` | False | Filters CDRs by caller ID (CLI). |
| destination | `string` | False | Filters CDRs by destination number. |

**sms\_in**

| Name | Type | Nullable | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| from | `string` | False | Start date and time of the SMS record range. |
| to | `string` | False | End date and time of the SMS record range. |
| source\_address\_eq | `string` | False | Filters messages by exact sender address. |
| source\_address\_cont | `string` | False | Filters messages whose sender address contains this value. |
| destination\_address\_eq | `string` | False | Filters messages by exact recipient address. |
| destination\_address\_cont | `string` | False | Filters messages whose recipient address contains this value. |
| status | `string` | False | Filters messages by state: `success`, `failed`, or `queued`. |

| sms\_trunk.id | `string` or Array of `strings` | False | Filters messages by SMS trunk ID. |
| sms\_id | `string` | False | Filters messages by SMS ID. |

| Name | Type | Nullable | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| to | `string` | False | End date and time of the SMS record range. |
| source\_address\_eq | `string` | False | Filters messages by exact sender address. |
| source\_address\_cont | `string` | False | Filters messages whose sender address contains this value. |

| sms\_id | `string` | False | Filters messages by SMS ID. |
| service\_type | `string` | False | Filters messages by service type: `a2p` or `p2p`. |
| sender\_id\_verification.id | `string` or Array of `strings` | False | Filters messages by sender ID verification ID. |

## Attributes

item.name: Encrypted File Object
Encryption Details
item.description:
Files passed to [Create Encrypted File](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/create-encrypted-files.html#create-encrypted-files-v35) should be encrypted with [DIDWW Public Keys](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/regulation-resources/encrypted-files/public-keys.html#public-keys-v35).

## Using SDK for encryption

Recommended way of using encryption is to encrypt files in browser.
it can be achieved via [@didww/encrypt](https://github.com/didww/didww-encrypt) JS library.

If you want to encrypt files on server side it can be done via following:

**Ruby Gem**

Use the APIv3 Ruby gem to perform file encryption on the server side.

[https://github.com/didww/didww-v3-ruby/blob/master/lib/didww/encrypt.rb](https://github.com/didww/didww-v3-ruby/blob/master/lib/didww/encrypt.rb)

**PHP SDK**

Use the official PHP SDK to implement server-side encryption.

[https://github.com/didww/didww-api-3-php-sdk/blob/master/src/Encrypt.php](https://github.com/didww/didww-api-3-php-sdk/blob/master/src/Encrypt.php)

**Java SDK**

Use the official Java SDK to implement server-side encryption.

[https://github.com/didww/didww-api-3-java-sdk/blob/main/src/main/java/com/didww/sdk/Encrypt.java](https://github.com/didww/didww-api-3-java-sdk/blob/main/src/main/java/com/didww/sdk/Encrypt.java)

**Python SDK**

Use the official Python SDK to implement server-side encryption.

[https://github.com/didww/didww-api-3-python-sdk/blob/main/src/didww/encrypt.py](https://github.com/didww/didww-api-3-python-sdk/blob/main/src/didww/encrypt.py)

**TypeScript SDK**

Use the official TypeScript SDK to implement server-side encryption.

[https://github.com/didww/didww-api-3-typescript-sdk/blob/main/src/encrypt.ts](https://github.com/didww/didww-api-3-typescript-sdk/blob/main/src/encrypt.ts)

**Go Encryption Sample**

> Use the Go sample project to implement server-side file encryption compatible with DIDWW API v3.

[https://github.com/didww/go-encrypt-sample](https://github.com/didww/go-encrypt-sample)

To implement encryption manually see figure:

![../../../../_images/enc.png](https://doc.didww.com/_images/enc.png)

**Fig. 1.** File encryption schematic.

For additional check you need to pass fingerprint of public keys along with encrypted files.
You can use our JS library or ruby SDK for that.

To implement fingerprint calculation manually see figure:

![../../../../_images/fingerprint.png](https://doc.didww.com/_images/fingerprint.png)

**Fig. 1.** Fingerprint calculation schematic.

item.name: Inbound Call Price Object
item.description:
An inbound call price returned by [Look up Inbound Call Prices](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/inbound-call-prices/lookup-inbound-call-prices.html).
Resource type: `prices`.

The `id` is a UUID that names the answering price of the plan. There is no endpoint that
returns a single price by its ID.

## Attributes

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| destination | `string` | Prefix of the plan that priced the number: the longest one covering it for this source type and destination country. |
| country | `string` | Destination country the price applies to, by name. `null` for a price of the plan's global country, which is not tied to one destination country. |
| src\_country\_name | `string` | Source country of the call the price applies to, by name. `null` for a price that applies to calls from any country. |
| source\_type | `string` | Calling party category the price applies to: the kind of line the call originates from, such as `cellular` or `fixed`. Each category covering the number returns its own price. |
| rate | `string` | Per-minute rate in USD, VAT excluded, as a decimal string that is never rounded. `null` when `reject_calls` is `true`. |
| connection\_fee | `string` | Fee charged once per call, in USD, VAT excluded, as a decimal string. `null` when `reject_calls` is `true`. |
| initial\_interval | `integer` | First billing increment, in seconds. A call is charged for at least this long. |
| next\_interval | `integer` | Each following billing increment, in seconds. |
| reject\_calls | `boolean` | `true` when the plan rejects calls to this destination instead of pricing them. `rate` and `connection_fee` are then `null`. A rejection is an answer, not a missing price. |

Prices are printed without rounding, with trailing zeros dropped and at least one decimal
kept, for example `0.0`, `1.5` or `0.002`.

item.name: Outbound Call Price Object
item.description:
An outbound call price returned by [Look up Outbound Call Prices](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/outbound-call-prices/lookup-outbound-call-prices.html).
Resource type: `prices`.

The `id` is a UUID that names the price by the plan, the prefix and the routing conditions,
so it stays the same when the same price is imported again. There is no endpoint that
returns a single price by its ID.

## Attributes

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| category | `enum` | Category of the price, as the sheets of the price list in the user panel group them. Several prices of one lookup can share a category. Possible values: `International` `Origin based` `Local` |
| country | `string` | Destination country of the prefix, by name. `null` when the prefix is not attributed to a country. |
| network | `string` | Destination network of the prefix, by name. `null` when the prefix is not attributed to a network. |
| prefix | `string` | Destination prefix of the plan that priced the number: the longest one covering it among the prices of the same routing conditions. |
| rate | `string` | Per-minute rate in USD, VAT excluded, as a decimal string that is never rounded. `null` when `reject_calls` is `true`. |
| connection\_fee | `string` | Fee charged once per call, in USD, VAT excluded, as a decimal string. `null` when `reject_calls` is `true`. |
| initial\_increment | `integer` | First billing increment, in seconds. A call is charged for at least this long. |
| recurring\_increment | `integer` | Each following billing increment, in seconds. |
| reject\_calls | `boolean` | `true` when the plan rejects calls to this destination instead of pricing them. `rate` and `connection_fee` are then `null`. A rejection is an answer, not a missing price. |
| next\_rate | `string` | Per-minute rate in USD, VAT excluded, from `effective_at` on. `null` when no change is scheduled, when the price is removed, or when the destination is going to reject calls. |
| next\_connection\_fee | `string` | Fee charged once per call, in USD, VAT excluded, from `effective_at` on. `null` whenever `next_rate` is `null`. |
| next\_initial\_increment | `integer` | First billing increment, in seconds, from `effective_at` on. `null` whenever `next_rate` is `null`. For a rejected destination that is about to open, the increment it opens with. |
| next\_recurring\_increment | `integer` | Each following billing increment, in seconds, from `effective_at` on. `null` whenever `next_rate` is `null`. For a rejected destination that is about to open, the increment it opens with. |
| effective\_at | `DateTime` | When the change named by `comment` takes effect. `null` when no change is scheduled. |
| comment | `string` | The scheduled change of the price. `null` when no change is scheduled. See [Comment values](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/outbound-call-prices/outbound-call-price-object.html#comment-values). |

Prices are printed without rounding, with trailing zeros dropped and at least one decimal
kept, for example `0.0`, `1.5` or `0.002`.

A prefix answers only while its price is in effect, and only for a number whose length is
within the bounds that the plan sets for that prefix.

## Comment values

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Increase` | The rate increases. |
| `Decrease` | The rate decreases. |
| `Connection fee change` | The connection fee changes. |
| `Billing increment change` | The initial or recurring billing increment changes. |
| Combined values | Two or three of the changes above at once, for example `Increase and Connection fee change`, or `Increase, Connection fee change, and Billing increment change`. |
| `No Change` | A change is scheduled, but the next values equal the current ones. |
| `Reject calls` | The destination is going to reject calls. The `next_` attributes are `null`. |
| `Removed` | The price ends within 30 days, and no price of the same prefix takes over when it ends. `effective_at` is the end of the price. |
| `New Breakout` | A destination that currently rejects calls opens within 30 days. |
| `null` | No change is scheduled. |

item.name: SMS IN Price Object
item.description:
An SMS IN price returned by [Look up SMS IN Prices](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/sms-prices/lookup-sms-in-prices.html). Resource
type: `prices`.

The `id` is a UUID derived from the content of the price: it stays the same across requests
while the price is unchanged, and differs for different prices. Any change to the price,
including its amount, gives it a new `id`, so the `id` does not follow the price of a
destination over time. There is no endpoint that returns a single price by its ID.

## Attributes

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| source\_prefix | `string` | Prefix of the sending number the price applies to. `null` when the price applies to an SMS from any number. |
| source\_number\_length\_min | `integer` | Shortest sending number, in digits, the price applies to. |
| source\_number\_length\_max | `integer` | Longest sending number, in digits, the price applies to. |
| destination\_prefix | `string` | Prefix of the receiving number the price applies to. With `filter[dst_number]`, the longest one covering the number among the prices that the filters admit and whose length range holds the number. `null` when the price applies to any destination. |
| destination\_number\_length\_min | `integer` | Shortest receiving number, in digits, the price applies to. |
| destination\_number\_length\_max | `integer` | Longest receiving number, in digits, the price applies to. |
| country | `string` | Country of the receiving number the price applies to, by name. `null` when the price is not attributed to a country. |
| price | `string` | Price per SMS in USD, VAT excluded, as a decimal string that is never rounded. |

Prices are printed without rounding, with trailing zeros dropped and at least one decimal
kept, for example `0.0`, `1.5` or `0.0525`.

Prices under one destination prefix can differ by the sending number they apply to and by
their length ranges. Prices that are equal in every stored value are returned once.

item.name: SMS OUT Price Object
item.description:
An SMS OUT price returned by [Look up SMS OUT Prices](https://doc.didww.com/api3/2026-11-19/prices-resources/sms-prices/lookup-sms-out-prices.html) for the
A2P, P2P and OTP domains. Resource type: `prices`.

The `id` is a UUID derived from the content of the price: it stays the same across requests
while the price is unchanged, and differs for different prices. Any change to the price,
including its amount, gives it a new `id`, so the `id` does not follow the price of a
destination over time. There is no endpoint that returns a single price by its ID.

## Attributes

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| source\_prefix | `string` | Prefix of the sending number the price applies to. `null` when the price applies to an SMS from any number. |
| destination\_prefix | `string` | Destination prefix the price applies to. With `filter[dst_number]`, the longest one covering the number among the prices that the filters admit. `null` when the price applies to any destination. |
| country | `string` | Destination country the price applies to, by name. `null` when the price is not attributed to a country. |
| mcc | `integer` | Mobile country code of the destination network the price applies to. `null` when the price applies to any network. |
| mcc\_name | `string` | Name of the mobile country code. `null` when `mcc` is `null`. |
| mnc | `integer` | Mobile network code of the destination network the price applies to. `null` when the price applies to any network of the country. |
| mnc\_name | `string` | Name of the mobile network. `null` when `mnc` is `null`. |
| reject\_sms | `boolean` | `true` when the plan rejects SMS to this destination instead of pricing them. `price` is then `null`. A rejection is an answer, not a missing price. |
| price | `string` | Price per SMS in USD, VAT excluded, as a decimal string that is never rounded. `null` when `reject_sms` is `true`. |

Prices are printed without rounding, with trailing zeros dropped and at least one decimal
kept, for example `0.0`, `1.5` or `0.0525`.

Prices under one destination prefix can differ by the sending number they apply to
(`source_prefix`), by the destination network (`mcc` and `mnc`, which only the delivery
decides) and by plan settings that the API does not return. A lookup therefore returns the
prices of the plan that apply, not the one price that is charged. Prices that are equal in
every stored value are returned once. Two prices can still look alike, because they can
differ in settings that the API does not return; their `id` values then differ.
